News.title: Two remain missing after boat carrying five people ‘got into distress’ in English Channel as huge rescue mission ongoing
News.content:
SEA SEARCH Two remain missing after boat carrying five people ‘got into distress’ in English Channel as huge rescue mission ongoing

TWO people remain missing after a boat got into distress in the English Channel.

A huge rescue effort continued through the night, with more than 15 lifeboats and a French warship drafted in after the vessel carrying five people got to into trouble off the coast of Plymouth, Devon, yesterday evening.

A coastguard helicopter, fixed wing aircraft and two RNLI lifeboats began the search near Eddystone lighthouse around 6pm on Saturday night.

HM Coastguard in Falmouth, Cornwall, confirmed that three of the five people aboard the vessel had been accounted for.





But they did not reveal any details about the boat or the nature of the emergency.

A large number of civilian boats, including fishing vessels have also joined what the coastguard called an “extensive search” of the area.

News.title: Bonking screws, bomb scares… and ‘frozen chips’ – inside Britain’s newest £400million prison ALREADY plunged in chaos
News.content:
BRITAIN’S £400million newest prison was hailed as “the standard for the future” when it opened its cell doors last year – but in the following 17 months it has been dogged by damning claims.

There has already been allegations of at least THREE flings between staff and lags, the bomb squad has been called in over a rumoured “pipe bomb” and violent prisoner clashes have erupted, according to a HMP Millsike insider.



The Category C lock-up, in Full Sutton, Yorkshire, which opened in March last year, was supposed to hold 1,500 inmates but is believed to contain 400 fewer due to staffing issues.

Part-run by private firm Mitie Care and Custody, it was erected as part of plans to ease Britain’s prison space and overcrowding crisis, which has led to more than 43,000 lags being freed after serving just 40 per cent of their sentences.

Even Prime Minister Andy Burnham conceded the system was “dangerously close to capacity” while vowing to deliver “the fastest prison building programme since the Victorian era”, promising 14,000 new spaces by 2031.



Then-Justice Secretary Shabana Mahmood – now Home Secretary – touted the prison as “the standard for the future, with cutting crime built into its very fabric” when it opened.

But judging by our insider’s sensational allegations, if HMP Millsike is the “standard for the future”, the future looks very bleak indeed.

And those hoping to see HMP Millsike as a template for success may be left wanting as former staff and our sources describe the “chaos” behind its walls.

Among the most shocking claims revealed to The Sun was our insider’s allegation that there has been at least three romances between prisoners and staff.

This includes one woman who allegedly became renowned among Millsike’s lag population for engaging in X-rated antics right under bosses’ noses.



Our source told us: “This officer would sneak off into the laundry room. She was well known for it among others on the landings.”

As for the alleged second, who worked in a management role, the source claims she was suspended after being “accused of an illicit relationship with an inmate”.

The third, which is said to involve a prison officer and happened in 2025, led to a suspension – but ended in tragedy.

Our source claims: “This lady arranged to visit her lover the following week. She was refused entry and unfortunately took her own life not long after that.”

In June this year, prison custody officer Beverley Frank, 42, received an eight-month suspended sentence after it was discovered she had a saucy relationship with a lag.



It is not known if she is one of the women spoken about by our insider.

But Frank, a mother, was found to have engaged in “steamy, sexualised exchanges” and sent erotic imagery, including snap in red underwear.

Frank, who was listed as ‘Jess Richardson’ and ‘Jess Love’ on the lag’s phone, was questioned about the month-long romance in September.



While being questioned, she admitted: “Do you know what? Yes, I have been doing it. I know it’s wrong.”

There is no suggestion Frank smuggled in a phone or drugs for the prisoner.

In addition to her suspended sentence, she was ordered to carry out 100 hours of unpaid work, 15 days of rehabilitation and was slapped with a one-year ban from contacting the prisoner.

While refusing to comment on individual cases, Mitie states they expect colleagues to uphold the highest standards of professionalism and take action when it has not been met.

The romance claims follow Freedom of Information request data published this week that revealed 32 prison officers across the UK were subjected to disciplinary action for an “inappropriate relationship” in the year to 2025.



While the figure appears low, only a handful of prisons across England and Wales submitted data, and it’s a dramatic 166 per cent rise and 20 more cases reported than in the year until 2018.

Former staff have spoken about concerns for their safety while walking down the Millsike’s wings – and that trepidation certainly wouldn’t have been helped by an incident on July 9.

That day, emergency services were called to the lock-up and locals told the BBC that they saw a “bomb squad vehicle” enter the prison site and later heard a “loud bang”.

Our insider says rumours have swirled that a makeshift “pipe bomb” was created from stolen lawnmower fuel.

Humberside Police and Humberside Fire and Rescue Service confirmed they did attend the prison, alongside an explosive ordnance disposal team.



Mitie insists they have never had an incident with a viable device or a detonation at the prison. They say they called in emergency services as part of their standard operating procedures.

Our insider tells us it is “comical that the prison denies there was a threat”. The source claims the lag who created the “device” was known for having a strong-disliking of authority figures.

They said: “He didn’t like staff and warned that he was going to cause a ‘huge problem’ for them, but wasn’t specific about what he meant.



“His partner called it in after he told her what he had done on the phone. He generally hated all figures of authority.

“They had to evacuate inmates directly above and below his call while the bomb squad came in and detonated it.

“Everyone in the prison heard the explosion. Local villagers saw the bomb squad driving in and heard the explosion too. But bizarrely, the prison continues to deny it.”

Prison officers told the BBC about “feeling unsafe on the wings” due to multiple incidents.

Trouble has also allegedly unfolded during outdoor exercise periods between ordinary and vulnerable prisoners – the latter our source describes as “mainly sex offenders and rapists”.



Despite being separated by fences and a distance apart, it is claimed that “low-level warfare” is regularly breaking out.

“To the ordinary prisoners, the prisoners on the other side are the scum of the earth,” they said. “There’s a lot of name calling and arguments breaking out.

“Issues are typically started by the vulnerable prisoners and they have chucked water bottles and fruit at prisoners on the other side.”

Staff seem to have been struggling too.

Steve Richardson, who worked in a maintenance capacity at Millsike for 10 months, told the BBC lags threw “faeces and urine” at him.



He also claimed a prisoner “absolutely lost it” and smashed six windows throwing pool balls and cues around. Mitie denies the claims.

Our insider suggests the incident took place in late 2025, during what is known inside as “the dark days”, when prisoners allegedly had less time out of cells due to staff shortages.

“There was a lot of hostility between prisoners and staff,” they said.

“Prisoners had a lot of anger towards the regime, which they considered poor and very inconsistent.”

In response to the problems, it was alleged that crooks were causing trouble and even flushing clothes down the toilet, leading to difficulties with the sewerage system. Mitie denies this.



Richardson also alleges a lag tried to escape by scaling a perimeter fence.

Thankfully, he was stopped by an elite prison squad from Operational Response and Resilience Unit (ORRU) who “stepped in and took him down”.

The ORRU, which only deals with the most serious incidents, was deployed to Millsike seven times in nine months during 2025, according to Freedom of Information request data.



That is triple the number of times it was called to HMP Fosse Way and HMP Northumberland and once more than HMP Oakwood. All three, like Millsike, are Cat C prisons..

Our insider claims lags have complained about being served “the worst food in the country” and once even said he received “raw, almost frozen chips”.

Mitie denies this and insists food is thoroughly checked before serving and that they have received no official complaints from prisoners.

Former prisoner officer Joe Chapman suspects many of the problems are due to Millsike being “pushed forward for opening far too early by the Government”.

He adds: “They are trying, but at this moment in time, in my opinion, failing.”



The Prison Reform Trust said it had received some “worrying and concerning” calls from prisoners fearing for their safety.

It’s believed the Independent Monitoring Board for the prison will publish its annual report next month, which will address safety concerns.

But for now, instead of being the exemplary blueprint for future prisons, it seems HMP Millsike is far from setting the bar.

A Mitie spokesperson told The Sun: “These allegations do not reflect the way the prison operates today.

“The prison works in line with established policies and procedures and is subject to independent oversight and scrutiny.



“The safety and wellbeing of prisoners, colleagues and visitors is a priority, and any concerns raised are taken seriously and investigated appropriately.

“Our teams provide professional care and support often in challenging circumstances, and we remain committed to maintaining a safe, secure and supportive environment for everyone in our care.”

The Ministry of Justice did not respond to The Sun’s request for comment.

News.title: Millionaire developer at war with irate neighbours demanding he rip down ‘monster’ mega-mansion ‘built illegally’
News.content:
TEAR IT DOWN Millionaire developer at war with irate neighbours demanding he rip down ‘monster’ mega-mansion ‘built illegally’

NEIGHBOURS next to a millionaire developer’s “mega mansion” are demanding it be torn down after it was erected without planning permission.

The monster-sized property on the edge of Bath has been constructed significantly higher and with a larger footprint than originally approved the local council.



Tavis Hamilton, 48, who lives next door, has spent 10 years battling developers and is now one of more than 100 locals to lodge formal objections.

With the seven-bedroom building, owned by Thomas Worrall, now “topped out” and nearly complete, a retrospective application has been submitted to validate the changes.



Local residents claim the situation highlights how multi-millionaires are able to exploit loopholes during the planning process – but the owner insists he’s “not the bad guy”, adding: “I just want to finish the job and move in with my family.”

The property is believed to be the biggest newbuild in the historic city of Bath for a century.



Bath and North-East Somerset Council declined to comment on the build, stating enforcement action would only be considered after the fresh application has been determined.

Mr Hamilton said: “It is an absolute mega home – it will prob be worth more than £3million when it’s finished.

“It is enormous and dwarfs all the cottages. You could fit around 24 of the other cottages into the footprint.”

He noted that the building work has spanned three years, but now it is topped out, the full scale and height are exposed.



He added: “It just shows how unfair the process is. It seems if you put the wrong guttering on your house or use the incorrect glazing, the council jump on you for enforcement.

“But you can build this enormous structure without the right planning permission and no enforcement is carried out until it is too late.”

More than 70 residents attended a recent site meeting to express their anger while construction continued.



Mr Hamilton explained that permission was initially granted for a low-lying, single-storey structure built into the hillside, but workers backfilled the excavation with concrete after striking groundwater.

The end result is a property positioned in a different spot and standing significantly higher than planned.

The plot has passed through three owners since 2007, with successive planning applications seeking to increase its height and prominence.

Council enforcement teams conducted a survey confirming multiple deviations from approved plans, including altered orientation, siting, height, volume, and footprint.

Mr Hamilton said: “The new application has been submitted as part of a wider game to avoid enforcement action.



“The changes are so significant and widespread that all the rest of the drawings from roof light location also require total update.”

He called for a cease order on all works, adding that had concerns been acted on when concrete was poured two years ago, the damage would have been far easier to rectify.

He added: “They have just pushed on and built whatever they wanted, with a slap dash, ill considered, gung-ho approach with total disregard to the approved plans.”



He described the process as deeply stressful, explaining that residents felt powerless while watching the character of the lane and nearby listed church be altered.

He added: “Some want to see it just torn down. It is an extreme measure and I don’t know if Bath and North East Somerset would ever enforce that.

“But it would be lovely to see it just built as it should have been.”

Mr Hamilton noted that his family are now sandwiched between two of the largest single residences built in Bath in a century.

He recalled that when previous excavators hit groundwater, they dumped rubble into the hole before selling, resulting in a structure that sits atop the hill rather than within it.



He said: “It has finally been propped up and reached roof height and it is taller than the listed church next door. It is monstrous.”

Another local objector stated on the council portal that the sheer volume of variations showed the developer treated formal approval as a mere box-ticking exercise.

They warned that approving extensive departures would create a dangerous precedent, rewarding unpermitted development that inflicts measurable harm on the environment.

Local ward district councillor Joanna Wright backed the residents, calling the development outrageous and questioning why enforcement had failed to stop it.

She said: “They are told they cannot do things and that is the end of it. Yet this developer ignores all that, they know the process so keep carrying on and jumping through all the hoops to get what they want.



“It is the reason people don’t trust politics and the planning process.”

Cllr Wright stressed that the build has severely impacted neighbours along the narrow single-track road, with windows now positioned right beside adjacent properties.

She added: “They should be made to tear it down. Why are they getting away with it.

“It is one rule for a wealthy person – they get what they want by playing the system – and another for everyone else.”

Bath and North East Somerset Council confirmed that the retrospective application is “currently being determined” and “formal enforcement action will only be considered” if it is refused.



In a design and access statement, agents for the applicant said the amendments were necessary for safety after encountering saturated ground and unstable foundations.

They asserted that the team tried to keep the building as low as possible and maintained that the actual scale and overall look above ground had hardly changed from approved plans.

House owner Mr Worrall defended the build, explaining he purchased the site with existing planning permission simply to build a family home.

“The whole street has been against me from day one,” he said.

“I only bought the site to build my own house with planning permission already on it. Someone else took it all to planning seven years ago.





“There have been complications on the ground and the professional builders were not able to make it work so it was a little bit higher to start with.”

He continued: “The neighbours all seem to think I have screwed the system and been sneaky. But I am not.

“I’ve now pulled all my guys off site and trying to deal with the planners.”

He explained that ground complications forced builders to raise the initial height and drop plans for a basement swimming pool, leading him to halt work entirely.

He added: “I am not the bad guy everyone seems to think I am.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“I just want to finish the job and move in with my family. Once it’s complete it will be a lovely building.”

Mr Worrall apologised for the inconvenience, promising the completed home would feature a green grass roof and that no further work would take place until planners were completely satisfied.

News.title: UK weather: Thunder, hail and lightning to batter Britain TODAY before ‘intense downpours’ hit, Met Office warns
News.content:
HAIL MARY UK weather: Thunder, hail and lightning to batter Britain TODAY before ‘intense downpours’ hit, Met Office warns

BRITS can expect to be battered by thunder, hail and lightning today before “intense downpours” strike, the Met Office has warned.

Scotland is already seeing showers this morning, particularly in western and southern parts, which stretch into northern England.



Scattered showers will mainly affect Scotland at the start of Sunday before spreading south into England, where some could turn heavy and thundery including around the Leeds Festival, the Met Office said.

Eastern parts will see the best of the sunshine moving into this afternoon.



However, a band of low pressure is forecast to dominate bringing rain to Northern Ireland and northern England, Wales and the South West.

Those rainy spells with bring some thunder, hail and “frequent lightning” as well as some gusty winds.

Reading Festival and Notting Hill Carnival could see occasional showers, with conditions turning wetter into the evening.

Met Office meteorologist Kathryn Chalk said: “Low pressure is firmly in charge throughout Sunday.



“This area of low pressure is moving its way eastwards bringing a rash of showers.”

In the sunshine though temperatures are expected to hit 23-24C but feeling cool during an “intense downpour”.

The low pressure will continue to move easterly during Sunday evening, bringing showers to many places.

Some clearer patches are predicted to move in behind as the bank holiday Monday gets underway.

There will be some brighter areas in the east initially, but showers will break out but are expected to be less “lively” than in recent days.



Most areas in the UK will see a “pleasant” afternoon.

Temperatures could reach 21-22C.

Nine areas were covered by Environment Agency flood alerts, meaning floods are possible, as of Saturday night.

It comes after continued hot weather across the UK, which coincided with extremely dry conditions.

The Met Office has previously said the UK is on course for its hottest summer on record after five heatwaves, with temperatures of up to 38.1C recorded in London.

News.title: Grandad, 85, killed after confronting burglars who broke into his home as cops hunt gang & probe ‘targeted’ attack
News.content:
DEATH MANHUNT Grandad, 85, killed after confronting burglars who broke into his home as cops hunt gang & probe ‘targeted’ attack

AN 85-year-old grandad has tragically died months after he was assaulted after confronting burglars who broke into his home.

Gordon Nicholass was attacked after bravely challenging those who broke into his property in Helmshore, Lancashire, shortly before 3am on April 29.

Gordon suffered a head injury and cuts to his face and was taken to hospital.

The grandad was initially discharged but was admitted to hospital again earlier this month before tragically passing away on August 12.





Cops have launched a major investigation to identify those responsible.

Detectives believe the attack may have been targeted and are working to establish a motive and the circumstances surrounding it.

Extensive damage was caused to the property during the burglary, although officers say nothing appears to have been stolen.

A Home Office postmortem examination has been carried out, but detectives are continuing to investigate whether the assault was a cause or contributory factor in his death.

In a tribute Gordon’s family said: “Gordon was a wonderful husband, dad and granddad.

“He was a lifelong motorcycle enthusiast and well known for his engineering skills.

“He was always there to do anything for anyone – family, friends even strangers, you name it!

“Mister fix it, Jack of all trades, we will all miss him dearly.”



Det Chief Insp Jill Vescovi, of our Force Major Investigation Team, said: “First and foremost my thoughts are with Gordon’s family and loved ones. We will continue to offer them any support they need at this time.

“We are working hard to try and establish who has done this and why and I would appeal to anyone with any information, however insignificant they may think it is, to come forward and speak to us.

“I would ask anyone in the area to please check CCTV /Doorbell cameras for any suspicious activity, people or vehicles that may have been in the area at around the time of the offence or in the days beforehand.”

Anyone with information is asked to contact police on 101, quoting log 0126 of April 29.

You can also contact independent charity Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111.

News.title: One dead after shooting at Swiss rave party as panicked festival-goers ‘hide under DJ booth’ – and cops hunt for gunman
News.content:
ONE person has died and several others are injured after a gunman opened fire at a packed rave in Switzerland.

Shots were fired into a large crowd during the Aarauer Rave at a horse racing track in Aarau, north of Zurich, early Sunday morning.



Cops have launched a frantic manhunt for the suspect with the public urged to avoid the area.

In a statement, Aargau Cantonal Police said: “Possible motives as well as the exact circumstances of the crime are still unclear.”



“Several shots were fired within a large group of people”, Vanessa Rumpold, media spokesperson for the Aargau Cantonal Police said.

In a further update cops said the manhunt is in “full swing, adding that it is unclear if the suspect is still in possession of a weapon.



Some 3,500 people attended the annual techno party between 3pm on Saturday and 2am on Sunday.

Swiss newspaper Blick reported that the shots were fired before 3am local time on the sidelines of the Aarauer Rave.



One witness recalled “bursts of gunfire” ripping through the rave.

A video obtained by the outlet shows the sound of multiple shots being fired at 2.35am.

Another witness initially mistook the shots for fireworks.



But when someone shouted “Everyone down!” she hid under the DJ booth with other terrified party goers.

Swiss DJ Tekibo, who was performing at the rave, said he “lost an important friend” in the shooting.

In a post on social media he wrote: “What happened at Aarauer rave is absolutely heartbreaking and something that should never have happened at our scene!

“I’m still trying to process what happened cause I lost an important friend and don’t have the right words for it.”

“RIP M”, he added.



Police have launched a large-scale operation with the Aargau Cantonal Disaster Response Unit (KKE) and an army Super Puma helicopter deployed to the scene.

Armed officers were spotted patrolling the highway up to 30km away from the shooting site.

Police confirmed on X before 6am that there are “several victims”.

“It is not yet clear what exactly happened”, Rumpold said.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Anyone with videos or photos of the incident is asked to send them to police to aid the investigation.



An area around the racing track, the town’s swimming pool and sports field has been cordoned off.

News.title: Two of PC Andrew Harper’s killers will NOT be freed after change to Early Release Scheme
News.content:
PC ANDREW Harper’s killers will remain behind bars after Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced changes to the early release scheme.

The PM said anyone convicted of unlawful killing – like Jessie Cole and Albert Bowers – would be exempt and will stay in prison.



Bowers and Cole were jailed for 13 years for the manslaughter of PC Harper, 28, who was dragged for more than a mile behind their car when he responded to reports of theft in 2019.

Plans to let out the killers in January – under Labour plans to release up to 5,000 prisoners over ten months from October – had sparked fury.



Now, Mr Burnham has said “hundreds” of people will remain in prison as part of changes to the scheme designed to ease prison overcrowding.

Prisoners convicted of historic child sex offences will also be blocked from changes.

Mr Burnham said: “I know how strongly people feel about this issue. I understand the concern and anger because I share it.

“That’s why I took action during my first weeks as Prime Minister to block some of the very worst in society being released before they should.



“We moved quickly to block vile criminals who commit rape, sexually abuse children and groom vulnerable young people.”

He continued: “But I always said I wanted to do more. We will now not only be keeping offenders serving time for indecent assault locked up, but also those in prison for manslaughter and death by dangerous driving.

“This means that the awful criminals responsible for the killing of PC Andrew Harper will not have their sentence shortened.”

The Prime Minister ordered a review of the changes to the Sentencing Act, which is being undertaken by Justice Secretary Alex Norris and is set to be published when Parliament returns from summer recess this week.

The changes increase the risk of the Government running out of space in jails, with only around 1,600 spare places available in men’s prisons, which are running at 98 per cent capacity.



Mr Burnham said extra space in prisons would be created by deporting foreign prisoners.

He is also looking to fix the dispute over Imprisonment for Public Protection (IPP) sentences — abolished in 2012 — under which more than 2,300 people are indefinitely detained or trapped in a cycle of lifelong recall, and the release of lower-risk offenders.

Mr Burnham added: “None of this is easy because people who were convicted under those sentences did cause harm. So it’s not an easy choice.



“However, I’ve applied common sense here, and I was faced with a situation where people on those sentences who have more than served their time not being released, when others who’ve committed very serious crimes being released early.”

The early release scheme is due to begin in October, with the first offenders freed in tranches over the next 10 months.

Full details of the latest changes are expected to be revealed by the Justice Secretary when Parliament returns.

Newly-married PC Harper died after getting caught up in a strap attached to the rear of a car.

He was dragged more than a mile as the killers fled the scene of a quad bike theft in Sulhamstead, Berks, in 2019.



Bowers and Cole, both 17 at the time of the crime, got 13 years in 2020 after being convicted of manslaughter and remain eligible to be freed in January, just halfway through their sentences.

Hopes were raised for PC Harper’s family when the PM ordered a review of the scheme.

Changes were made including preventing rapists and paedophiles from being let out early — but did not include those convicted of manslaughter like Bowers and Cole.

The exemption from early release will now be extended to voluntary manslaughter – intentional killing with a partial defence such as provocation – and gross negligence manslaughter caused by extreme carelessness.

The rule changes mean up to 500 killers convicted of manslaughter will no longer be released early from October.



Thames Valley Police welcomed confirmation from the Prime Minister that Bowers and Cole will not be released under the early release arrangements that had previously been proposed.

Chief Constable Jason Hogg said: “Today’s confirmation that these offenders will not be released under the proposed arrangements will be welcomed by many across policing and our communities.

“Over recent weeks we have consistently expressed our concerns about the potential impact these release arrangements could have had on Andrew Harper’s family, friends and colleagues, the wider policing service and the communities he served.

“I am grateful that those concerns were listened to and carefully considered. Throughout this process, our focus has been on ensuring that the voices of victims, families, colleagues and communities were heard and understood and properly considered alongside the wider challenges facing the criminal justice system.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“We know this case has resonated far beyond Thames Valley Police. Today’s announcement may bring reassurance not only to Andrew’s family, but to other victims and bereaved families who have followed this issue closely and who continue to seek confidence that the most serious offences are treated with the gravity they deserve.



“Today is not about politics. It is about remembering Andrew, recognising the profound impact his death continues to have on those who knew him, the communities he protected and those who serve in policing today.”

News.title: Shocking moment fire breaks out on luxury 30ft boat after explosion on board sparked huge trail of smoke as 3 injured
News.content:
THIS is the shocking moment a boat is seen up in flames as thick plumes of choking smoke billow into the air.

Three people were rushed to hospital after a luxury 30ft vessel exploded off the coast of City Island in the Bronx and sparked a huge fireball.



The terrifying inferno unfolded at around 1.40pm.

Shocking footage shows flames raging across the body of the vessel as a thick column of black smoke spirals into the sky.



Two people can be seen hugging on the docks as they watch the terrifying scene.

Half of the hull collapsed and was destroyed in the blast as the sleek white vessel transformed into a blackened husk.



More than 70 firefighters from 21 units raced to the scene of the inferno.

Rescuers rushed three people to hospital with minor injuries.

The boat had been docked at 691 Bridge St. in City Island when it ignited from causes as yet unknown.

Firefighters battled the flames for nearly an hour.



Cops have launched a probe into the mystery explosion.

It comes as a horror blast ripped through a charter boat in Florida, hospitalising 15.

The vessel exploded in Biscayne Bay, a bustling tourist spot in Miami in May.



Two children were among the victims – with one being treated for 18 per cent burns which scorched his body.

An adult is also in hospital with burns covering roughly 30 per cent of his skin.

Last year a boat captain was arrested following the explosion of his vessel.

More than 20 of his passengers leapt into icy waters to escape the boat-turned-fireball.

News.title: Man, 49, ‘seriously injured’ after incident on 147ft Batman rollercoaster in Madrid
News.content:
Man, 49, ‘seriously injured’ after incident on 147ft Batman rollercoaster in Madrid

A man was flown to hospital by air ambulance after an incident on the Batman Gotham City Escape rollercoaster at the Warner Park in Madrid.

View Image Warner Theme Park in Madrid, Spain (file photo)

A man has been left with potentially serious injuries after an incident on a rollercoaster at a popular amusement park in Spain.

‌



The 49-year-old was airlifted to hospital after suffering injuries on the Batman Gotham City Escape ride at Warner Park in Madrid on Saturday.

‌



The man reportedly broke both his legs on the coaster, which features a 98-degree drop from a height of 45 metres (147ft) and multiple complete turns and reaches speeds of up to 100 kilometres per hour.

‌



Emergency workers said the man had suffered an open fracture in his left leg as well as a closed fracture in his right leg, EuropaPress reports.

Park management said the ride had been stopped immediately and emergency procedures had been activated, with the injured man treated by emergency teams at the scene.

‌



After initial treatment at the scene, he was taken by air ambulance to the 12 de Octubre Hospital where he was reportedly admitted in a potentially serious condition for further evaluation.

The roller coaster remains closed while the incident is investigated in coordination with the authorities after Spanish Civil Guard and local police officers also arrived at the scene following the incident.

Juan José Molina, who was in the park at the time, around 2:30 p.m., told Europa Press that after the incident "there were people crying and having anxiety attacks." He added that the rest of the park was operating normally after the incident.

Article continues below

In a statement on social media the park’s owners, Parque Warner Madrid, said: “There was an incident today at the Batman Gotham City Escape, Warner Park attraction.

“The attraction stopped immediately and our emergency procedures were activated. The victim was treated immediately by the emergency services.

“Currently the roller coaster remains closed while the incident is being reviewed in coordination with the authorities.”

News.title: Nutrition expert says this 41p ingredient helps lower cholesterol
News.content:
Nutrition expert says this 41p ingredient helps lower cholesterol

A cheap supermarket staple could be an easy way to change what goes on your plate

View 3 Images Lower your cholesterol by adding this cheap ingredient to your plate (Image: Cris Cantón)

Keeping cholesterol under control does not necessarily mean making expensive changes to your weekly shop. One familiar cupboard staple costs as little as 41p at major UK supermarkets, and can be used in everything from curries to salads.

‌



The food in question is chickpeas, with nutrition expert Lucy Kershaw of Nature’s Best highlighting them as one of several affordable foods that can form part of a cholesterol-friendly diet. Tesco currently lists its own-brand 400g chickpeas in water at 41p.

‌



Chickpeas do not directly lower cholesterol on their own, but they can help people make dietary swaps that support healthier cholesterol levels. Kershaw explained: "Some red and processed meats, including sausages, bacon and ham, can be high in saturated fat, which can contribute to higher cholesterol levels when eaten in excess.

‌



View 3 Images High cholesterol leads to a buildup of fatty plaques in your arteries (Image: Getty Images)

"Replacing some of these foods with plant-based protein sources such as chickpeas, beans and lentils is a simple way to reduce your saturated fat intake. Canned chickpeas and legumes are inexpensive and convenient, while dried versions can be bought in bulk for just a few pounds."

The NHS says eating too much saturated fat can raise the amount of LDL, or "bad", cholesterol in the blood and increase the risk of heart disease. Its guidance recommends adding vegetables and beans to meals as one way of reducing the amount of saturated fat eaten.

‌



Chickpeas are part of the pulses family and are naturally low in fat while providing fibre and protein. The NHS says pulses including beans, peas and lentils are naturally low in fat and high in fibre, protein, vitamins and minerals

HEART UK also lists chickpeas among its cholesterol-smart protein choices, alongside other beans and lentils. It recommends including pulses regularly as part of a healthy diet, with a serving roughly equivalent to half a large can when drained.

View 3 Images Assorted legumes in burlap sacks with chickpeas, lentils, soybean and beans (Image: Getty Images)

Article continues below

The 41p Tesco tin can be added to a number of everyday meals without much preparation. Kershaw suggests using chickpeas in sauces, dips, curries and casseroles, while they can also be roasted and added to salads or stir-fries.

You shouldn't rely on one ingredient as a quick fix. HEART UK also recommends eating plenty of plant-based foods, including vegetables, pulses, fruit, nuts, seeds and wholegrains, while choosing healthier sources of protein and reducing foods high in saturated fat.

Kershaw recommends the likes of avocado, sardines, oats and barley, berries and foods containing plant sterols as other affordable or useful options for people looking to improve their diet. Anyone with concerns about high cholesterol should speak to a GP or healthcare professional before making significant dietary changes.

News.title: Sarah Ferguson to appear in TV documentary as part of UK comeback plan
News.content:
Sarah Ferguson to appear in TV documentary as part of UK comeback plan

The former Duchess of York is said to have been inundated with requests as she maintains a tight friendship group in the UK despite the fallout from her Epstein associations

View 3 Images Fergie is reportedly high in demand following her return to the UK (Image: Kirsty Wigglesworth/PA Wire)

Sarah Ferguson is set to appear in a tell-all documentary and interview as she returns from exile to a tidal wave of requests, it has been reported.

‌



The former Duchess of York left the UK amid fallout from hers and former Prince Andrew's association with paedophile financier Jeffrey Epstein, and the latter's arrest on suspicion of misconduct in public office. She is now said to have returned, having spent seven months abroad on mainland Europe.

‌



Her return has not gone unnoticed, with a source claiming she has been "bombarded with requests" as she reportedly settles into a £10,000-a-month Home Counties property.

‌



Sarah Ferguson in UK comeback plan following Harry and Meghan's return READ MORE :

View 3 Images Sarah Ferguson is reportedly returning to the UK (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

The source told The Sun that Fergie has been approached by "big streamers" to sit down for interviews and "tell her side of the story". They said: “Fergie has been bombarded with requests from all over the world to do sit-down interviews, especially with the big streamers, to tell her side of the story.

“She is looking at her options. For her, it’s more about retaining editorial control rather than making money.” The former left the UK earlier this year after she was dropped by multiple charities and stripped of her honours.

‌



The major shunning stemmed from fallout over her previous association with Epstein, revealed in the release of a tranche of three million emails from the US Department of Justice in January. In one email released amongst the trove from 2011, she privately apologises for publicly rejecting Epstein.

View 3 Images Andrew and Fergie divorced in the 1990s (Image: Popperfoto via Getty Images)

She says: "You have always been a steadfast, generous and supreme friend to me and my family." Another email indicated that she took her daughters to see the disgraced financier days after he was released from prison for child sex crimes.

‌



The emails do not serve as an indication of any wrongdoing, of which Ms Ferguson has never been accused. Andrew has strenuously denied any wrongdoing stemming from his relationship with Epstein.

Despite the immense public pressure, and both former royals having been stripped of their honours and top positions, Fergie remains well connected in the UK, the source said. They claimed: “Sarah has a tight-knit group of friends and is extremely well connected.

“She would only allow someone she knew well to tell her story.” The news comes after another source said she had been eyeing her return to the UK for some time.

Article continues below

They said: “She’s had her eyes on a return for some time but it takes time to find the right new house. She hasn’t had to worry about accommodation for 20 years as she had Royal Lodge with Andrew. Now’s the right time to get back to her life. With everyone looking out for Harry and Meghan she thought she could slip back under the radar after seven months away."

News.title: One dead and five injured in Switzerland rave shooting as manhunt under way
News.content:
One dead and five injured in Switzerland rave shooting as manhunt under way

Police cars, ambulances, and firefighters descended on the rave at a racecourse in the Swiss town of Aarau after gunshots rang out at 2.30am this morning

View Image Armed police officers block a street near the Schachen horse racing track near Aarau, Switzerland (Image: MICHAEL BUHOLZER/EPA/Shutterstock)

A manhunt is underway after one person was killed and five injured in a shooting at a rave party in Switzerland in the early hours of this morning, police say.

‌



Emergency services descended on the party, which was held at a racecourse in the Swiss town of Aarau.

‌



Police cars, ambulances, and firefighters arrived on the scene at about 3am, shortly after multiple shots were fired at around. One person is dead, and five others were injured, some seriously, Blick reports.

‌



Authorities are still hunting the shooter, according to local media reports. "The search for the unknown perpetrators is ongoing. Possible motives and the exact circumstances of the incident are still unclear," a police spokesperson told reporters.

Vanessa Rumpold, media spokesperson for the Aargau Cantonal Police said: "It is not yet clear what exactly happened." Cops confirmed that "several shots" had been fired.

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

A Disaster Response Unit and an army Super Puma helicopter were spotted at the scene as area around the horse racing track remains cordoned off by armed police with a major search getting underway.

One eyewitness described how they hid under the DJ booth after the shooting started, while others reportedly thought the shots were fireworks at first. Multiple witnesses reported hearing “repeated gunfire” during the terrifying incident.

Article continues below

A nearby swimming pool is also reportedly closed and the area around the horse racing track and sports field is cordoned off while there is a heightened police presence in the area as the hunt for the suspect or suspects continues.

Pictures from the scene show armed police officers and an armoured vehicle at the site of the incident, meanwhile dashcam footage taken in the early hours shows armed cops stationed throughout the town of Aarau.

News.title: Big Church Festival live: Hero helped lift sign off victims after it came 'crashing down' killing man
News.content:
A huge wooden sign carrying the words “Everything’s Unmissable” fell on the man who died, according to an eyewitness.

One person has died after a sign fell on people at Big Church Festival in Steyning in West Sussex, with ambulance crews treating six people at the scene

Big Church Festival live: Hero helped lift sign off victims after it came 'crashing down' killing man

A 41-year-old man has died after a huge wooden sign came “crashing down” onto people at Big Church Festival in Steyning.

The sign, which reportedly carried the words “Everything’s Unmissable”, fell near a tented area at the Christian festival in West Sussex on Friday afternoon.

One eyewitness has since revealed he and his wife were walking just a few paces behind when the sign came down. He said they rushed to help lift it off those underneath and gave first aid alongside others until paramedics arrived.

Six people were treated for injuries following the incident at around 3.38pm. Sussex Police later confirmed a man from Eastbourne had died.

The festival, which had been due to continue until Sunday, has now been cancelled by organisers.

South East Coast Ambulance Service was called to reports of multiple people in need of medical attention, while an air ambulance was pictured leaving the scene.

News.title: UK corner shop chain to close all stores as it plunges into liquidation
News.content:
UK corner shop chain to close all stores as it plunges into liquidation

The independently owned corner shop chain will close all of its locations after nearly 40 years with the local community stating they will be 'sorely missed'

View 2 Images The UK corner shop chain will close all five stores (Image: Google )

A UK mini-chain of corner shops is set to shut all stores after nearly 40 years.

‌



The retailer announced the closures after plunging into liquidation.

‌



The five Premier Foreways stores in Carlisle will close with Armstrong Watson appointed as liquidator.

‌



View 2 Images The independently owned stores have entered liquidation (Image: Google )

The shops operated under the Premier brand but are independently owned.

The locations had been open for nearly four decades, a staple corner shop in the community.

‌



Residents labelled the closures of the Wigton Road, Bedford Road, Blackwell Road, Newlaithes Avenue, and Warwick Road stores a 'shame'.

One local posted on Facebook: “They’ve been there so long. Hope the staff find something else.”

Others added that the shelves has been 'empty a while' with others saying they thought they 'were doing okay'.

‌



The shops were owned by Billy Bone, who has been praised on social media by many previous employees.

One posted: "Good employers like this are few and far between, and I know many of the staff who have worked for them over the years will wholeheartedly agree. They will be sorely missed in the community."

Mr Bone said the decision to enter liquidation was a difficult one as they were the first Premier stores in Carlisle.

‌



A spokesperson for Armstrong Watson said: “We can confirm that Armstrong Watson has been instructed by the directors to assist them in placing the company into liquidation," reports the News and Star.

Premier is a convenience store brand owned by Tesco with more than 4,000 shops across the UK.

A majority of the stores across the nation carry the Premier signage but are also independently owned.

Article continues below

The next steps of the stores are currently unclear.

News.title: PC Harper's killers to stay in jail as PM announces changes to early release scheme
News.content:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham has told the BBC that PC Andrew Harper's killers will remain behind bars as he announced changes to the early release scheme aimed at easing prison overcrowding.

In an exclusive interview with BBC Breakfast, Burnham said anyone convicted of unlawful killing, including all forms of manslaughter, will be excluded from the scheme, which would have made two of the officer's killers eligible for early release.

Burnham said extra prison space would be created by deporting foreign prisoners and releasing some inmates serving indefinite sentences.

It follows months of campaigning from PC Harper's family and former colleagues to block the release of his killers.

The 28-year-old was responding to a burglary in Berkshire in 2019 when he was dragged along a road by a vehicle as three teenagers fled the scene of a quad bike theft.

When it emerged that two of the killers, Jessie Cole and Albert Bowers, could be released early, there were passionate calls for the government to intervene and block those convicted of manslaughter from early release.

"I heard obviously what Andrew Harper's family were saying, I mean who couldn't? Nobody would want a position to arise where those guilty of killing a police officer are let out early from prison," Burnham told the BBC.

He conceded the announcement will mean "hundreds" more people stay in prison, meaning additional space will need to be found in a system that is more than 97% full in England and Wales.

News.title: Burnham gets the early prison release changes he wanted - but at what cost?
News.content:
The prime minister's announcement that he will keep hundreds of criminals behind bars who would otherwise have been released early is one he has wanted to make for weeks.

Andy Burnham had already expanded the list of people ineligible for early release and had consistently said he wanted to go further.

What is not clear is exactly what has changed to allow him to do so.

Earlier this month, the Ministry of Justice warned that exempting any more prisoners risked "prisons reaching capacity and collapsing".

The prime minister himself previously said he had "pushed to the very limits of what is possible to do".

In his exclusive interview with BBC Breakfast, Burnham picked out the release of people on controversial indefinite sentences and the deportation of foreign criminals as measures that had made his latest intervention possible.

It is understood extra capacity will also be created by immediately beginning work to create new cells in existing prisons.

But none of these are short-term solutions.

Ending indefinite sentences will require new legislation, meaning it could be years before space is freed up.

Previous governments have struggled to quickly deport foreign offenders and there are not thought to be any new returns agreements with other countries. The case of grooming gang ringleader Shabir Ahmed, who Pakistan has resisted attempts to deport, is one example.

Retrofitting prisons to create more cells is also expected to take months.

People in government concede that in the short-term, Burnham will only be able to follow through on today's announcement by making prisons even more full.

With the adult male prison estate already running at 98% capacity, it is a move that could worry some in the sector.

But in the end, the prime minister believed he simply had to act.

The extra exemptions Burnham has announced are being described within government as a "political decision".

That is not surprising given the intense pressure that had built up, especially around the potential for PC Andrew Harper's killers to be released early.

Burnham's inner circle are mindful that political misjudgements at the start of Sir Keir Starmer's premiership caused long-lasting damage.

They believe Sir Keir never recovered from early rows over freebies and winter fuel payments, and point to a lack of major mishaps in Burnham's first six weeks in office as evidence of a more slick political operation.

There was some surprise in Downing Street about how much media attention the issue of early release received over the summer.

That is one reason why the prime minister's aides are relishing the new parliamentary term, when news stories come along at a faster rate and so are less likely to linger in the headlines.

After the initial flip-flopping on whether the government would be able to exempt more prisoners, the mother of PC Harper told BBC Breakfast that the handling of the situation had been a "hash".

Government officials working on the plans have spoken to the families of victims, who made it clear they did not want the new measures to be dripped out in leaks to the media.

Instead it was decided one big announcement would be the neatest option.

It had seemed likely that would come in the form of a parliamentary statement on Tuesday from the justice secretary.

Instead, the prime minister decided to make the announcement himself in an interview with BBC Breakfast.

It is understood Burnham was mindful of mounting speculation and wanted to give victims and the public as much certainty at the earliest possible opportunity.

In doing so, he may have risked the ire of the Speaker Sir Lindsay Hoyle, who is generally disdainful of governments that make major announcements outside of Parliament.

He may also have offered up ammunition to the Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch, who has already accused Burnham of being a "people pleaser" who finds it difficult to say no to people.

That characterisation is likely to be tested again when more stories inevitably appear about the victims of prisoners who will still be released early.

It already started on Sunday morning, when the domestic abuse commissioner said she remained "deeply concerned about the number of abusers" still set to be freed.

While this is not the first time Burnham has said he has pushed the system to the limit, Whitehall sources are now adamant there will be no more additional exemptions.

News.title: Search continues for boat 'in distress' in Channel as two people still missing
News.content:
Rescue efforts are continuing for a vessel in distress in the English Channel as two crew members remain missing, the Maritime and Coastguard Agency has said.

A coastguard rescue helicopter, fixed wing plane and two RNLI lifeboats began searching an area south-west of Eddystone Lighthouse off Plymouth shortly after 18:00 BST on Saturday night.

In an update early on Sunday, HM Coastguard in Falmouth confirmed three of the five people aboard the boat had now been accounted for. It did not share further information about the vessel or the nature of the emergency.

A large number of civilian vessels were assisting the "intensive search", a HM Coastguard spokesperson added.

They also confirmed that an intensive search was maintained during the night.

"It is continuing today with multiple assets sent to help," they said.

Lifeboat crews from Newlyn and Salcombe have taken over the search from the Plymouth and Falmouth RNLI crews, who worked through the night.

News.title: British heavyweight Moses Itauma handed harsh world-title lesson
News.content:
It would be too simplistic - and unfair - to say Hrgovic won the fight purely through mind games, but the 34-year-old had succeeded in making the build-up uncomfortable.

Hrgovic spent fight week repeatedly attacking Itauma's age, dismissing him as "just a kid". As the week wore on, Itauma looked increasingly irritated and eventually lost his composure at the weigh-in, shoving Hrgovic before the Croatian responded with a slap.

Itauma prides himself on being unusually cerebral for a heavyweight. He reads psychology and self-help books, talks openly about sharpening his mind and appears to spend far more time analysing himself than most 21-year-olds.

But there is always a danger that deep thinking becomes overthinking, something Anthony Joshua has been accused of repeatedly during the latter stages of his career.

Whether the pre-fight barbs played any part or not, Itauma's gameplan once the bell rang was clear; he wanted to end the night early.

"Someone said to me he doesn't feel like he'd win a world title unless he knocks him out. I didn't like that," promoter Frank Warren said afterwards.

That mindset was understandable because it had served Itauma extraordinarily well until now. But perhaps Hrgovic had been underestimated by almost everybody - Itauma, the media, pundits, former fighters and bookmakers who installed the Briton as a heavy favourite.

Hrgovic is an Olympic bronze medallist who went 12 hard rounds with the giant Zhilei Zhang, while against Daniel Dubois - the only defeat on his record - he was leading on two of the three scorecards before the fight was stopped because of cuts.

'El Animal' knew what it felt like to be hurt, to become tired and to remain in a fight when things were going badly. Itauma did not.

News.title: China censors videos showing deadly flash floods on the Nepal-Tibet border
News.content:
Dramatic footage showing flash floods tearing through the main border crossing between Nepal and Tibet has been widely shared around the world.

But the footage has become almost impossible to find on China's heavily censored internet service, with only a single image broadcast by state media.

Hundreds of people are feared dead, and thousands remain missing as a major rescue operation continues into the weekend.

On Saturday, Chinese state media shared videos of rescue teams searching through mud and debris, but there has been little footage of the floods themselves, or accounts from survivors or anxious families.

Tibet remains a highly sensitive subject for China following its annexation in the 1950s. The region has long demanded greater autonomy and is one of the most strictly controlled regions in the country, with access for foreign media tightly restricted.

Read more on this story.

News.title: 97-year-old woman rescued after Nepali floods looked like 'a warrior'
News.content:
A 97-year-old woman pulled from flood debris in Nepal is recovering in hospital, according to her doctors.

Guna Maya Bohara's great-nephew, Dipak Bohara, has told BBC Nepali she looked like "a warrior" who had returned victorious from battle.

The operation to pull Bohara out of the rubble of her care home took four hours.

Bohara travelled from Kathmandu to help rescue his great-aunt.

Hundreds of people have been confirmed dead after Wednesday's flash floods, which scientists believe were triggered by a glacier collapsing in the Himalayan border region with Tibet.

Video produced by Mansi Kapur and Kamal Pariyar. Video edited by Suneth Perera, Jasmin Dyer and Andrew Webb.

More on this story here.

News.title: What we know about the 33 British nationals missing in Nepal
News.content:
Families are flying out to Nepal to help the ongoing search for 33 British nationals still missing after deadly floods hit the country.

The brother of Neetu Goyal Tiwari, one of the missing Brits who has not been seen since Wednesday, has appealed to officials to locate his sister.

"Please help us find her", Naresh Goyal told the BBC as he struggled to hold back his emotions.

On Friday, Nepalese authorities named 573 tourists who are still missing in the country and despite fears of a second wave of flooding, search efforts have continued.

To help, the UK is deploying a rapid deployment team to Nepal to support British nationals affected in the region.

The specially-trained crisis response team is expected to arrive in Kathmandu on Saturday, a move that follows Prime Minister Andy Burnham's pledge of Â£5m worth of humanitarian support for relief and recovery efforts.

And as rescue efforts continue in the aftermath of the disaster which killed at least 538 people, details of the missing are slowly emerging.

News.title: They fell in love - then had to check they weren't brother and sister
News.content:
For years, Arthur Kermalvezen, the child of a sperm donor, saw possible fathers everywhere he went. "I imagined it might be my teacher, the people I saw on the bus... and I was very angry because it's impossible to live like this."

When, as an adult, he fell in love with Audrey, another sperm donor baby from Paris, the question became even more pressing.

Audrey describes the moment they met at a gathering for donor conceived activists in 2010 as "love at first sight" - but was this connection a romantic or genetic attraction?

When they were born, there were only two sperm banks in Paris and many men had made multiple donations - so there was a real possibility they could be half-siblings.

Before building a life together, Arthur and Audrey needed to know whether they were related. But in France, laws governing genetic testing and donor anonymity made finding the answer extremely difficult.

News.title: Girl faces six-month recovery after 'freak accident' bus crash on holiday
News.content:
After eight days in hospital, Greta was transported back to the UK for treatment with Williams in an air ambulance which their Â£106 travel insurance policy covered.

"They [the pilots and medics] told me it cost â¬50,000 just for the flight. That was quite scary, Â£106 paid for that. Anything can happen."

Williams said Jet2, which sold them the package holiday, waived the cost of changing Len and Eiry-ana's flights back to the UK.

Greta was admitted to The Grange University Hospital in Cwmbran and had physiotherapy, and will find out on 2 September whether she can return to school.

"We can't do anything until that assessment. It's strict bedrest at the minute.

"She's not allowed to do much, she's not allowed to walk loads or do much which is a massive shame. Her friends have been fantastic."

Williams added: "She was petrified when it happened. All she wanted was reassurance from me. We tried to keep it as positive as we could in the circumstances.

"She was phenomenally strong. I'm so proud of how she coped."

"This is something that's going to haunt us forever," added Williams.

"It's going to take a long time to get over it all. We need normality to hit first, as we're in the summer holidays, before we can process it properly.

"You can see the accident has impacted them, and being in a foreign country has escalated their fears.

"We were trying to fill it in with so many experiences and memories as possible to make it fun-filled.

"They don't want to go on holiday ever again. We're going to try and take them somewhere - probably not on an excursion - to ease their mind. It was a one-off freak accident, and these things don't generally happen."

Graeme Buck from the Association of British Travel Agents said travel insurance was "one of the must-haves whenever you travel overseas".

"While most holidays go ahead without any problems, accidents and unexpected events can happen, and the costs of medical treatment and getting home can be significant.

"Cheap isn't always the best, and it's important not to choose a policy based on price alone. Holidaymakers should check what their policy covers and make sure they have comprehensive cover that is appropriate for their trip, including any activities they plan to take part in, such as winter sports."

News.title: Cleverly quits shadow cabinet to run for London mayor
News.content:
Conservative MP Sir James Cleverly has said he is resigning from the shadow cabinet to run for London mayor.

"I am putting myself forward to be the Conservative candidate for mayor of London, because our capital needs more than an administrator," he wrote in the Times, external.

Sir James said he has told Tory leader Kemi Badenoch he is stepping down as shadow housing secretary, saying: "I must be free to speak about every aspect of London's future and concentrate fully on winning this race."

The capital is not set to vote on a new mayor until May 2028. Labour incumbent Sir Sadiq Khan is yet to confirm whether he will seek an unprecedented fourth term.

The Conservatives are yet to pick their candidate for the London mayoral race.

A source close to Badenoch said Cleverly "is a formidable politician and will out-campaign Khan".

Sir James, who was foreign secretary under former Prime Minister Rishi Sunak, wrote that he intended to make London a city to be proud of again.

"We must rebuild its reputation and make it, once again, the best place in the world to live, work, invest and build a business," he added.

A senior Conservative politician, Sir James has held a number of ministerial positions under three prime ministers - including roles as home secretary and education secretary.

The army reservist represented the Tories on the London Assembly before his election as MP for Braintree in 2015.

After rising through the backbenches, he unsuccessfully ran for Conservative party leader in 2024, losing out to Badenoch.

Reacting to Sir James's announcement, a source said Badenoch "really didn't want James to leave shadow cabinet", but believed "he will be a big asset in London".

Current London Mayor Sir Sadiq began his first term in 2016. Cleverly wrote that the capital has been "let down by Labour".

He accused Prime Minister Andy Burnham of treating London as a "cash cow: somewhere to tax, regulate, raid and blame".

Sir James said: "Londoners need homes they can afford to buy or rent. Entrepreneurs need to be able to start and grow businesses without being strangled by cost and regulation."

The last time Londoners voted for their mayor in May 2024, Sir Sadiq beat Conservative rival Susan Hall by more than 275,000 votes - representing a swing of 3.2% to Labour.

The mayor won nine of the 14 constituencies including two gains from the Tories, and gained 43.8% of the vote share.

Reform UK revealed its candidate for the May 2028 election in January when it announced Westminster City councillor Laila Cunningham would be standing.

Reacting on social media, Reform UK leader Nigel Farage wrote the Conservatives are "done for", and said Cleverly "will not be the first Tory MP to give up any hope of winning their seat in Essex".

Cleverly has not resigned as an MP yet.

His announcement follows speculation in recent weeks that he would step down and launch a bid to become London's next mayor.

During his time at the London Assembly, Cleverly chaired the London Fire and Emergency Planning Authority, and also worked for Boris Johnson while he was mayor of London.

News.title: Christian festival 'devastated' after man's death
News.content:
Organisers of a Christian festival say they are "devastated" after a man died and six other people were injured by a falling sign.

Sussex Police said it had been called to the Big Church Festival at Wiston Park, near Steyning in West Sussex, at about 15:38 BST on Friday.

It was later confirmed a 41-year-old man from Eastbourne in East Sussex had died.

The Archbishop of Canterbury said she was "sad and shocked" to hear about the fatal incident.

Dame Sarah Mullally said: "I pray for his family, friends and loved ones as they grieve. I pray for those receiving treatment, and the healthcare workers looking after them.

"And I pray too for the other festival goers, staff and event organisers as they come to terms with these tragic events.

"May the God of comfort and healing be with them all."

South East Coast Ambulance service said four of the six people injured were taken to local hospitals for further treatment, with two people having serious injuries.

The Big Church Festival, which describes itself as the UK's biggest Christian festival, was founded in 2009.

The festival began on Friday and was due to continue until Sunday, but a decision was made by organisers to cancel the remainder of the event after the incident.

"We are working with the emergency services, police and the Health and Safety Executive as they establish the circumstances surrounding today's incident," the organisers said.

"We are incredibly grateful to everyone who responded, and to our teams and community for the care they have shown one another."

News.title: Strong winds and thunderstorms kick off the bank holiday weekend
News.content:
After weeks of scorching heat and drought the summer's swan song is set to be one of frequent downpours as well as gales for some.

Areas of heavy rain and showers are expected to sweep across parts of the UK on each day of the weekend, which is a bank holiday for many.

This could make for some soggy moments at many of the festivals taking place over the coming days.

Strong winds and gales may also cause problems for travellers and holidaymakers in southern parts of the UK.

News.title: Swimmers told to avoid beauty spot as 'hidden hazards' revealed by drought and fires
News.content:
People have been warned to stay away from a popular beauty spot pond used for swimming and other water sports due to "hidden hazards" exposed by reduced water levels.

Keepers Pond in Abergavenny poses "serious safety risks" with levels dangerously low, according to Bannau Brycheiniog National Park, also known as the Brecon Beacons.

It said that along with the prolonged dry spell, the water had been used to tackle recent wildfires.

"As the water has receded, previously hidden hazards and unknown objects have been exposed on the pond bed, creating serious safety risks. For your own safety, you must not enter the water under any circumstances," the park authority said in a Facebook post, external.

News.title: 'Click, don't pick' warning as fungi posts mushroom
News.content:
Social media posts showcasing fungi picking is affecting a forest's ecosystem, according to officials.

Picking wild mushrooms from Epping Forest in Essex is banned under by-laws but fungi-related content has surged in popularity online.

Foragers risk getting fined or prosecuted for picking the mushrooms, but they can also be poisonous if eaten.

Caroline Haines, the chair of the City Corporation's Epping Forest and Commons Committee, said posts showing mushrooms being collected "can encourage others to follow suit" and urged people to "click, don't pick".

Picking the fungi can disrupt the forest's ecosystem, which helps recycle nutrients, support wildlife, and preserve some 55,000 ancient trees.

However, fungi-related content continues to grow in popularity on social media, with posts showcasing unusual mushrooms and foraging finds attracting large audiences.

News.title: Woman detained in Egypt over 'sister's activism'
News.content:
A mother-of-four from Birmingham has been detained by the Egyptian authorities, with her husband and lawyer claiming it is due to her sister's online activism.

Eman el-Shazly, 45, from Handsworth Wood, was taken from her mother's house in Cairo in the early hours of Monday 17 August. Her husband, Zeesharn Moustapha, said this was 24 hours after Egyptian security forces "ram-raided" the property and told her: "You need to tell your sister to stop".

Three of el-Shazly's other siblings have also been detained, with her two brothers already being held when she was taken, and one of her sisters detained soon after.

The BBC has contacted the Egyptian consulate in London but has not had a response.

Moustapha said: "The family's a bit traumatised. [The children] are heartbroken.

"We really need the UK government to get their fingers out as quickly as possible."

A spokesperson for the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO) said: "We are supporting the family of a British national detained in Egypt, and are in contact with the authorities."

News.title: Royal Navy warships track Russian vessels for three days in UK waters
News.content:
Royal Navy warships and a helicopter spent three days tracking Russian Navy vessels and sanctioned cargo ships in an "intense" operation in the North Sea and English Channel.

HMS Duncan, HMS St Albans and HMS Severn used radars to monitor four vessels last week, while a Merlin helicopter provided surveillance from the sky.

"Since that successful operation, we have seen Russian shadow fleet vessels increasingly forced to change their routes, imposing significant cost and delays to their journeys," Gen Sir Gwyn Jenkins, the First Sea Lord and Chief of Naval Staff, said.

It comes as data shows Royal Navy activity to monitor Russian movements is up 25% so far this year compared to 2025.

During the August operation, the Royal Navy warships including a Type 45 destroyer and a Type 23 frigate, tracked Russian destroyer Admiral Levchenko as it escorted sanctioned cargo vessels General Skobelev and Sparta south through the North Sea and into the English Channel.

The Royal Navy said Russia was "forced" to respond with "costly military resources" including the frigate Neustrashimy.

A statement said a Nato ally then took over monitoring off the coast of France, without specifying the country.

The operation comes after Royal Marine Commandos boarded a Russian "shadow fleet" oil tanker in the English Channel in June.

Marines joined by National Crime Agency (NCA) officers, with the support of the RAF, intercepted and boarded the Smyrtos in a six-hour operation - the first of its kind by UK armed forces.

NCA officers arrested an Indian national, 38, on suspicion of sanctions offences under the Russia Regulations and he was taken into custody.

News.title: Scandal of indefinite jail terms will end this parliament, Burnham says
News.content:

Read our Privacy notice

The prime minister has announced he will end the injustice of indefinite jail terms in this parliament in a major victory for victims of the scandal.

Andy Burnham said he had taken a “common sense” approach to Imprisonment for Public Protection (IPP) sentences, which he said he had “long-standing concerns” about.

The Independent has long campaigned for all IPP prisoners to have their sentences reviewed, highlighting the plight of thousands still languishing without a release date.

The action to address IPP comes as the government overhauls plan to release other prisoners early, including two of the killers of Pc Andrew Harper.

"I was faced with a situation where people on those sentences who have more than served their time, not being released when others who've committed very serious crimes being released early," he told the BBC.

"The judgement I've made is the public, in my view, would prefer a situation where people who have served their time to be considered for release before those who haven't."

The government will table legislation to terminate the sentences by the "end of this Parliament", he added.

The open-ended sentences – which The Independent has campaigned for more than two years to have reviewed – were outlawed in 2012, but not retrospectively. Introduced under New Labour in a bid to be tough on crime, they were handed to many repeat offenders, even if their crimes were minor. They have left thousands languishing without a release date, with some now having served up to 22 times longer than their original tariff.

Reacting to the news, campaigner Shirley Debono, whose son Shaun Lloyd has been recalled five times and served nearly 14 years for snatching a phone, said she was “absolutely overwhelmed”.

The mother, who co-founded IPP Committee in Action, said: “After all these years of campaigning, fighting, being ignored and watching IPP prisoners and their families suffer, to finally hear the prime minister say he will end the injustice of IPP sentences this parliament feels incredible.

“The words “people will no longer be trapped indefinitely under a sentence abolished more than a decade ago” are something I never thought I would hear from a prime minister.

“I’m so excited, but also emotional, because I know what this has meant for so many families. I’m thinking of every IPP prisoner who has spent years trapped under this sentence and every family who has fought alongside them.”

Now the fight is to ensure no one is left behind by the legislation being drafted, she said, adding: “After 12 years of campaigning, this is a massive moment.”

Campaign group United Group for Reform of IPP (UNGRIPP) said the IPP nightmare may finally be ending, halting “decades of disproportionate punishment, institutional trauma, and loss of hope”.

CEO Marc Conway said: “This is a day that thousands of families have spent years fighting for. For too long, their loved ones have been trapped by a sentence that was acknowledged as flawed over a decade ago.

“While we welcome this critical action by the government, we do so with heavy hearts for those who did not live to see this day, and for the families torn apart by years of endless uncertainty.

“Legislation alone cannot undo twenty years of damage, but it is the essential first step toward healing.”

UNGRIPP urged the Ministry of Justice and probation services to ensure that the implementation of this decision is swift, transparent, and accompanied by comprehensive community and mental health support for all those transitioning off IPP licenses and out of custody.

Tragically, the move comes too late for 96 IPP prisoners who took their own lives in after losing hope of getting out, including Tommy Nicol, who died aged 37 in 2015. Before he died, Tommy described his IPP sentence as “psychological torture of a person who is doing 99 years.”

More follows on this breaking news story…

Moses Itauma was taken to hospital as a precautionary measure after his IBF world heavyweight title bid ended in a ninth-round stoppage by new champion Filip Hrgovic.

Itauma was carried from the ring on a stretcher following an explosive clash for the vacant belt at The O2 that saw Hrgovic become Croatia’s first champion in the division.

The 21-year-old from Kent was in complete command of the fight but had punched himself out in search of the knockout and was exhausted when referee Howard Foster came to his rescue with trainer Ben Davison also throwing in the towel.

“Moses has gone to the hospital for a check up,” promoter Frank Warren said.

“It’s precautionary that he’s gone to the hospital. That’s what we always do to make sure because the most important thing is the boxer’s health.

“He’s there and he’s in the best place. We’ll see what happens when I’ve got a report. We’ll obviously let everybody know.

“He’s done something to his leg as well and he was quite tired. It was a high paced, fast fight for both the guys. It was just edge of your seat stuff all the way through.”

open image in gallery Hrgovic and Itauma slugged it out in the final rounds (Steven Paston/PA) ( PA Wire )

Itauma rained down blows on Hrgovic for the first seven rounds but the wily 34-year-old was able to soak up the punishment and then took control in the eighth and ninth rounds.

Showing a granite chin and enormous heart, he won the exchanges as the rivals went toe to toe and Itauma lurched across the ring until Foster intervened.

The clash had been billed ‘Witness History’ in anticipation of Itauma being crowned Britain’s youngest ever world heavyweight champion, but his career has stalled and Warren was unable to guarantee he would be back.

“I don’t know what he’s going to say,” Warren said. “I’m sure he’s a fighting man. He showed that right to the end. At the end, that’s the type of fight it was – they were standing there just letting bombs go.

open image in gallery Itauma started well but tired (Steven Paston/PA) ( PA Wire )

“I don’t even know how he feels mentally. Mentally, he’s going to be completely down. We’re going to have to talk to him and lift him and see what he’s like.

“It’s going to take some time. He’s going to have a nice break. It’s not even the time to talk about it with him at the moment.

“It’s something we’re probably doing in two weeks or even a month’s time, see where we go with it.”

Hrgovic must now take on the IBF’s mandatory challenger Frank Sanchez, who was paid step aside money to enable him to face Itauma.

“I can’t believe it’s happening,” he said. My head is ringing from everything. It will take time for my feelings to settle. But I can’t believe that after 20 years I have my dream.

“God gave me the best possible gift to fight to win a world title against the best guy in the division. The most talented guy in the division. There is no better way for me to become a world champion.”
