Police say one person has died and five are wounded after a shooting at a rave party in Aarau in northern Switzerland.

The shooting happened shortly after 2.30am on Sunday at a horse racing track in Schachen, on the edge of the town, where a rave was being held.

Police wrote on X that one person was killed and five injured, some seriously, by a shooting at event in the canton's capital Aarau, 46km (29 miles) west of Zurich.

Police said a manhunt for the shooter was underway.

"Aarau: Nighttime shots at event in Schachen. Several victims. Major police operation underway. Stay away from the area. More info to follow," police said earlier in a post on X.

The police have urged the public to avoid the area, and asked people to share any videos or pictures they had captured of ​the ​incident.

The Aargau Cantonal Police said it had deployed to the scene "with a large contingent" and had begun its investigations.

open image in gallery Armed police officers patrol near the Schachen horse racing track in Aarau following a shooting during a rave event near Aarau, Switzerland ( AP )

"The manhunt for the unknown perpetrator is underway," police said. "Possible motives as well as the exact circumstances of the crime are still unclear."

The Aargau Cantonal Disaster Response Unit (KKE) and an army Super Puma helicopter were also deployed at the site, according to Blick.

"It is not yet clear what exactly happened," media spokesperson for the Aargau Cantonal Police, Vanessa Rumpold, told the newspaper. The police can currently only confirm "several shots being fired at a large group of people."

open image in gallery Police officers secure the area where a shooting occurred, in Aarau, northern Switzerland ( AFP/Getty )

Aarau's public swimming pool has been closed until further notice because of the ongoing operation, police said.

“Due to the ongoing major police operation, Aarau Swimming Pool will remain closed until further notice. Visitors are requested to stay away from Aarau Schachen,” the police said in another post on X.

open image in gallery Police officers patrol a street in downtown Aarau, Switzerland Sunday ( © KEYSTONE / MICHAEL BUHOLZER via AP )

The shots were fired on the sidelines of the "Aarauer Rave," an annual techno party that drew around 3,500 people to the Schachen racecourse between 3pm on Saturday and 2am on Sunday, according to Blick.

A reader told the newspaper they had heard "repeated shots," and a video obtained by the newspaper captured the sound of multiple gunshots at 2.35am. Another witness who was present said they initially thought the noise was fireworks, before hiding under the DJ booth.

It is unclear whether anyone has been apprehended in relation to the shooting.

open image in gallery Police officers secure the area behind a poster advertising a rave where a shooting occurred, in Aarau, northern ( AFP/Getty )

Switzerland has one of the highest rates of civilian gun ownership in Europe, with around 27 firearms for every 100 residents, behind only a small group of countries such as Finland, Austria and Norway. Despite this, violent shootings remain rare.

Much of the country’s gun culture stems from its militia-based military system, under which many men complete compulsory service, and a significant share of households have firearms linked to military or shooting club participation, although rules on keeping service weapons at home have been tightened over time.

In 2019, Swiss voters approved tighter gun control rules in a referendum, aligning the country’s firearms laws more closely with those of the European Union.

South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus has hit back at New Zealand counterpart Dave Rennie over claims that the Springboks are scrummaging illegally.

The hosts levelled the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series at 1-1 with a hard-fought win in the second Test in Cape Town, which came after a week of the two sides trading press conference barbs.

All Blacks boss Rennie had suggested that the world champions had been unfairly rewarded during a dominant scrummaging performance even in a 33-16 first Test defeat at Ellis Park, believing that they were walking around and failing to drive straight.

Saturday’s scrum-time action was protracted as referee Angus Gardner sought to repeatedly make clear his expectations to the two front rows, with a messy contest nonetheless resulting in few penalties.

And Erasmus believes that Rennie’s “moaning” had got into the heads of the officials – before picking out a few bugbears of his own.

“It’s the first time in history that people are talking about us walking around,” Erasmus insisted. “Why would we all of a sudden walk around? The first six scrums New Zealand had, every single one collapsed and it was reset, reset, reset. Why is it only on their ball that the scrum collapses every single time?

“So don’t come with that nonsense and saying we are walking around and trying to put things out in the media. The last lineout was skew. I’m not going to moan my arse off about that. If he’s going to start moaning about stuff like that, then they are under pressure.

open image in gallery The scrum has been a key battleground on and off the field ( Reuters )

“Last week we didn't moan when there was clearly a lot of head contacts. Today in the first 40 there were four head contacts and nothing was done about it, and then Lood [de Jager] gets the first one.

“Don’t try and convince people through the media. The first week they tried to convince people in the media we were slowing the game down – and we’re not. There is obviously a plan to get that message out. We’re not going to stay quiet and say, ‘ya, we’re walking around’. We’re not f****** walking around. We are scrumming through.

“We’re never ever been accused of walking around. I don’t understand it.”

Erasmus had tinkered with his line-up at the last moment at Cape Town Stadium, swapping his front rows with the trio of Gerhard Steenekamp, Deon Fourie and Thomas du Toit starting.

Steenekamp and Fourie were removed before half time with Ox Nche and Malcolm Marx – originally named to start – brought on and making a pivotal impact.

Despite defeat, Rennie was happier with the officiating at the set-piece.

open image in gallery Dave Rennie and Rassie Erasmus disagree on the scrum battle ( Reuters )

“The scrums were better tonight,” said Rennie. “I think Angus [Gardner] was pretty strong around setting a mark and trying to keep the hookers in the same sort of spacing. If the Springboks moved across further left, he stopped them.

“We’ll give a bit of feedback on that. It’s still a bit of an issue for us because they’re able to walk around and go straight through our tighthead. There are a couple of technical things we’ll share again. In the end both teams were able to play off the scrums and Angus did a reasonable job there.”

The series continues on Saturday as the two sides return to Johannesburg for the third Test at FNB Stadium. It will conclude in Baltimore on Saturday 12 September.

When Nadia Perrier’s phone flashed up with her mother-in-law’s number, she immediately sensed something was badly wrong.

At five months pregnant in May 2021, she was making a final trip before the birth to visit family in London before returning to Switzerland, where her husband, Michael, worked as a professional footballer. He was on a day out with his teammates and she hadn’t heard from him for hours, but she hadn’t been worried until that moment.

Picking up the phone, she heard his mother “screaming in terror” down the line: “I couldn’t understand what she was saying to me,” she said. “All I asked her was, ‘is he dead?’.”

Later, Ms Perrier learned that at 32 years old, her husband had suffered a sudden cardiac arrest while on a go-karting day out with his teammates. His foot had slipped onto the accelerator, causing him to crash into a wall before he was pulled from the vehicle and emergency services were called.

She was told that he was almost pronounced dead at the scene, unresponsive to the defibrillations given by medics, but that his desperate teammates had begged them to continue, telling them his wife was pregnant. Eventually, they saw a flicker in his throat - enough of a sign of hope to helicopter him to hospital in Lausanne, where he was put into an induced coma.

open image in gallery Michael Perrier was a fit and healthy professional footballer when he suffered a cardiac arrest ( Nadia Perrier )

“I think it’s probably the worst news you can ever hear when you’re pregnant,” she said. “I heard something to do with his heart, but I had to put the phone down because I felt like I was going to collapse. I was in a state of panic.”

Mr Perrier was given a fewer than three per cent chance of survival by doctors. But miraculously, he did survive - thanks to the life-saving actions of one of his teammates. After he had crashed his go-kart and before the paramedics arrived, one of his team members had pulled Mr Perrier from the car and began performing CPR. Without that knowledge, Ms Perrier said there is no chance her husband would have lived to meet his daughter.

open image in gallery Mr Perrier was rushed to hospital in Lausanne where he was put into an induced coma ( Nadia Perrier )

Not only that, but Mr Perrier survived without any significant brain damage or other health consequences. He now has a defibrillator fitted and is unable to play football, but otherwise lives a normal, healthy life in London, where the family now live.

“His life was saved because that one person knew how to perform CPR,” Ms Perrier said. “It’s genuinely a miracle what we’ve had, not just for him to survive, but him to be who he is. Okay, he can’t play football, but what is that compared to everything else?”

The Central London Alliance (CLA), of which Ms Perrier is the director, is now calling on businesses, schools, and communities across London to come together and take part in a life-saving world record attempt for a CPR relay.

Held over two days on 22 and 23 September, the relay hopes to recruit 4,000 participants from across London to gain CPR training and take part in the event. The Independent is proudly partnering with the event as its official media partner.

“You teach people these skills, and I am convinced people will have to use it at some point in their life,” Ms Perrier said. “My husband’s life was saved because that one person knew how to perform CPR.

open image in gallery Ms Perrier is now hoping to raise awareness and education through a record-breaking CPR relay ( Nadia Perrier )

“Look at that ripple effect of what one person has done for my family,” she added. “I could be in a very different position right now, bringing up my daughter alone as a single parent, and her not having a father from day one. We’re not in that position because one person knew it.”

“It is so vital because you’re not just saving someone’s life but you’re saving the condition of their life - the fact my husband knows who I am, could talk, could remember we were pregnant. It’s because of that that the function of his brain was protected.”

Anyone interested in taking part is asked to register for the event, that aims not only to make history, but to help save lives.

“We will teach you and give you the confidence to do it,” Ms Perrier said. “For me, we’ve had so many people help us through our journey and we want to help other people now. We want what we went through to stand for a good reason.”

Businesses, schools, community groups and individuals are all encouraged to register for the event, which takes place on 22 and 23 September at Tower Suites by Blue Orchid Hospitality in London.

News.content:

Tom Hardy has returned with his rap alias Frankie Pulitzer to deliver a new collaborative album, Czarface Meets Frankie Pulitzer, with the underground supergroup.

Czarface is made up of duo 7L & Esoteric and Wu-Tang Clan’s Inspectah Deck.

Fans in the know will already be aware of the Oscar-nominated British actor’s underground music career. In 2011 he spoke about recording “loads of stuff” that had never been released.

Well, now Hardy has surprised them by finally releasing his debut rap album, which features plenty of references to films and comic books – as well as an X-rated reference to Hollywood veteran Kathy Bates.

On “Raw Forever”, Hardy namechecks Martin Scorsese’s 1999 movie Bringing Out the Dead, along with Willem Dafoe’s depiction of the Green Goblin in 2002’s Spider-Man.

Meanwhile, on “Mad Technology” – also featuring Wu-Tang’s Method Man – he references Stephen King film adaptations Cujo and Misery, sandwiching them around his NSFW Bates mention.

open image in gallery Tom Hardy raps about Martin Scorsese, Marvel comics and Kathy Bates on his new album ( AFP/Getty )

“You s***-for-brain no-name lame, that bites like Cujo,” he raps. “I’d rather masturbate to Kathy Bates than hear you flow/ And you know that Misery, it loves company.”

Bates won the Oscar for Best Actress when she starred in the iconic 1990 film Misery, directed by the late Rob Reiner and based on King’s 1987 novel, as obsessive fan Annie Wilkes who holds famed novelist Paul Sheldon (James Caan) captive.

open image in gallery Kathy Bates as the psychotic nurse Annie Wilkes opposite James Caan as Paul Sheldon in Rob Reiner's 'Misery' ( Getty Images )

The Independent has contacted Bates’s representative for comment.

Other collaborators on the project include Run the Jewels’s LP on “Dragon Cannon”, Kendra Morris on “Frankie”, and Busta Rhymes on “Raw Forever”.

Hardy deploys his voice-acting skills across the record, sounding a little like his character Eddie Brock from Marvel’s Venom franchise as he raps: “I eat people, break ribs, throw bodies off the Golden Gate bridge/ And I get it how I live like a cannibal/ I talk sick, toxic, highly flammable.”

Meanwhile, on “Grim-Visaged War”, fans will be reminded of his famous performance as Bane from Christopher Nolan’s Batman film, The Dark Knight Rises, as he recites Shakespeare’s Richard III monologue.

Hardy has not spoken publicly about his work as Frankie Pulitzer, but has appeared on previous Czarface albums and also released standalone singles.

In 1999, he recorded and released a mixtape titled Falling On Your Arse, which resurfaced on Reddit back in 2018.

Speaking to the BBC in 2011, Hardy commented: “I used to be [signed] with the guy who managed Leela James and Lauryn Hill, Pras, the Fugees and all that. I worked out with [Grammy-winning producers] Warren Riker and Gordon Williams. I’ve recorded loads of stuff but it’s never been released.”

So far, the fan reaction to Czarface Meets Frankie Pulitzer has been hugely positive. Is there a Grammy nomination on Hardy’s horizon?

Richard Osman’s hugely popular The Thursday Murder Club books have made him one of the UK’s best-selling fiction authors – but despite a starry cast, Netflix’s attempt at adapting the first novel in the series fell flat.

The former Pointless star has now addressed the disappointment, admitting: “I can’t really talk about the film very much.”

“Let’s not let it detain us,” he tells The Times. The publication adds that “when pressed”, the 55-year-old continued: “It was only one book. The other books I would like to adapt myself.”

With Harry Potter director Chris Columbus at the helm, and the central quartet of cold case-obsessed retirees played by Dame Helen Mirren, Pierce Brosnan, Sir Ben Kingsley and Celia Imrie, The Thursday Murder Club debuted on the streaming platform and in selected cinemas last year.

The film was written by comedian Katy Brand and screenwriter Suzanne Heathcote, whose credits include Killing Eve and Fear The Walking Dead.

The film controversially deviated significantly from the source material, most notably altering the trajectory of the much-loved Polish handyman Bogdan (played by Henry Lloyd-Hughes), and completely removing a number of other popular characters.

open image in gallery Osman with the film’s four stars and director ( Ian West/PA Wire )

Unfortunately, the adaptation was met with lukewarm reviews, with The Independent’s critic Clarisse Loughrey awarding it a dismal two stars.

“The whole affair is so flimsy you’ll lose nothing from watching it on an iPad while cooking dinner,” she wrote.

The Thursday Murder Club initially performed well on Netflix – with the streaming service claiming it had 24.7 million views in its first four days – but the film failed to top the global most-watched chart, and dropped to fifth on Netflix’s most-watched film chart within a week of debuting.

And Osman has insisted he enjoyed working on the project, telling The Times it was “a lot of fun meeting [producer Steven] Spielberg, Helen, Pierce and everyone else. Really cool.”

While a number of the cast members have said they’d love to return, a sequel is still yet to be confirmed.

open image in gallery Osman has said he would like to adapt future adaptations himself ( Getty )

The first Thursday Murder Club book was released in 2020 and according to publisher Penguin, almost 700,000 copies were sold in the first four months in the UK alone.

Another four books in the series have followed and Osman has so far sold more than 17 million books worldwide – making him the UK’s second most-popular author, beaten only by children’s author Julia Donaldson.

Osman, who recently stepped away from House of Games, last year debuted the first in a new series, We Solve Murders, which will be followed by We Chase Shadows next month.

News.title: Moses Itauma lifted out of ring after losing IBF title bout to Filip Hrgovic
News.content:
The 34-year-old Hrgovic had gone into the fight as the underdog, with Itauma heavily fancied after a precocious early career. Had the Briton won, he would have maintained his undefeated record and become the second-youngest world heavyweight champion in boxing.

Itauma, 21, is famous for his early stoppages. He had never previously gone past six rounds in the ring, and he raced out of his corner for the first two rounds in pursuit of victory.

The youngster dominated the early exchanges and forced a standing count for Hrgovic as his opponent stumbled after a heavy blow, with the referee intervening. At that point it looked as if he would become just another of Itauma’s victims.

However, the older man proved the value of his chin as he took plenty of jabs and hooks to the face, but only rarely looked rattled. Occasionally, he sent some of his own jabs back in Itauma’s direction, but for most of the fight he looked to be holding on, just in case something happened to rescue him.

Salvation eventually came, as it became suddenly clear that Itauma simply was not conditioned for a fight that would go the distance. In round eight, the two traded blows and looked totally spent.

They both took their minute to rest, but it was Hrgovic who sucked the most oxygen into his lungs. The Croatian punished Itauma from the opening seconds and it became evident that the Briton did not have the energy to remain upright and competently defend himself. While he bravely attempted a few more wild swings, he bounced off the ropes worryingly and the referee stepped in to bring the fight to a close.

News.title: £380m = zero points: Big-spending Spurs humbled by Newcastle
News.content:
“After the first goal we lost confidence,” said De Zerbi. “The reaction was not good enough, not what I want to see on the pitch. The solution is not to put the head down, but to react.”

To be clear, Spurs were not quite as bad as they had been against Brentford on the opening day. They did create chances here, taking 17 shots and forcing a few terrific saves from Lukas Hornicek, Newcastle’s impressive goalkeeper. But in the key moments they suffered from the same absence of clarity and execution as they did last season. Troublingly, this seemed to affect the new signings as much as it did the longer-serving players.

Of the five new arrivals who featured for Spurs, Tonali was the least effective. The Italian had been vigorously booed by the away fans before kick-off and the travelling Geordies waited with palpable excitement for his first mistake. Much to their delight, it arrived after only three minutes: an underhit pass, in his own half, which directly led to Micky van de Ven picking up a yellow card. Tonali was outshone by new Newcastle midfielder Nico Gonzalez, who excelled only a few days after completing his move from Manchester City.

News.title: Lawrence seizes his opportunity on rain-ruined day at Lord’s
News.content:
On a bleak day for batting, Dan Lawrence seized an opportunity that he must have feared had passed him by.

Lawrence was one of the victims of Bazball excess, shoved up to open in place of Zak Crawley two years ago in a punt that backfired and could have ended his Test career.

It took the sudden retirement of Ben Stokes and an injury to first-choice replacement Sam Curran to open up a position at No 6, Lawrence’s natural home, and it has come at just the right time.

At 29 he is a much more rounded cricketer than the one who debuted in Sri Lanka under Joe Root in 2021 and he showed it here with a hard-fought half-century on a gloomy, dank Saturday when only 25 overs were possible between the frequent drizzly showers, forcing MCC into a 50 per cent ticket refund.

It was a second fifty in three innings since his recall and he will not have faced many tougher conditions than this, with the ball seaming around on a spiteful pitch. With Mohammad Abbas teasing the ball off the surface and the athletic Mohammad Rizwan snaffling everything up to the stumps, this was a real challenge of mind and technique.

Lawrence will never win awards for aesthetic beauty but he chose the right balls to put away in a 66-ball unbeaten 50 that stretched England’s lead to 357 at 177 for seven in their second innings. Lawrence settled any wobbles about Pakistan pulling off a miracle recovery.

News.title: Springboks level Greatest Rivalry series with blood-and-thunder victory over All Blacks
News.content:
South Africa aim to bounce back from losing the first game of the Greatest Rivalry Tour as they take on New Zealand in game two from Cape Town. The All Blacks claimed an impressive 33-16 win in game on in Johannesburg last weekend, outscoring South Africa five tries to one. That victory takes New Zealand above South Africa in the world rankings into top spot.

The Springboks know that a defeat today will mean they cannot win the series. They have not lost two consecutive Tests since November 2022. Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu has been given the nod to start at fly-half but Handre Pollard has pulled out of the matchday squad due to a calf injury.

“There were a handful of positives and negatives last week, but the main thing that let us down was that we created so many chances, but mistakes at crucial times cost us,” South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus said.

“We will put in a lot of work this week to ensure that we are sharp in that regard this weekend because if we had used even some of those chances, the result could have been completely different. That said, we know New Zealand will be charged up after winning last week, and they will want to build on that. But the key for us will be to focus on our game and ensure that we are as effective as possible all around.”

News.title: Iraola fumes at bungling fourth official for costing Liverpool a penalty
News.content:
He did know, though, why Liverpool had needed to drag themselves off the deck again for the second week in a row. Iraola has shown in his opening weeks on Merseyside that he is not someone who seeks excuses.

“A lack of intensity hurt us,” Iraola said with obvious disdain and it was only down to a show of character in the second period that a slovenly first half did not enable Forest to win at Anfield for the third consecutive year, for all that the travelling fans thought it was “happening again!”

Forest, bruised after two defeats in four days to Leeds, looked like an Oliver Glasner side. They were aggressive and well organised, the only failing was that physically they could not see the job through, but the Austrian insisted that will change in due course.

Once Glasner is settled in and he gets his transfer business done – “definitely one, possibly two and probably three,” was his mischievous reply to how the window will unfold – Forest will be a formidable proposition, especially if the first 45 minutes are a barometer.

They had been knocking on the door before Dan Ndoye eventually broke the deadlock, sweeping a left-footed drive past Alisson after Igor Jesus had won a header from a long clearance. It was a simple goal, marginally onside, but it was absolutely deserved.

News.title: Cherki magic helping Maresca to step out of Guardiola shadow
News.content:
Rumours of Manchester City’s supposed demise without Pep Guardiola appear to be much exaggerated.

They swept past Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park with a style of play under new manager Enzo Maresca that was just as swashbuckling as under his predecessor, with Rayan Cherki playing the role of chief architect. The Frenchman’s two goals included a captivating mazy dribble, which will long be remembered by those who had the fortune to see it.

City created enough space for themselves through clever movement. With Cherki zigging one way and Phil Foden zagging the other, they created even more by dribbling past a mesmerised Palace back three that became a back five at times and still could not cope.

Erling Haaland also scored twice. Even with the creative and unpredictable talents of those behind in a four-man attacking City midfield, Haaland remains irreplaceable with his ability to convert chances.

However, this night belonged to Cherki. Guardiola chided him publicly after he set up a City goal with a “rabona” cross last season. The thrust of Guardiola’s comments were that Cherki was not Lionel Messi. Of course not, but he possesses a genius all of his own, which Maresca would surely be foolish to rein in.

The jaw-dropping splendour of Cherki’s first goal drew a collective intake of breath at Selhurst Park.

Collecting a Foden pass, he attacked the Palace area on a diagonal path, slaloming between Jaydee Canvot, Takehiro Tomiyasu and Chris Richards, before having the spatial awareness and technique to flick his left foot at the ball to send it rolling on a perpendicular trajectory past Dean Henderson.

News.title: England light years ahead of lamentable Pakistan
News.content:
Who needs Ben Stokes? Actually, it is hard to think of any side that would need him against this Pakistan team.

After just five days of cricket, and despite their own limitations with the bat, England are on the cusp of a series victory at Lord’s with a 261-run lead and power to add thanks to the prowess of a seam attack that has emerged quickly from the shadow of its former captain.

It will take longer to feel the full effects of Stokes’s absence. When England need a spinner in the side, they will miss the seam-bowling all-rounder to balance the XI. There will be times when they are up against it on a flat deck on a boiling day and be desperate for Stokes’s sheer will to win. It is still hard to think he will not play some part in the Ashes next summer.

For the final two years of his career it was Stokes’s bowling that was top class, his batting having become ordinary. But with bowlers of the quality of Ollie Robinson, Jofra Archer, Josh Tongue and Gus Atkinson gelling, England are more than making up for Stokes’s retirement. This bowling attack against Pakistan’s batting was a complete mismatch.

Joe Root has stepped into Stokes’s shoes confidently, laying down the law off the field and tactically he has been spot on, although Pakistan have hardly stretched him. The only stir they have made since arriving was the stink they kicked up over Sky Sports’ interview with Imran Khan’s sons.

Conclusions are impossible to draw with any confidence against such poor opponents. Sri Lanka and West Indies two years ago put up a stronger fight in the first two Tests of their series. Tamim Iqbal scored two hundreds as Bangladesh at least landed some blows in 2010. Pakistan have managed one fifty in three innings and were bowled out for 171 and 135 at Headingley and a lamentable 110 here.

They were a batsman down at Lord’s because of a calf injury to opener Imam-ul-Haq, but only reached three figures because England dropped top scorer Azan Awais on eight; he went on to score 46.

England’s batting is hardly firing, but with a 180 first-innings lead, they could afford to be 13 for two without panic spreading. Losing Root for 24 kept Pakistan interested, but Emilio Gay toughed it out in the gloom to reach stumps unbeaten on 30; England 81 for three, light years ahead in the game.

Robinson’s astonishing figures of 13-6-11-4 set him on the way for a probable third man-of-the-match award in a row and continued his unexpected resurgence. Rarely did his pace go above 78mph, he just landed the ball time and again on a length and let movement off the seam do the rest.

News.title: I’ve lived in Norfolk for more than 30 years. Here’s how to explore England’s windswept east
News.content:
Norfolk’s vast sandy beaches are its chief draw for visitors: even on the busiest summer day there is always space for games, kite-flying or a family picnic in the dunes. Boating, crabbing, digging for cockles and wading in creeks provides hours of entertainment for all.

But there’s much more to Norfolk’s coast than its beaches. It’s also a landscape of dense pine forest and large expanses of salt marsh, which flush purple with sea-lavender in August. Birdlife is astonishingly rich, and wildflowers include yellow-horned poppies and lilac-flowering sea pea.

Inland, the undulating countryside and sleepy flint-built villages are perfect for gentle cycling, walking or touring by car. Grand stately homes make enjoyable days out, and almost every village has a sublimely beautiful medieval church at its centre.

Lively Georgian towns such as Burnham Market and Holt offer quirky shopping – and, wherever you are, you’re never far from an atmospheric pamment-floored pub serving local ales, or an excellent delicatessen selling the region’s specialities. Look out for pungent cheeses, smoked fish and salt-marsh flavoured honey.

Sports.title: Transfer news: Cody Gakpo twist, Bradley Barcola latest, Man Utd agree Arsenal deal
Sports.content:
The latest transfer news from the Premier League and further afield, including updates on Arsenal, Manchester United, Liverpool, Tottenham Hotspur and many more

Welcome to Mirror Football's transfer blog for Saturday, August 29.

Bradley Barcola's seemingly imminent transfer from Paris Saint-Germain to Liverpool has continued to dominate the headlines, as one of the most exciting sagas of the summer is set to come to an end. It is claimed that an agreement has been reached between the two clubs, and that the Reds will pay a total of £123million for the 23-year-old winger.

That's broken down into a guaranteed £106m, as well as £17m in add-ons. A move to Anfield is expected to be formalised in the coming days. Barcola isn't the only talent that could bolster Andoni Iraola's first-team in the coming days, however.

The Reds are also reportedly setting their sights on Crystal Palace's Ismaila Sarr, with Nicolo Schira claiming that an agreement in principle over a contract running to 2031 has been met between Liverpool and the player. A new bid is expected to come, after Palace rebuffed an initial offer of around £51m.

In the English capital, meanwhile, Arsenal are still chasing Julian Alvarez's signature, with his future with Atletico Madrid up in the air. The 26-year-old centre-forward has missed training thrice this week, albeit, citing illness as the reason for his absence, as the Gunners prepare to table a £130m bid to secure his signature.

Manchester United's search for a new left-back also runs on, having seemingly ditched their pursuit of Lews Hall as a result of Newcastle United refusing to sell the 21-year-old. While Alejandro Balde was considered an ideal candidate, the 22-year-old has now told Hansi Flick that he wants to fight for his place at Barcelona.

Stay tuned as we bring you all of the latest news in our transfer blog below...

Sports.title: Man Utd hero Roy Keane offered Ipswich fan out in car park and threatened to end star's career
Sports.content:
Man Utd hero Roy Keane offered Ipswich fan out in car park and threatened to end star's career

Roy Keane's time in the dugout with Ipswich Town produced fireworks

View 3 Images Roy Keane was in charge of Ipswich from April 2009 to January 2011 (Image: PA)

Roy Keane has had his fair share of heated moments involving Ipswich Town as the newly-promoted side play his former club Manchester United in the Premier League on Sunday afternoon.

‌



The Tractor Boys, who Keane managed between 2009 and 2011, sealed automatic promotion back to the top flight at the first time of asking last season, having been relegated in the summer of 2025. They began their 2026/27 Premier League campaign with a dramatic 2-1 win against Sunderland at home, before sealing a 3-1 victory over Leicester in the second round of the Carabao Cup on Tuesday.

‌



United, meanwhile, suffered a painful 2-0 defeat at Hull City to kick off their league campaign last Saturday. And the sides' meeting is bound to stir up some old feelings for Keane, given the Irishman's affiliation with the clubs, having captained United for eight seasons as a midfield enforcer.

‌



After a glittering career, Keane hung up his boots in June 2006 as a 34-year-old at Celtic. It didn't take long for the hot-headed midfielder to return to football, beginning his first stint as a manager in charge of Sunderland just two months later.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Micah Richards has told Sky Sports and BBC of retirement plan with Roy Keane set to quit first READ MORE :

He guided them to promotion in the 2006/07 season, but resigned the following year, in December 2008. After that, the now Sky Sports pundit took charge of Ipswich in April 2009, where he spent just under two years as head coach in a largely forgettable stint that ended with his sacking following a run of seven defeats in nine league matches.

‌



During his time at Portman Road, the fiery manager clashed with several of his players. Such feuds, most notably with Pablo Counago and Jon Walters, continued long afterwards, and Keane's two former players later accused him of being a "complete mess as a football manager" and a "liar", respectively.

Another notable falling out involved then-Ipswich striker Kevin Lisbie. Lisbie shed light on his tense relationship with Keane on Undr The Cosh last year, saying he had tried to erase the Irishman's tenure at Portman Road from his memory as it was so difficult. Lisbie lifted the lid on some of the former Manchester United captain's wildest moments in his two-year stint, including a dressing room outburst targeted at other players.

He recalled: "We had a pre-season tour in Ireland, we lost 2-1, and he spent 40 minutes just hammering players. [He said to certain players] 'You're going to be working in McDonald's in a couple of weeks... I heard we turned down a £1million bid for you and I would've snapped their hand off for it now.'"

‌



View 3 Images Keane didn't like Kevin Lisbie (Image: Getty )

Lisbie revealed that, despite scoring in the match, Keane then took one look at him and berated him. He threatened never to play him again and to end his time at the club.

He explained: "I'd actually scored on that day, so I was sitting with a smile thinking he's got nothing to say about me, he's going to compliment me, but he just walked up to me and said, 'And I just don't like you. I just don't like your body language, and I just don't like anything about you. Yeah, yeah, you suck your teeth at me, you'll never play for me again'. We went back, and I never played for him again, so at least he was a man of his word! Literally that was it, and he just said, 'Try and find a club.'"

‌



Lisbie added that Keane only wanted to work with young players as he could influence their careers more than veterans, which he saw as a sign of the manager-turned-pundit's low self-esteem. "I don't think he was too interested in having senior pros, I think he much preferred to have the younger generation that he could mould. I don't know if it's an insecurity," he said.

"Ben Thatcher was there at the time, he tried to get Ben out, but he was retiring that year. Roy said to him he might as well leave, but Ben wanted to stay. He got him in at 6am everyday and he lived about two hours away. I remember when he told him he had to come in over Christmas. As we were walking out, there was a helicopter over our training ground. It lands on the ground, and Ben Thatcher runs out in his boots! And Roy Keane was just like [shaking his head]."

View 3 Images Keane clashed with Ipswich fans after Ipswich vs Manchester United two years ago (Image: X)

‌



Keane's history of heated exchanges at Ipswich did not end with his sacking as manager. The United hero over the past decade has become one of Sky Sports' most popular pundits, showing a warmer side while still offering no-nonsense analysis on TV. But the former Ireland international lost his cool while on punditry duty in November 2024, when he offered to fight a pitch-side fan during a fixture between United and Ipswich at Portman Road.

A home supporter goaded Keane from the stands, after which he approached the culprit during an advert break and told him that he would see him outside afterwards if he wanted to take their heated exchange any further.

Explaining what happened and why he was not looking for a fight, Keane later told the Stick To Football podcast: "I wasn't angry at the Ipswich Town game. What happens when we're doing matches is and the analysis is happening at the end of the match when fans can be up or down, whatever emotions they are feeling – and people think they can abuse you, and it seems to be a, 'We're supposed to accept that'.

Article continues below

"I went over to him twice – I said, 'No problem, if you want to abuse me or if you want a discussion with me, well I'm working'. I went over to him twice at different stages, and he was swearing in front of kids. I said, 'If you want to see me afterwards' – and people thought I was asking him for a [fight] – I said, 'I'll see you in the car park'. Where else was I going to see him? He wasn't there!"

Sports.title: Liverpool news: Bradley Barcola saving emerges as Reds 'plot' another transfer hijack
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Bradley Barcola saving emerges as Reds 'plot' another transfer hijack

Liverpool's imminent signing of Bradley Barcola may not be the last piece of business taking place at Anfield this summer

View 2 Images Liverpool are making a huge saving on Bradley Barcola despite the deal coming close to a British transfer record (Image: Aurelien Meunier - PSG/PSG via Getty Images)

Liverpool are finally set to get their way after agreeing a deal to sign Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain. The Frenchman is set to join for a fee that comes close to rivalling the British transfer record but there's more business to be done.

‌



The summer transfer window has been a slow-burner for Andoni Iraola's side despite a number of problem areas emerging. There's still some concern regarding a lack of defensive depth at Anfield despite the additions of Jeremy Jacquet and Ronald Araujo, while Mohamed Salah still hasn't been truly replaced.

‌



For all that, the majority of transfer rumours around Liverpool are situated largely in attack. Mirror Football brings you all the latest murmurs from around the club with a little more than 48 hours to go before Tuesday's deadline.

‌



FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Reds make big Barcola saving

As expensive as Barcola's signing may be on paper, fans will be heartened to know his arrival comes at a discount. The total cost of the transfer is reportedly made up of a £106million guaranteed payment, plus another £17m in add-ons.

Should Liverpool be spending £122m on Bradley Barcola transfer after Newcastle issues READ MORE :

That's a full £22m cheaper than PSG were originally seeking for their forward earlier this summer. Les Parisiens opened negotiations with a starting price point of £145m but were whittled down thanks in large part to their own business.

‌



Luis Enrique has added new creative weapons to his ranks this summer in the shape of Mika Godts and Maghnes Akliouche. Add to that the fact Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue already appeared ahead of him in the pecking order and it's easier to see why PSG have decided to cash in.

It's still an eye-watering sum for Liverpool to pay in the grand scheme of things. Many would even argue Barcola hasn't done enough in his career as of yet to justify such a massive expense.

‌



However, it won't be long before Reds fans see their shiny, new signing attempting to do just that at Anfield. And it will please those same supporters to know the board is at least doing all it can to save the pennies (read: millions) where they can.

Fernandez Pardo poach reported

View 2 Images Could Liverpool be set to beat Newcastle to the signing of Lille forward Matias Fernandez Pardo? (Image: Getty Images)

Liverpool could be set to hand Newcastle more misery in the transfer window after already snatching Victor Munoz from their sights. The Reds are now being touted to complete a move for Lille forward Matias Fernandez Pardo, who is reportedly valued at around £60m.

‌



Iraola's side have been linked with the Belgian already this summer, so it's hardly out of the blue, as was the case for Munoz. However, it could throw another late spanner in Newcastle's plans if they were to get beaten to the punch by Liverpool again.

TEAMtalk reported the Reds have already made contact with Lille regarding a late bid for their star. This comes after The Telegraph reported Newcastle were accelerating their own ambitions to recruit the youngster.

Fernandez-Pardo has operated largely as a striker for Lille and would presumably provide back-up behind Alexander Isak. However, he is also capable of working off either flank.

Article continues below

The 21-year-old would present a similar profile to Cody Gakpo and could be viewed as a replacement if the Dutchman leaves. He continues to be linked with Manchester City and Tottenham entering the final few days of the transfer window.

Sports.title: Man Utd news: Marcus Rashford transfer interest emerges as teammate told time at club is 'gone'
Sports.content:
Man Utd news: Marcus Rashford transfer interest emerges as teammate told time at club is 'gone'

Round-up as Manchester United look to complete their final pieces of business before the transfer deadline

View 3 Images Marcus Rashford could still be on the move before Tuesday (Image: Getty Images)

A mixed transfer window for Manchester United is drawing to a close, with a new left-back at the top of the club's wish-list. Michael Carrick's side have successfully recruited in midfield, with Carlos Baleba joining Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans through the door.

‌



However, there will be frustration if United don't strengthen in another area, specifically on the left side of defence. An alternative to Luke Shaw is needed, with the long-serving left-back in the final year of his contract.

‌



Lewis Hall is a long-time target but Newcastle have issued a strong hands-off warning. There are also calls for United to freshen up their attack.

‌



As for potential outgoings, speculation about Marcus Rashford's future continues to rage after he rejected a move to Fenerbahce. Ahead of United's first home match of the season against Ipswich Town, here's a round-up of the latest transfer news.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Rashford interest

Despite being reintegrated into the squad, talk of Rashford leaving refuses to go away. The latest link involves Arsenal, who have agreed to let Gabriel Martinelli join Al Hilal before Tuesday's deadline.

‌



According to the Independent , the Premier League champions are weighing up whether to launch a loan bid for the enigmatic forward. Whether United would sanction a third loan move for Rashford is unclear, but they could at least expect the Gunners to cover the bulk of his £325,000 per week wages.

A bigger priority for the Gunners is Atletico Madrid's wantaway striker, Julian Alvarez, whose dream move to Barcelona has been blocked by his club. Back to Rashford, and there has been surprise talk that Barcelona haven't completely ruled out re-signing him, despite not taking up the option to take him permanently after last season's loan. According to TeamTalk, Barca remain in contract with Rashford's camp.

View 3 Images Rashford is still attracting interest (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Time's up for Shaw

Patrice Evra has told United to sign a replacement for Shaw. Despite having plenty of respect for his fellow left-back, the Frenchman believes it is time to move on from the 30-year-old, whose Old Trafford career has been marred by injury.

Speaking on his Kick stream, Evra slammed Shaw's performance at Hull last weekend. He said: "What I'm really disappointed about is all the back passes in that game. Luke Shaw, I love you, but it's going to be a tough season for him.

"Why? He's been at the club for years, he's had a lot of injuries that killed his football career. When I talk with him, he's still traumatised by [the injuries], he wouldn't go 100 per cent into every challenge.

‌



View 3 Images United need to move on from Luke Shaw, according to Patrice Evra (Image: Getty Images)

"I have to tell the truth. Man United fans want to hear my opinion, and I think [Shaw's] time has gone. Don't get me wrong, he might have a great game next game, but I don't care. If Luke Shaw can give me a 35-game season, then that's a good season.

"I don't care if he has 10 good games and three bad ones, if he doesn't play at least 35 games in a row, Man United fans will go crazy. He's lucky because he's English. I love Luke Shaw, but I love Man United even more. That's why I'm saying they need another left-back."

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher shares Tottenham transfer theory during Newcastle defeat - 'The evidence'
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher shares Tottenham transfer theory during Newcastle defeat - 'The evidence'

Jamie Carragher has delivered his verdict on Tottenham Hotspur during Saturday's dismal 2-0 defeat at home to Newcastle United

View 2 Images Jamie Carragher delivered his verdict on Tottenham during the loss to Newcastle (Image: PA)

Jamie Carragher reckons Tottenham Hotspur are sufficiently short in attacking areas to push Roberto De Zerbi into further transfer activity. Spurs have splashed out considerably this summer and brought in Savio and Omar Marmoush from Manchester City in an attempt to bolster their forward line.

‌



Yet they failed to find the net in the opening 45 minutes of their first home fixture of the Premier League campaign against Newcastle United. Savio was absent, days after his goal and assist in the Carabao Cup victory over Charlton Athletic, due to muscle fatigue.

‌



Marmoush was given a start in the XI following his arrival on a temporary deal. Carragher felt Spurs' toothless attacking showing will prompt additional transfer moves before September 1.

‌



Ex-Premier League referee speaks out after Andoni Iraola rages at Liverpool controversy READ MORE :

Liverpool star Cody Gakpo selects next club as talks on to complete late transfer READ MORE :

He said: "They have been let down in the final third, I think it is probably the evidence that De Zerbi will still be in the market after this game, in the next few days, for attacking reinforcements.

"They have certainly been left a little bit short in this first half by the ability of the wide players to beat the man or do something clever or creative."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Spurs' summer signings were on show with Sandro Tonali and Matheus Fernandes starting alongside Marmoush. The clearest opportunity of the half came to Pedro Porro but his strike from 12 yards out sailed over the bar.

The opening exchanges were decidedly one-sided, with Spurs commanding the ball against the Magpies yet failing to convert their dominance into any meaningful attempts on Lukas Hornicek's goal.

View 2 Images New signing Sandro Tonali struggled against his former club Newcastle (Image: Getty Images)

‌



With the transfer deadline fast approaching, De Zerbi is eyeing further additions to his squad following a £300million spending spree this summer.

Ahead of the Newcastle fixture, he said: "I didn't expect a market like we have done. I think we can do one player more and in one specific position.

"Yesterday we went for dinner with the owner, with Vinai (Venkatesham, chief executive), with Johan (Lange, sporting director) and with Enrico (Venturelli). We spoke about this.

Sports.title: Ex-Premier League referee speaks out after Andoni Iraola rages at Liverpool controversy
Sports.content:
Ex-Premier League referee speaks out after Andoni Iraola rages at Liverpool controversy

Liverpool’s opening Premier League home game against Nottingham Forest was marred by controversy, with Reds boss Andoni Iraola left furious by the behaviour of the officials during the board

View 2 Images Andoni Iraola was left irritated with the fourth official at Anfield (Image: Getty Images)

Former Premier League referee Graham Scott has said that the substitutes' boards are ‘not fit for purpose’ after Andoni Iraola’s outburst. The Liverpool head coach was left furious after his side’s 2-2 draw with Nottingham Forest on Saturday.

‌



He suggested that the fourth official was taking too long to get the boards ready as he attempted to make a triple substitution just before Forest’s second goal.

‌



The Liverpool boss said: “Yes, I cannot explain because I don't have explanation. I wanted to make those three subs like three minutes before. And there have been two, three or four times I think the ball has gone out and I still don't know the reason why we haven't made the subs. I think definitely he was having some problems with the board or something.

‌



"[It] would have happened, definitely. You stop [the game] because you want to sub [but] it doesn't happen.

“The quick throw-in, because we are waiting for the subs, so if I ask for the sub, and I already asked and I complained even the previous time that the ball went out and everyone was - even the supporters, I think they were shouting - aware of the situation, but I don't know the reason why they haven't done it. And the penalty, I leave you to decide if it's a penalty or not.”

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Ex-Premier League referee Graham Scott has now issued his thoughts on the incident and claimed that the technology is now outdated, albeit Iraola’s own complaints might have been exaggerated.

Taking to X, he wrote: “The subs boards are not fit for purpose. Each number has to be entered manually, and they only count up one at a time. Entering number 38 on its own could take several seconds and there are six numbers to plug in here.

“Also, the sponsors’ advertising makes them heavy and unwieldy, which is why the 4th has them on the ground. In UEFA comps the clubs have to enter the numbers themselves, which means they can get the subs done quicker. The PL only did this during Covid.

‌



View 2 Images Graham Scott has offered his take on the controversy surrounding Liverpool's draw with Nottingham Forest (Image: Getty Images)

“The 4th official would have had to check and double check the names and numbers of all six players involved in the substitutions against the official team sheet in case the club has made an error, which happens frequently enough to make such checks necessary.

After a fan suggested it took not take three minutes to make a substitution, he replied: “It shouldn’t take three minutes, agreed. But we have no evidence that it did, only Iraola’s word for it. I’ve stood next to him many times and say there’s just a chance he’s exaggerating for effect and to deflect from his goalkeeper’s rash challenge. I could be wrong, obvs.”

Sports.title: Newcastle get last laugh vs rotten Spurs as Sandro Tonali flops vs former club - 5 talking points
Sports.content:
Newcastle get last laugh vs rotten Spurs as Sandro Tonali flops vs former club - 5 talking points

SPURS 0-2 NEWCASTLE: Matthias Jaissle has his first victory as Newcastle boss with the Magpies having put on a second-half show at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium

View 3 Images Yoane Wissa celebrates his first goal of the season (Image: Getty Images)

A rejuvenated Yoane Wissa helped Newcastle to a 2-0 win against Tottenham on Saturday afternoon.

‌



Spurs, aiming to recover from their opening-day defeat by Brentford, struggled once again against their North East opponents. And they found themselves 1-0 down just after the hour mark as Anthony Elanga scored with a lethal finish.

‌



Wissa then doubled Newcastle's lead with an acrobatic effort from a corner, leaving Spurs staring at back-to-back defeats at the start of the campaign and without a single goal.

‌



Newcastle in the meantime have had a positive start to life under new boss Matthias Jaissle.

Here are all of the talking points from the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Elanga again

After scoring in Newcastle's opening game of the season against Liverpool, Anthony Elanga was at it again in North London. The winger had twice threatened before he actually scored, having gone close early on, while he was also unfortunate not to scored having gone past Spurs goalkeeper Antonín Kinský.

But just after the hour mark, he did get his goal. Nico Gonzalez's brilliant crossfield ball was nodded down by Admir Dedic.

Elanga picked up the ball, span and then placed it with pinpoint precision into the bottom corner via the post. Having only scored three times last season, Elanga looks a good bet to beat that record this season.

‌



View 3 Images Anthony Elanga has two goals from as many games this season (Image: Getty Images)

Wicked Wissa

While Elanga faced severe criticism for his displays last season, the same could certainly be said of Yoane Wissa. The forward struggled in his debut campaign at St James' Park following a move from Brentford.

But he looks a player reborn this term. He was brilliant against Liverpool and now has his first goal of the season after hooking home acrobatically after Spurs failed to clear a corner.

‌



It might be early days but if Newcastle can get both Wissa and Elanga firing throughout the season, they could be in for a very promising year indeed.

Porro a problem

Not necessarily for Spurs, but Pedro Porro is a problem for opposition teams. The Spanish defender had a brilliant World Cup and looks set to be a major star for the North London side again.

He had two brilliant opportunities to open the scoring in the first-half, having had an effort blocked by Lewis Hall, while he also lifted a couple of efforts over the crossbar.

‌



Despite two defeats, Porro has been a bright spot for Tottenham.

Tonali's tough reception

It wasn't quite a baying St James' Park but Tottenham midfielder Sandro Tonali still received a less-than-welcoming response by supporters of his former club Newcastle. The £92.5m midfielder saw his every touch booed by those assembled in the away corner of the ground.

He was taken off in the 75th minute to loud cheers from Newcastle fans. While his reception will have left a bitter taste, the result might even more so.

‌



View 3 Images Tonali was making his first appearance against former club Newcastle (Image: Getty Images)

Spurs' poor home record continues

Roberto De Zerbi had yet to lose on home soil since being appointed as Tottenham boss. But he's not quite managed to escape their dreadful record at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

The North London side were woeful on their own patch last season, winning just three Premier League games in all. If this display is anything to go by, it could potentially be another season of pain for the home supporters - and that's simply not good enough given all of the money they have spent this summer.

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola makes honest admission on Liverpool transfers after Bradley Barcola question
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola makes honest admission on Liverpool transfers after Bradley Barcola question

Liverpool are poised to announce the £123million signing of Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain and manager Andoni Iraola will be relieved when the transfer window closes

View 2 Images Andoni Iraola hasn't enjoyed the transfer window (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

Andoni Iraola admitted he is looking forward to "working with certainties" once the summer transfer window is closed and Bradley Barcola is a Liverpool player.

‌



Liverpool have agreed a deal worth £123million for the Paris Saint-Germain attacker, who will undergo a medical this weekend. After a long saga, they have agreed to pay the French side an initial fee of £106m, plus a potential £17m in add-ons.

‌



Barcola will bolster Iraola's attacking options and join Jeremy Jacquet, Victor Munoz and Ronald Araujo as the new arrivals. Liverpool have begun the season with back-to-back 2-2 draws after they were held by Nottingham Forest at Anfield on Saturday and Iraola is looking forward to Tuesday's 11pm deadline.

‌



"We've been patient all summer and now we just have to wait," he told BBC Match of the Day when asked about Barcola post-match. "We just have to wait a couple more days and see how we finish and how the squad looks in the second half of September.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"Honestly, I am looking forward to having who we have and a definitive squad so we can start working with certainties."

Munoz's late strike earned Liverpool a point against Forest after Morgan Gibbs-White's penalty, Dan Ndoye's low finish and Alexander Isak's tap-in. The Reds have been far from solid in their opening two matches and still have a few days to recruit more players.

Asked in the post-match press conference whether there would be further additions before the transfer deadline, Iraola said: "I cannot tell you anything different right now. It's true that there are things going on, like is normal because we are talking about the last weeks of the market, but now we have to wait.

‌



View 2 Images Liverpool are on the verge of signing Bradley Barcola (Image: Getty Images)

"I'm looking forward to having the squad [on] September 2, [so we can say] this is who we are and working with certainties. Now everything is quite like uncertain and it's the same for every team, but it's how the competition works. Now we have to wait just some [more] days and work with what we have after the market closes."

Pressed further on his squad, Iraola said: "We are talking now about the hypothesis because we don't know what's going to be the squad on September 2. I think every analysis that I can make is when I know and when everything finishes, when I know who's going to be here all the season or at least until January.

‌



"So now, we've waited all the summer, so we have to wait two, three more days, analyse and see what we have when the market closes."

Liverpool legend Steven Gerrard is excited by the arrival of Barcola. "Incredible talent," he said on TNT Sports. "This is a player who has won two Champions Leagues in the last two years. I don't think he's hit his ceiling yet, still think there's potential there.

"Growth. He can evolve into an even better player which is very exciting. But it's the type of level of player that's going to help take Liverpool to the next level. So I think it's a fantastic deal."

Sports.title: US Open key questions: Is Alcaraz fit? Will Sabalenka make history?
Sports.content:
The US Open, of all the four slams, is notoriously the hardest to predict the winners of as it falls at a time of year when eight months into the season the players are more likely than not nursing aches and pains with their bodies battered from the grind of the tour.

It's also played on a surface where more players fancy their chances; many have love-hate relationships with clay and grass but hard courts are their bread and butter.

The US Open is now a three-week event, week one is fan week, which this year saw five-time champion Roger Federer return for an exhibition, Karolina Muchova and Jakub Mensik win their first Grand Slam title after being crowned mixed doubles champions - in a competition that saw a return to Flushing Meadows of six-time champion Serena Williams - and the qualifying competition, which started with 15 Brits in the draw.

The main draw starts on Sunday and contains nine Brits, with a record five coming through qualifying. The men's competition is headed up by Sascha Zverev in the absence of Jannik Sinner [knee injury] and the women's by world No 1 Aryna Sabalenka.

In terms of questions to be asked, there are five main ones...

How will the wrist of returning champion Carlos Alcaraz hold up under the pressure of best-of-five-set Grand Slam play? Will 39-year-old Novak Djokovic finally get his hands on Grand Slam title No 25? Can an American finally win the men's title in New York? The last to do it was Andy Roddick in 2003. Can Aryna Sabalenka make history and win the US Open title for a third consecutive year? It's something that hasn't been done since Serena Williams in 2012-14. And maybe more importantly... who will end the tournament as world No 1, with four players in the running?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Alexander Zverev heads into the US Open having lost to Tommy Paul at the Cincinnati Open

If we break down the draws starting with the men, the top half is headed up in the absence of Sinner by Zverev, top seed at a Grand Slam for the first time and with a major title under his belt having won the French Open earlier this year.

The draw has been kind to the German, who will fancy his chances and comes into the tournament with an 18-2 record at Grand Slam level this year.

The question, as always, is how will he cope with the pressure having fallen early in both Masters 1000 events in the lead-up as the top seed.

Working from top to bottom, the second quarter is headed up by the Australian and sixth seed Alex de Minaur, projected to meet Zverev in the quarter-finals. He might not have Djokovic or Alcaraz in his section but he does have former finalist Taylor Fritz, French Open finalist Flavio Cobolli and last year's semi-finalist Felix Auger-Aliassime.

The bottom half is absolutely stacked and features all five former US Open champions in Alcaraz, Djokovic, Daniil Medvedev, Stan Wawrinka and Marin Cilic.

Working our way down next up is Djokovic's quarter, which features Medvedev, finalist in Cincinnati Francis Tiafoe, finalist in Canada Brandon Nakashima, and a second-round meeting with one of Wawrinka or Matteo Berrettini. That's before any talk of a meeting with Alcaraz - the defending champion who heads up the final quarter.

The seeds in the Alcaraz section include winner in Canada, Ben Shelton, winner in Cincinnati, Arthur Fils, Alexander Bublik, Tommy Paul and big-hitting Roman Safiullin, who has beaten him before and is, for me, one of his toughest tests for the Spaniard having not played a singles match since April.

Into the women's draw with each quarter containing very different stories...

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the US Open final between Aryna Sabalenka and Amanda Anisimova in 2025

The main story involving Sabalenka in the first quarter who is not only looking to try and become the first woman since Serena Williams to win three consecutive US Open titles but she's also trying to hold on to the world No 1 ranking.

On paper her draw isn't too bad until the quarter-finals, where she could face Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova.

The worry is Sabalenka's lack of form going 17-7 since April and not having won a title since March. She is without a Grand Slam title so far in 2026 and is looking vulnerable.

The second quarter is headlined by Jessica Pegula who is in contention to end the tournament as world No 1. For that to happen, the former finalist would need to win the title; nothing less would do.

Dangers lie around every corner for Pegula with Elina Svitolina, Karolina Muchova and Sorana Cirstea in her section and a second-round meeting with one of former Australian Open Champion Sofia Kenin or two-time US Open Champion Venus Williams.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Cincinnati Open final between Coco Gauff and Jessica Pegula

Former US Open champion and current Cincinnati champion Coco Gauff heads up the top of the bottom half; she also has a chance of reaching world No 1, but only if she wins the title.

Lying in wait for her in the third quarter are last year's finalist Amanda Anisimova, French Open Champion Mirra Andreeva, Washington champion Alex Eala, and a potentially tricky early meeting with Paula Badosa.

And finally, to what surely is the toughest quarter of the draw with Elena Rybakina, Iga Swaitek, Naomi Osaka, Madison Keys and Belinda Bencic.

Rybakina will be the new world No 1 if she reaches the semi-finals, that is in her hands. What isn't is the left ankle/Achilles injury that she has been managing for a while, but flared up in Cincinnati forcing her to withdraw in her match against Swiatek. She has looked tentative in practice, so only time will tell if it will hold up to allow her to reach world No 1 for the first time in her career.

What about British interest?

Image: Arthur Fery lost in the Winston-Salem Open final on Saturday

When it comes to the Brits, a word on Arthur Fery, who in his second tournament since reaching the semi-finals of Wimbledon this summer, reached the final of Winston-Salem - losing out to third seed Ignacio Buse in the title decider.

Perfect preparation for Fery who has had a whirlwind summer and now heads to New York as the British No 1 thanks to that run.

The Brit will be making his debut at the US Open and it's a tough one up against 13th seed Lorenzo Musetti.

Musetti recently found some form in Cincinnati but isn't long back from a back injury, so Fery will fancy his chances.

Fery sits in the top quarter draw with top seed Zverev. Also in that section is Jan Choinski, who takes on the Dutchman Botic Van De Zandschulp.

And the other Brit to qualify on ranking is Cameron Norrie, who is in the bottom half with Alcaraz. He is the 29th seed and faces the Frenchman Luca van Assche, for the right to take on Miomir Kecmanovic or Dennis Shapovalov in round two.

In total, there are nine Brits in the main draw and for the first time at the US Open five having come through qualifying.

Among them is Toby Samuel, the world No 110, who will make his US Open main draw debut, with the 23-year-old having drawn the Czech Tomas Machac, the world No 58.

Harry Wendleken is also set for his debut after playing nine sets and nine hours to reach the main draw, and his reward is the 21st seed Luciano Darderi. Jacob Fearnley, in as a lucky loser for his second US Open appearance, will take on the Spaniard Martin Landaluce.

Image: Katie Boulter faces American wild card Carol Young Suh Lee

In the women's draw, Katie Boulter was the only direct entrant and has been handed a good first round up against the American wild card Carol Young Suh Lee.

Lee is 24, sitting at her career-high ranking of 140, and will be making her Grand Slam main draw debut.

Should Boulter win, then more than likely she will face US Open mixed doubles champion and Wimbledon finalist Karolina Muchova in round two.

Joining Boulter through the qualifying route is Harriet Dart, who beat Heather Watson in the final round to set up a meeting with the American and world No 54 Peyton Stearns, who she recently played and lost to in Cincinnati, but did beat the American in US Open qualifying in 2021.

And Fran Jones, who for a second year running has secured qualification into the main draw where she will face Magda Linette of Poland in what will be a first meeting between the two.

Serena will return...

Also a reminder that we haven't seen the last of Serena Williams at the US Open this year.

Sports.title: Norris: I can be forceful to get what I want at McLaren
Sports.content:
Reigning world champion Lando Norris says he is in a position at McLaren where he "can be forceful to try to get what I want" after signing a contract extension with the team.

Norris claimed his maiden title in 2025 to become McLaren's first world championship winner since Lewis Hamilton triumphed for them in 2008.

Having emerged victorious in an intense season-long title battle with his team-mate Oscar Piastri, Norris has further enhanced his status within the Woking squad by clearly outperforming the Australian so far in 2026.

The 26-year-old Brit's position at the centre of the team's future was cemented on Saturday when he signed a contract extension to stay with McLaren until at least the end of 2030, with a multi-year option to potentially extend further beyond that included in the deal.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch Norris' roller-coaster season so far, which has seen several DNFs and race wins, putting him in the mix to challenge for the title

Asked during an exclusive interview with Sky Sports News about how his role within the team has changed over time, Norris said: "You learn over the years when you should talk, when you shouldn't.

"In terms of how much power you have as the driver and as an individual, in the first few years, you're not going to overstep any mark. I'm certainly not going to raise my voice above someone else, kind of thing.

"With time, you learn that my role is not simply just driving the car. It's also how can I be a leader, how can I lead the team, how can I be a voice for all the people that work here, all the guys and girls? How can I push them to do better, to be better? As well as pushing myself, of course. And how can we all work and do that as a team?"

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The moment Norris became F1 2025 World Champion!

Norris is driving his eighth season for McLaren, having been given his F1 debut by the team as a 19-year-old in 2019. His 163 Grand Prix starts are a team record, with Norris having surpassed fellow Brit David Coulthard's mark of 150 at last year's Qatar Grand Prix.

He continued: "I've just learned the power that I can have and influence I can have over directions that we work in as a team. Of course, I never want to abuse that, but at the same time, I know that I'm in a position where I can be forceful to try and get what I want, from a car, from the team, from people around me.

"And that's a very important thing. You've got to utilise that, I think, as an athlete, no matter what sport you're in. You've got to know how to try and get what you want as an individual.

"And I feel like I'm in a very good place right now with the people I have around me, my team, people we have in different positions, team leaders, all of those things, and the work ethic of the whole team, which is really the most important thing at the end of the day."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player An emotional Norris looks back at his career up until his World title win in Abu Dhabi

'I'm in a similar situation to Verstappen last year'

A poor start to the season for McLaren appeared to have blown Norris' hopes of defending his title, but upgrades to the MCL40 have enabled him to win the last two races in Hungary and the Netherlands.

Norris' latest victory in Zandvoort reduced his deficit to championship leader Kimi Antonelli to 83 points with 11 rounds remaining. Norris, who is fourth in the standings, must also leapfrog Antonelli's Mercedes team-mate George Russell and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton, who both trail the Italian by 59 points.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Norris hunted down Kimi Antonelli and Lewis Hamilton to take the race lead at the Dutch Grand Prix

Comparisons have been made to last year's championship, when Piastri led Norris by 34 points and Red Bull's Max Verstappen by 104 points with nine rounds remaining, before losing form.

Norris ultimately won the title by two points from Verstappen, with Piastri finishing 13 points behind his team-mate.

Asked whether he can take anything from Verstappen's fightback last year, Norris said: "Just the fact that it's possible. Just the fact to keep believing, keep working hard, keep motivating the team in all the right ways. That's the biggest thing.

"He didn't do anything better than we were doing, apart from the fact we made some mistakes as a team in certain places."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on the Sky Sports F1 Show podcast, Bernie Collins believes Norris is still in the title fight after his recent improvement with two back-to-back wins

Norris, who is currently 55 points ahead of seventh-placed Piastri, also perhaps hinted that he expects the team to prioritise him over his team-mate for the remainder of the season.

He continued: "There wasn't anything that we were doing wrong at the time. We just had two drivers fighting for our championship. They just had one.

"It's kind of a similar situation to what Mercedes are in now versus where I am.

"So, there's not a lot, I would say, to take from it, apart from just keep believing that it's possible until it's not. And that's the attitude we're going to fight with."

Sports.title: Today on Sky Sports Racing: British raiders on show at Deauville
Sports.content:
There is plenty of British interest on a quality card at Deauville this Sunday, all live on Sky Sports Racing.

2.50 Deauville - Al Aasy, Mazzala and Arrow Eagle seek Group 2 honours

There's an open feel to this Group 2 Grand Prix de Deauville as Al Aasy takes on Arrow Eagle.

Al Aasy, William Haggas' veteran nine-year-old, has racked up 12 career wins in a fantastic career stretching back to 2019. He continues to show his enthusiasm for the game, winning at Beverley in July and running a solid third at Goodwood so deserves to step up in class again.

Arrow Eagle represents the soon-to-retire Jean-Claude Rouget and carries the privilege of being his last Group 1 winner, taking the Royal-Oak last year. He might find this easier after being slightly disappointing when weakening in the Prix Vicomtesse Vigier.

Mazzala arrives unbeaten in four starts and having claimed Listed and Group 3 events on his last two starts he is a huge danger for Yann Barberot.

3.25 Deauville - British raiders Into The Sky and Mitbaahy clash

Image: Jim Boyle trains the well-fancied Into The Sky

British pair Into The Sky & Mitbaahy clash in a terrific edition of the Group 3 Prix de Meautry at Deauville.

Jim Boyle's stable star Into The Sky made a sparkling return this spring when fourth behind Bow Eacho in the 2000 Guineas but could not back that up at Royal Ascot. That defeat was over seven furlongs and he merits respect as he dips in class and trip under top pilot Pierre-Charles Boudot.

Mitbaahy is a solid operator at this sort of level and produced an excellent display to chase home Symbol Of Honour at Newbury on his penultimate run. A neck third in the Stewards Cup next time was another great performance and a repeat would put him in the mix.

Others to consider include fellow UK runners La Brodeuse and Zoum Zoum.

2.55 Yarmouth - Adrestia & Hypnotised among 9 runners

The feature at Yarmouth, the Bodhi Solutions - Exceeding Expectations In Construction Handicap, looks a belter with Hypnotised and Adrestia among nine runners.

The Harry Charlton-trained Hypnotised has proved steadily progressive and was only just denied when second at Newbury last time. A 3lb rise seems fair and he ought to go close under Lewis Edmunds.

William Haggas' Kinswomen only has a couple of lengths to find with the Charlton runner and makes the shortlist.

Adrestia, the Palace Of Holyroodhouse Stakes winner of 2025, hasn't been beaten far in a couple of hot handicaps this summer and with her mark sliding another 2lb she should be involved.

Arthur Fery's hopes of landing his maiden ATP Tour title at Winston-Salem Open was ended in emphatic fashion by Peruvian Ignacio Buse on Saturday.

From 3-3 in the first set, Fery lost six straight games before eventually going down 6-3 6-2 to Buse.

The promising 22-year-old clinched his second trophy of the season having lifted his maiden tour-level trophy at the ATP 500 event in Hamburg.
