World.title: Foreign Pupils on the Rise in Czech Schools — Nearly One in Five in Prague
World.content:
Of the nearly one million pupils attending Czech primary schools last academic year, almost 8% were foreign nationals, most commonly from Ukraine.

According to the Czech Statistical Office (CSO), Prague recorded the highest proportion, with foreign pupils making up 18% of all children in its primary schools.

Compulsory education is mandatory for Czech citizens as well as citizens of other European Union member states who reside in the Czech Republic for more than 90 days. The requirement also applies to foreign nationals with long-term residence permits.

Their children therefore have the same rights as Czech children, including access to free education, school meals and extracurricular activities.



The number of foreign pupils increased significantly after Russia invaded Ukraine in February 2022, nearly doubling that year. Their numbers have continued to rise ever since. Today, children from Ukraine account for 5% of all pupils in the Czech Republic.

The trend is similar in secondary schools, where the proportion of foreign pupils reached its highest level in the past 10 years, at almost 5% of the total.

Although the number of children in primary schools has remained relatively stable at just over one million in recent years, a sharp decline is expected in the coming years due to the falling birth rate, according to Vendula Kašparová of the CSO’s Social Development Statistics Department. The office said the birth rate has been falling continuously for the fifth consecutive year.

The decline is already visible at the kindergarten level. The number of children enrolled in kindergartens fell below 350,000 in the 2025/2026 academic year, the first time this has happened since 2013. Over the past three years, enrolment has dropped by more than 21,000 children, or around 5.8%.

Fewer Children Receiving Deferrals From Starting School

Kašparová identifies another clear trend: fewer children are being granted deferrals from starting compulsory school. Since the 2021/2022 academic year, the proportion of six-year-olds whose school entry was deferred has fallen from 24.1% in September 2021 to 17.7% in September 2025, representing just under 21,000 pupils.

Furthermore, an amendment to the Education Act is expected to reduce the number of deferrals even further. Under the new rules, deferrals will only be granted when justified by a medical condition that prevents a child from attending school.

This could include a serious medical condition following surgery, cancer treatment or a moderate intellectual disability.

World.title: Czechia, the Land of Burgers. More Fast Food Chains Enter the Market
World.content:
The Czech fast food market is expanding beyond its established players, with new international brands entering the country and existing chains opening restaurants in smaller cities.

McDonald’s and KFC continue to build their networks, while brands from Germany, the United States and Poland are looking for opportunities in the Czech Republic.

The expansion is increasingly moving beyond Prague and other major cities, with retail parks becoming an important location for new restaurants.



Burgermeister prepares Czech debut

One of the newest international brands preparing to enter the Czech market is Germany’s Burgermeister. The Berlin-based burger chain plans to open its first restaurant on Wenceslas Square at the beginning of next year.

The company already sees its Prague location as more than a single restaurant. It is also considering further locations across the country.

Popeyes and Burger King continue expanding

Burger King entered the Czech market 18 years ago and now operates around 70 restaurants. Popeyes arrived much later but has expanded quickly, opening 19 locations during its first three years in the country.

The companies are building a network that stretches from smaller regional towns to central Prague. In Králův Dvůr, a town of around 11,000 people, both Burger King and Popeyes operate at the Litavka Retail Park.

Popeyes is preparing additional restaurants at the Eden shopping centre and in the Budějovická area of Prague. The chain is also expanding into regional cities, with planned locations in Klatovy and Písek.

Five Guys adds another international brand

The Czech burger market gained another major international name last December when U.S. chain Five Guys opened its first Prague restaurant.

The restaurant is located in the former Máj department store on Národní Street. Five Guys is known for burgers prepared to order and a wide range of toppings, allowing customers to customise their meals.

Its prices, however, are generally higher than those of traditional fast food chains.

Another U.S. brand, Dave’s Hot Chicken, is also expected to enter the Czech market this year, according to consulting firm Cushman & Wakefield.

The chain specialises in spicy fried chicken and will therefore compete directly with established players such as KFC and Popeyes.

Czech chains are looking beyond their home cities

The expansion is not limited to international companies.

Czech burger chain Mama’s Burger is also developing its network. Originally based in Ostrava, the company has expanded into several larger Czech cities and operates a restaurant at Prague’s Arkády Pankrác shopping centre.

The company is also seeking franchise partners as it looks to increase the number of locations.

World.title: Slavia Prague to Face Bayern Munich, Arsenal and Porto in Champions League
World.content:
Slavia Prague have learned their eight opponents for the 2026/27 UEFA Champions League league phase following Thursday’s draw in Monaco.

Slavia will play four matches at home at Eden Arena and four away.

At home, Slavia will welcome Arsenal, Aston Villa, Villarreal and Lens. Their away fixtures will take them to Bayern Munich, Porto, Fenerbahçe and Sabah Baku in Azerbaijan.



The most high-profile home fixture will be against Arsenal, the reigning Premier League champions. Slavia also faced the London club in last season’s Champions League campaign, making the return meeting at Eden Arena particularly notable.

The toughest away assignment is likely to come in Munich, where Slavia will face six-time European champions Bayern at the Allianz Arena. The team will also travel to Portugal to meet Porto and to Istanbul for a match against Fenerbahçe.

The longest trip of the league phase will be to Baku to face Azerbaijani champions Sabah, who are making their debut in the Champions League league phase.

How the Champions League league phase works

The 2026/27 competition is being played under UEFA’s new league-phase format for the third consecutive season. Instead of a traditional group stage, all 36 teams are placed in one league table.

Each club plays eight matches against eight different opponents, with two opponents drawn from each of the four seeding pots. Every team has four home and four away games.

The top eight teams in the final standings will advance directly to the round of 16. Teams finishing ninth to 24th will enter a knockout playoff for the remaining eight places, while clubs finishing from 25th to 36th will be eliminated.

The league phase begins on September 8–10, with six rounds taking place before the end of 2026. The final two matchdays will be played in January, with the league phase concluding on January 27. UEFA will announce the exact dates and kick-off times for each individual match later.

World.title: MINT Market Returns to Prague’s Náplavka with More Than 130 Local Brands
World.content:
MINT Market returns to Prague’s Rašín Embankment on Sunday, September 6, bringing more than 130 independent brands and makers to the Vltava riverbank.

From 10 a.m. to 5 p.m., visitors can browse a wide selection of independent fashion, jewellery, ceramics, natural cosmetics, illustrations and original accessories, with many of the products made by small Czech and Prague-based businesses.



The popular design market is also known for its relaxed atmosphere, food stalls and chill-out area. Admission is free, and the riverside venue is fully accessible. The event is suitable for visitors of all ages.

MINT Market has been supporting independent and local creators since 2010.

Over the past 16 years, the project has grown from a small market into a nationwide platform, hosting more than 450 events in over 20 Czech cities and bringing together a community of more than 1,500 designers and makers.

For visitors, the September event offers a chance to discover products that are often made locally and in small quantities, while meeting the people behind the brands directly.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by The best design markets in CZ (@mintmarket.cz)

“Supporting small and local brands has been one of the core ideas of our project from the very beginning,” says MINT Market organizer Lenka Šašková.

“We provide creators with a place where they can showcase their products and meet their customers, because nothing can replace a personal meeting.”

The full list of vendors and further information about the September market can be found on the MINT Market website. Updates are also available through the Facebook event and Instagram.

World.title: Historic Invalidovna Building in Prague Begins Major Reconstruction
World.content:
The long-awaited reconstruction of Prague’s Invalidovna has officially begun.

The Baroque complex in Karlín will undergo a major renovation costing CZK 2.15 billion, with work scheduled for completion in 2030.

The project is the largest investment in the history of the National Heritage Institute (NPÚ). Alongside the restoration of the historic building, two new extensions will be constructed on the southern side of the complex.



One will provide facilities for the Prague Philharmonic Choir, while the other will house technical infrastructure needed to operate the site.

Much of Invalidovna will remain open to the public

Once the reconstruction is complete, the NPÚ will use part of the complex for restoration workshops, laboratories, archives and study rooms.

An underground garage with space for 50 vehicles is also planned.

Around 80 percent of the complex is expected to remain accessible to the public. The restored site will include exhibition and conference spaces, visitor routes through the Baroque interiors, a café and facilities for children’s groups operated by Prague 8.

A new multi-purpose hall in one of the extensions will be suitable for concerts, conferences and other events. The modern section will also contain technical facilities that cannot be accommodated inside the protected historic building.

The courtyard and gardens will be opened through the original entrances.

A Baroque complex with a long military history

Invalidovna was built between 1731 and 1737 based on plans by Kilián Ignác Dientzenhofer, one of the leading architects of the Czech Baroque. The institution provided accommodation and care for war veterans and their families until 1935.

The original complex was designed at a time when European armies were beginning to develop more systematic forms of care for soldiers who had been wounded or disabled in war.

Military campaigns were often accompanied by outbreaks of diseases such as cholera and typhus, which could kill even soldiers whose battlefield injuries were not life-threatening. Separate psychiatric institutions were later established for veterans suffering severe mental trauma after their military service.

World.title: PIZZA! PIZZA! POP-UP Returns to Holešovice Market on September 3
World.content:
Prague’s Holešovice Market will turn into a one-day celebration of Italian food next Thursday, September 3, with the fourth edition of PIZZA! PIZZA! POP-UP.

The event will run from 11 a.m. to 10 p.m., with more than two dozen food and drink businesses serving pizza, pinsa, pasta, arancini, Italian desserts, coffee and drinks. Admission is free.



Among the returning participants will be Pizza Metro, Mate’s PIZZA TRUCK, PIZZA Therapy, Pinsa Al Forno, HOLY PASTA, La Mia Spitzeria, Spojka Karlín, ŝam.ŝam.Piaggio, PIZZAKOLEM, Picoška, Vege Stará Placka, Naše maso and Cukrárna U Moučků.

This year will also bring a new style of pizza to the event. Third Coast Pizza will serve Detroit-style pizza, alongside the wide selection of Neapolitan pizza available from other vendors.

Visitors looking for something beyond pizza can try fresh pasta, pinsa, arancini and Italian sweets.

Drinks will include prosecco, beer, cocktails and coffee, with Gin Twist, Aperol Ape, Milujemě Prosecco, Pivovar Chroust and Garage 22 running various bars and stands. Garage 22 will also operate a negroni bar.

Bovelii Caffé will arrive in its red Piaggio, serving coffee roasted in Parma, Italy.

The programme will include music and Italian lessons from Lingua Nostra. Beads & Lemons will also be at the market with jewellery inspired by life by the sea.

PIZZA! PIZZA! POP-UP has been held at Holešovice Market for four years, bringing together restaurants, food producers and other businesses focused on Italian cuisine. This year’s edition will feature more participants than last year, including both returning vendors and newcomers.

World.title: Manifesto Market’s Craft Beer Returns for Its Third Edition
World.content:
Prague’s beer lovers can look forward to one of the city’s biggest beer events of the year as Manifesto Market brings back its annual beer festival for a third edition.

The two-day event will bring together some of the Czech Republic’s best-known craft breweries, alongside a guest brewery from Berlin, with more than 40 beers available to taste throughout the weekend.

Zichovec, Sibeeria, Chroust, MadCat, Fracek, Pivovar VIK and Berlin-based BRLO will each have their own pop-up tent, giving visitors the chance to explore a wide range of beer styles directly from the breweries.



More breweries are expected to be announced ahead of the event.

One of the highlights will be the festival’s limited-edition glass. It serves as the ticket for accessing the festival specials and can also be taken home as a souvenir.

The beer will be accompanied by food from more than 10 international kitchens at Manifesto. Visitors can expect everything from juicy burgers and tacos to spicy ramen and authentic Chinese roast duck, making it possible to turn the beer tasting into a full weekend meal.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by Manifesto Market (@manifestomarket.prague)

Tickets cost CZK 150 and are valid for both days, while early-bird tickets are available for CZK 125.

Tickets are available online at sevn.ly/x6Qy2mwE.

World.title: More Czechs Are Living Paycheck to Paycheck, New Survey Finds
World.content:
The number of Czechs who have nothing left from their paycheck at the end of the month is rising.

This year, 13 percent say they have no money left after covering their expenses, up from 9 percent last year. Meanwhile, 84 percent have at least a small amount left over, five percentage points less than in 2025.

The findings come from a May survey conducted by loan provider Provident Financial among 1,000 respondents.



According to the survey, Czechs’ ability to save is declining. Only 43 percent of respondents have at least 20 percent of their monthly income left after covering their expenses, down nine percentage points from last year. Almost half of Czechs nevertheless regularly set aside part of their paycheck each month.

At the same time, their overall financial resilience appears to be improving. More than a quarter of respondents have enough savings to cover their expenses for more than a year, compared with just 15 percent last year. The share of people with no financial reserve at all has also fallen, from 18 percent in 2025 to 13 percent this year.

The gap between men and women in the amount of money left at the end of the month has also narrowed. This year, 45 percent of men have at least 20 percent of their paycheck left after expenses, compared with 59 percent last year. Among women, the figure has fallen from 45 percent to 39 percent.

The share of Czechs with enough savings to cover 12 months without their main source of income has increased sharply this year, rising by 11 percentage points compared with 2025. At the same time, the proportion of respondents whose savings would last less than three months fell to 12 percent, down from 17 percent a year earlier.

Men are considerably more likely than women to report having enough savings to cover at least six months of expenses. The figure is 63 percent among men, compared with 39 percent among women.

Education also appears to play an important role in financial preparedness. Seven in ten respondents with a university degree say they have enough savings to cover at least six months, compared with 43 percent among people with lower levels of education.

World.title: One Hungarian among 261 foreigners missing on Tibetan side after devastating Nepal floods
World.content:
The death toll from the catastrophic floods and landslides in Nepal has continued to rise, while hundreds remain missing on the Tibetan side of the border. Chinese authorities say 261 foreign nationals from 23 countries are unaccounted for, including one Hungarian.

One Hungarian listed among missing foreigners

Authorities in China’s Tibet Autonomous Region are searching for 261 foreign nationals from 23 countries following the devastating landslide and flash floods near the Nepal–China border, according to the regional governor.

One Hungarian citizen is among those reported missing on the Tibetan side of the border. Chinese authorities have informed the embassies and consulates of the countries concerned.

The missing foreign nationals include 104 Nepali, 49 Indian, 33 Latvian, 18 American and 15 British citizens, alongside people from several other countries. The list also includes six Australians, six Canadians, three Germans, three Russians and one Hungarian.

The latest figures from Chinese authorities say 16 people have died and 546 remain missing in the Tibetan Autonomous Region. The situation on the Nepali side is even more devastating. As of Sunday morning, at least 734 people had died and around 2,498 were still missing, according to official figures, Reuters reported.

People gather as search operations continue at a town hit by the flash flood, amid increasing deaths and missing people, in Nuwakot, Nepal, on 29 August 2026. Photo: Anadolu Agency

Three Hungarians were previously reported missing

The latest Chinese figures come after Hungary’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs previously confirmed that three Hungarian citizens were believed to have been at the disaster site and had been reported missing.

The three were reportedly travelling with a pilgrimage group. Among them were a mother and her daughter, who arrived in Nepal just two hours before the flash flood struck on Wednesday morning. The Foreign Ministry said their whereabouts were unknown.

The disaster struck northeastern Nepal near the Tibetan border after a massive glacier-related collapse sent water, ice, mud and rock debris downstream. The resulting floods and landslides destroyed roads and bridges and severely damaged local infrastructure, making communication with people trapped in the affected areas extremely difficult.

An aerial photo shows houses at a town along the Trishuli River destroyed by the flash floods. Photo: Anadolu Agency

Search operations hampered by bad weather

Rescue efforts have continued, although poor weather has repeatedly disrupted operations. Nepal’s army said helicopter missions were temporarily suspended because of weather conditions, while search and rescue work continued on the ground. In Nuwakot district, helicopters have been delivering relief supplies and evacuating survivors from flood-hit areas, according to 444.hu.

More than 100 people may also be trapped inside a tunnel where large quantities of mud have accumulated. Rescuers have managed to reach some of those trapped, but the operation is extremely difficult: mud is reportedly up to 1.5 metres deep in parts of the tunnel, while there are few suitable landing areas for helicopters nearby. Authorities are also monitoring lakes that have formed near the border, as they are concerned about the possibility of further flooding.

Climate change blamed for worsening disaster

The catastrophe was triggered by the collapse of a glacier, with huge quantities of water, ice, mud and rock sweeping through settlements and destroying critical infrastructure. UN climate chief Simon Stiell said disasters of this kind are becoming more likely, frequent and severe as a result of humanity’s continued consumption of coal, oil and gas.

Chinese authorities have similarly linked the disaster to glacier instability caused by the long-term effects of global warming.

Nepal’s Foreign Minister Sisir Khanal stressed that the country contributes only around 0.01 per cent of global greenhouse gas emissions, yet its population is among those most severely affected by climate change.

The financial consequences are expected to be enormous. Nepal’s Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle told Reuters that preliminary estimates put the cost of rebuilding after the floods at USD 4–5 billion, equivalent to almost 10 per cent of the country’s annual GDP.

Many victims have yet to be identified

The full scale of the disaster is still unclear, with authorities still working to identify victims. DNA testing is required in some cases. Of the 49 bodies taken to a health facility in Kathmandu, only seven had been identified by Saturday. Relatives have been looking at photographs released by the facility in the hope of identifying missing family members.

Nepal has said it does not require foreign rescue teams, but has requested targeted international technical assistance to rescue people trapped in tunnels, restore transport and telecommunications links, and help identify victims. With thousands still missing on the Nepali side and hundreds unaccounted for across the border in Tibet, the final human toll of the disaster could rise further.

World.title: New Danube barrier is completed ahead of schedule, Paks reaches full capacity
World.content:
The first phase of a temporary bottom sill at Paks has been completed in just 17 days, using 43,000 cubic metres of rock, according to Prime Minister Péter Magyar. The project was designed to help secure sufficient cooling water for the nuclear power plant amid exceptionally low Danube water levels.

First phase completed across the Danube

The first phase of the bottom sill being built on the Danube at Paks has been completed, with the structure now spanning the full width of the river, Péter Magyar announced on Facebook on Saturday.

According to the prime minister, 43,000 cubic metres of rock have been used for the project since 12 August. He said the first phase was completed in 17 days, considerably faster and at a lower cost than originally planned.

Magyar described the work as an “extraordinary human and professional achievement”, arguing that it had helped the Paks Nuclear Power Plant return to reliable operation at full capacity.

“If the bottom sill had not been completed in time, two Paks turbines would now be standing,” Magyar wrote.

Emergency measure after record-low water levels

The project was launched after weeks of extreme heat and exceptionally low water levels on the Danube threatened the nuclear plant’s ability to obtain enough cooling water. Earlier this month, the situation came close to forcing the plant to shut down almost completely. One turbine was kept running, preventing a total shutdown.

To secure the necessary water supply, the government decided on 12 August to deploy barges and construct a bottom sill at Paks. The structure was intended as a rapid solution to raise the water level around the plant’s intake system and ensure that sufficient cooling water remained available.

Paks back at full production

The emergency measures came as the nuclear power plant was gradually returning to normal operation. The third turbine began being reconnected last Saturday, while three of the plant’s four units were already operating at full capacity by Monday. The plant subsequently returned to full output, according to Magyar.

The prime minister said the newly completed bottom sill played an important role in allowing the plant to reach peak production again.

Magyar also praised those involved in the construction, saying that during visits to Mohács, Paks and Dunaszentbenedek on Saturday, he had found that people cared about results rather than who was officially in charge of the water-management or military aspects of the project.

“People looked at whether the work had been done – faster and cheaper,” he wrote. The first phase of the bottom sill was completed two weeks ahead of schedule, according to the prime minister. Further work on the project is expected to continue.

World.title: Bus and car crash at Budapest’s Astoria leaves nine injured, woman in life-threatening condition
World.content:
A serious collision between a bus and a car at Budapest’s busy Astoria intersection has left nine people injured, including a woman who suffered life-threatening injuries. Two children were among those taken to hospital.

Serious crash in central Budapest

Nine people were injured when a bus collided with a car at Astoria in central Budapest on Saturday, the Hungarian National Ambulance Service (OMSZ) told MTI.

Several ambulance units were dispatched to the scene following the crash. A middle-aged woman was taken to hospital with serious, life-threatening injuries, while eight other people suffered less serious injuries. Two children were among those hospitalised.

Crash happened during a lane change

The accident happened at around 1:40 PM as the vehicles were travelling from Ferenciek Square towards Blaha Lujza Square, the National Police Headquarters told Index.

Initial information indicates that the car collided with a bus travelling in the same direction in the designated bus lane while the driver of the car was changing lanes.

The exact circumstances and cause of the collision are being investigated by the Budapest Police Headquarters (BRFK). Despite the severity of the accident, the vehicles did not cause a traffic obstruction, police said.

The investigation will determine how the collision occurred and whether any further circumstances contributed to the crash.

World.title: Terrifying: Bungee jumping goes wrong as rope gets wrapped around jumper’s neck
World.content:
A young festival-goer was taken to hospital after a bungee jumping accident at the Szeged Youth Days (SZIN) festival in southern Hungary on Friday night.

Almost fatal accident at Hungarian festival

The incident happened at the festival’s bungee jumping attraction at around 11 PM, with witnesses reporting that the participant encountered difficulties after being pulled back upwards by the elastic rope.

According to reports by RTL Híradó and local media, the rope became tangled around the young man’s neck during the jump. This particular detail has not been officially confirmed by authorities, however.

Bungee jumping rope reportedly wrapped around jumper’s neck

The participant had the bungee cord attached to his legs before being lifted in a basket by a crane to the jumping platform. He then jumped from the elevated basket.

The elastic rope stretched during the initial fall before pulling the jumper back upwards. According to witness accounts, the rope then became entangled around his body and neck, repeatedly pulling him up and down.

The incident prompted the festival’s on-site medical team to intervene immediately. Additional ambulance units were subsequently called to the scene, and the young man was taken to hospital in a stable condition.

Festival organisers say no serious injuries were found

SZIN organisers said the participant had been involved in an “unfortunate jump” and suffered an accident. The organisers remained in contact with his friends throughout the night.

At around 2 AM, they were informed that the hospital examinations had produced negative results and that the young man had been discharged. The incident occurred at the festival’s Partfürdő venue, where emergency services were also seen arriving at the scene.

Police launch investigation

Hungarian police have launched proceedings over suspected negligent endangerment in connection with an occupational activity. The investigation is expected to examine the circumstances of the accident and whether safety procedures surrounding the bungee jumping attraction were properly followed.

Despite the potentially serious nature of the incident, the participant was able to leave hospital without serious injuries, according to the information provided by the festival organisers.

World.title: This week’s Hungary Weekly Briefing is here: Russia pushes back, asset recovery begins and the euro moves closer
World.content:
Hungary’s post-Orbán transition entered a more consequential phase this week as Moscow openly challenged the new government’s foreign-policy direction, warning that changes in Budapest’s relationship with Russia could put energy supplies under pressure. At the same time, disputes over Paks II highlighted just how difficult it will be for the Magyar government to reduce Hungary’s dependence on Russian energy while protecting its long-term energy security.

Domestically, the government’s new asset recovery office moved from political promise to practical operation, only to face controversy over the appointment of its leadership and questions from critics, including some within the Tisza camp. The institution could become one of the most powerful tools for investigating and recovering public assets transferred or allegedly misused during the Orbán era.

The week also brought a major economic signal: Hungary has set 2030 as its target for adopting the euro. But with the 2026 deficit still expected to reach 7.5% of GDP, achieving that goal will require a dramatic improvement in the country’s public finances.

World.title: Tisza supporter organised protest a day after the appointment of the new head of national asset recovery office
World.content:
A small demonstration was held in front of Hungary’s Parliament on Saturday over the Tisza government appointment of Anna Unger as head of the National Asset Recovery and Asset Protection Office (NVVH).

A protest was organised over the new leader of the asset recovery office

The protest, organised by Tisza supporter André Nyerges, was announced just one day after Parliament elected Unger to lead the newly established authority. The demonstration was billed as being “for the National Asset Recovery and Asset Protection Office, Miklós Ligeti and the political transition”.

Nyerges argued that the appointment of Unger represented a serious threat to Hungary’s political transition, claiming that the selection resulted from behind-the-scenes agreements. He said politicians needed to be held accountable, referring to previous remarks by Tisza leader Péter Magyar about the role of the party’s supporters in scrutinising politicians.

Unger elected with 137 votes

Parliament elected Unger, a political scientist by training, as head of the NVVH on Friday with 137 votes in favour, seven against and one abstention. Her nomination had previously been approved by Parliament’s Justice Committee following hearings of the candidates. Within the Tisza delegation, Márton Melléthei-Barna was the only member of the committee to vote against Unger’s nomination.

Melléthei-Barna later explained that he had wanted a legally qualified person to head the office. Prosecutor Katalin Tasnády was appointed as deputy head responsible for investigations. The decision caused controversy among some Tisza supporters, many of whom had backed Miklós Ligeti, legal director of Transparency International Hungary, for the position.

Protest attracts limited turnout

As HVG.hu reported, the demonstration was scheduled to last around 30 minutes. Fewer than 500 people had indicated their intention to attend on Facebook shortly before it began.

Nyerges later said on the event’s Facebook page that another, unnamed demonstration had allegedly been organised at the same time, making it difficult to determine which event some participants had intended to attend. He expressed disappointment at the turnout and argued that the political system had been able to avoid visible consequences despite the controversy.

Stay up-to-date: What’s the public’s problem with Unger? PM Magyar responded strongly to critics of Hungary’s new asset recovery chief

Government defends appointment process

The appointment also prompted criticism from some Tisza and Fidesz supporters. Prime Minister Viktor Orbán responded in a video message, arguing that the head of an important government institution should not be selected through a popularity contest or “reality show”, but through a professional concept and a strictly regulated selection process.

Following her appointment, Unger sought to address concerns about the new office in an interview, saying its focus would be on locating and securing assets while operating within the framework of the rule of law. The dispute over her appointment has nevertheless exposed divisions among Tisza supporters, with some questioning the decision to overlook Ligeti and others defending the parliamentary selection process.

World.title: Relief for drivers as Budapest traffic becomes easier with important flyover now finished
World.content:
Road traffic could resume on the renovated northern flyover at Flórián Square towards Szentendrei Road in the early hours of Sunday, 30 August, the Budapest Transport Centre (BKK) has announced. This marks the completion of the full-scale renovation of the two flyovers connecting Szentendrei Road with Árpád Bridge.

Budapest can finally have traffic eased a bit

In the coming period, only minor repairs and the restoration of the surface junction at Flórián Square will remain, meaning the bulk of the work — the two bridges themselves — will be completed in time for the start of the school year.

According to Budapest Transport Centre, the renovation of the more than 40-year-old flyovers was made necessary by the significant deterioration that had occurred over the approximately 20 years since their previous reconstruction.

Moisture and dirt had damaged the reinforced concrete structures in several places, while water ingress around the pillars had caused the reinforcement steel to rust and the concrete surfaces to deteriorate. The two flyovers play a key role in transport in the capital and its surrounding metropolitan area, carrying tens of thousands of vehicles every day.

Both flyovers have been renovated

The renovation, carried out as a BKK investment with KM Építő Kft. as the general contractor, involved a comprehensive structural and condition-improvement reconstruction of the northern and southern flyovers at Flórián Square, including their bridge fittings. The most important works included:

Reconstruction of the road deck: the condition and geometry of the deck slabs were improved, new full-surface waterproofing was installed on both bridges, and new asphalt surfacing was laid on the bridges and connecting ramps;

Repairs to the reinforced concrete structures: damaged concrete surfaces were removed, corrosion of the reinforcement steel was halted, missing reinforcement was replaced, new reinforced concrete surfaces were created, and the concrete surfaces were given renewed protection against salt corrosion;

Reconstruction of the abutments and bridge ends: new bearings and expansion joints were installed at the abutments, expansion joints above the pillars were eliminated, and the bearing structures above the supports were renovated;

Replacement of kerbs and barriers: new monolithic reinforced concrete kerbs were constructed, while new prefabricated apron elements were installed along the sides of the superstructure and retaining walls, with high-containment road barriers and fall protection fitted on top;

Renovation of the stone cladding on the abutments: the deteriorated stone cladding was refurbished and broken sections were replaced;

Aesthetic restoration: defects in the structural surfaces were repaired, graffiti was removed, and an anti-graffiti coating was applied.

The renovated bridges of Budapest have a combined structural length of 686.57 metres, in addition to the renovated sections of the connecting ramps.

The renovated Flórián Square flyover in Budapest. Photo: BKK

Flyovers completed on schedule

The project’s total gross budget is HUF 3.27 billion (EUR 9 million). Thanks to competition during the public procurement procedure, a highly favourable bid was received, meaning the works were completed for 59.45 per cent of the originally estimated value, saving Budapest residents more than HUF 2 billion (EUR 5.5 million).

The renovation is being funded by the Municipality of Budapest, with a significant part of the necessary funding coming from money recovered in litigation related to the electronic ticketing system.

The first phase of the renovation began on 1 March 2025 with the closure of the southern flyover. Once the flyover was dismantled, its technical condition was found to be worse than expected. Previously hidden damage to the deck slabs meant that additional technical works had to be added to the project, resulting in changes to the original renovation schedule.

The southern flyover reopened to traffic in November 2025, after which work began on the northern flyover. Drawing on the experience gained during the southern flyover’s renovation, specialists carried out a particularly thorough assessment of the northern structure.

Structural works continued throughout 2026, with the project exceeding 70 per cent completion in technical terms by May and passing 90 per cent by the end of July.

Once the official traffic-opening procedure has been completed, road traffic on the northern flyover is expected to resume on 30 August, in time for the start of the school year. This will mark the completion of the structural renovation of both flyovers, with the contractor maintaining steady progress despite the technical difficulties encountered during the project.

Minor repairs related to the investment and the restoration of the surface junction will continue afterwards, alongside the removal of temporary traffic-management measures, and are expected to be completed by 17 September.

The successful bus priority measures introduced on Szentendrei Road and Pacsirtamező Street will remain in place. Temporary traffic-management measures and diversions — including the U-turn facility on Pacsirtamező Street — helped traffic flow during the renovation and eased the difficulties caused by the works. BKK thanked road users for their patience and co-operation.

World.title: Tiszalök’s hydropower plant stops operating as drought pushes River Tisza to a critical point
World.content:
The turbines at Tiszalök fell silent on 27 August, but the most important story is not the electricity that disappeared from the grid. It is the water that Hungary can no longer afford to use in the same way. As the Tisza’s flow has fallen to exceptionally low levels, water managers are changing the way the river is controlled — releasing stored water from Tiszalök downstream while trying to protect the remaining reserves of Lake Tisza and secure drinking water supplies farther south.

Author: Zotya Rokonál

When the water itself becomes the scarce resource

At Tiszalök, the change was gradual rather than dramatic. As the Tisza’s flow declined, the familiar operating regime of the Tiszalök Water Barrage became increasingly difficult to maintain. By the morning of 27 August, electricity generation at the Tiszalök Hydropower Plant had stopped.

The plant has an installed capacity of 12.9 megawatts, although its actual output had already fallen to minimal levels during the preceding period of exceptionally low water. The shutdown therefore represents a relatively small loss for Hungary’s overall electricity system and does not threaten the electricity supply of Tiszalök or the surrounding region.

The significance of the shutdown lies elsewhere. It is one of the clearest signs yet of how far the current water shortage has progressed. The crucial distinction is that the Tiszalök facility is not simply a power station. The wider water-control system has a much more important role in regulating the Tisza. In the present emergency, that function has taken priority over electricity generation.

A barrage built for water management, not just power

The situation at Tiszalök illustrates an aspect of hydropower that can easily disappear from public discussion: turbines are only one part of a much larger river-management system. According to the North Hungarian Water Management Directorate (ÉMVIZIG), the current water level and discharge are no longer sufficient for the hydropower plant to operate. The authority has therefore taken over water control at the Tiszalök Water Barrage using its No. 3 tilting gate.

At the same time, the upstream water level at Tiszalök is being gradually reduced. The level, which had been around 420 centimetres, is expected to fall towards approximately 400 centimetres over about a week. The measure is intended to allow additional water to be transferred towards Lake Tisza, the Eastern Main Canal and the Körös Valley, where water shortages have also become increasingly serious. That may sound counterintuitive: when water is scarce, why release more of it?

The answer lies downstream. The available water reserves now have to be redistributed along the river system to protect more critical needs farther south. The objective is not to restore the Tisza to normal summer conditions, which would be impossible under the current inflow. Instead, water managers are trying to make the remaining reserves last as long as possible while directing them towards the areas where they are most urgently needed.

The numbers behind the drought

The scale of the problem is particularly striking in the Tisza’s catchment. The river’s flow does not depend solely on rainfall around Tiszalök. Precipitation across the entire catchment, soil moisture, tributary flows, groundwater conditions and evaporation all determine how much water ultimately reaches the Hungarian section of the river.

This year, the catchment has received exceptionally little precipitation, while persistent heat has increased evaporation. The result is a particularly difficult combination: less water is entering the system, while more is being lost.

The consequences are already visible around Lake Tisza. Earlier this month, Daily News Hungary reported that the lake’s water level had fallen below 700 centimetres at the Kisköre upper gauge, with water-management authorities pointing to the lack of rainfall, exceptionally low inflows and increased evaporation as key factors.

The situation has since deteriorated further. The problem is not simply that the landscape looks different. Lower water levels affect habitats, recreation, navigation and the ability of the wider water-management system to meet competing demands.

More on Hungary’s water crisis: Lake Tisza under threat: alarm bells ring at tourist hotspot

Why 610 centimetres matters

One of the most important figures in the current situation is 610 centimetres. This is the minimum operating water level at Kisköre-felső that has become critical for the management of Lake Tisza. Once the reservoir reaches that level, the amount of water that can be released downstream becomes increasingly constrained. Further depletion could create serious ecological consequences.

This is why the water released from the Tiszalök area has become so important. The purpose is not simply to send as much water downstream as possible. It is an attempt to manage a shrinking resource across a connected system of rivers, canals and reservoirs.

The challenge is essentially one of timing. Water retained today can protect one part of the system, but it cannot simultaneously serve every downstream need. If too much is held back, lower sections of the Tisza face greater pressure. If too much is released, reserves elsewhere can be exhausted more quickly.

The consequences are already visible in Tiszalök

For people living around Tiszalök, the crisis is not merely a number on a hydrological chart. The shrinking water level is particularly visible around the Kis-Tisza oxbow area. As the water retreats, exposed mudflats and changing shorelines become increasingly prominent.

For boat owners, the conditions also bring practical hazards. Vessels can become stranded in shallow or muddy areas, while previously submerged sections of the riverbank may become unstable. Anyone using the waterway therefore needs to take considerably greater care than under normal conditions. The wider Tisza region has been showing similar warning signs.

Just days before the Tiszalök shutdown, Daily News Hungary reported that another popular Hungarian lake was experiencing critical water shortages, with large areas of exposed lakebed visible around the Bölömbika lookout. Taken together, these developments show that the current drought is not an isolated local problem. It is affecting several interconnected water systems at the same time.

See the photos: Another popular Hungarian lake dries out, Bölömbika lookout shows critical conditions

The pressure moves downstream

The most sensitive point may ultimately be farther south, at Szolnok. According to current water-management calculations, extremely low water levels could develop there if the Tisza’s discharge falls further. That is where the water shortage becomes a direct question of public infrastructure. The Tisza is an important source of drinking water for Szolnok and surrounding settlements.

Earlier this year, Daily News Hungary reported that authorities had prepared a floating water-intake system in Szolnok because of the exceptionally low river level, including mobile pumps that could be activated if conventional water abstraction became difficult. The current situation therefore goes beyond agriculture or environmental protection. At sufficiently low water levels, drought can become an issue of basic public infrastructure and drinking-water security.

Watch the video: River Tisza nears historic low as tens of thousands face risk of water shortages

Electricity is losing the argument to water security

The Tiszalök shutdown also raises an uncomfortable question about renewable energy in a changing climate. Hydropower is renewable, but its output depends directly on water availability. During an extreme drought, the same river may simultaneously be needed for drinking water, ecological protection, agriculture, water transfers and electricity generation.

In Tiszalök, the priorities are now clear: water regulation comes first. The shutdown was announced publicly by Péter Lajos Szakács, the local Member of Parliament for the Tisza party. He stressed that the hydropower plant’s primary role is water-flow regulation and that electricity generation is a secondary function. He also said that the electricity supply of Tiszalök and the surrounding region remains secure, while the Paks Nuclear Power Plant is operating at full capacity.

This distinction is important. The loss of 12.9 MW of installed hydropower capacity does not amount to an electricity crisis for the region. What it demonstrates is something different: when a river becomes severely depleted, electricity production can no longer be treated as the overriding purpose of the infrastructure built around it. The water itself has become more valuable than the electricity that could be generated from it.

How long can the system keep adapting?

That may be the most important unanswered question. Water-management authorities are continuously monitoring river levels and reservoir conditions. Water transfers are being reduced where necessary, and some irrigation activities have been suspended. Emergency measures are also being prepared where drinking-water supplies could eventually be affected.

But no water-management intervention can manufacture rainfall. The longer the drought persists, the more difficult the choices become. Sending water downstream can protect drinking-water supplies but reduce reserves elsewhere. Retaining water can protect ecosystems or future users but leave lower reaches under greater pressure.

Maintaining hydropower production can generate electricity, but when water has become scarce enough, that may no longer be the responsible priority. The Tiszalök shutdown is therefore best understood not as an isolated power-sector event, but as a visible sign of a much wider water crisis.

For now, the authorities are managing the available reserves and trying to protect the most critical functions of the river system. Whether the Tiszalök turbines can resume generation later this year will ultimately depend on something that no control gate can provide: enough water arriving from upstream. Until then, the silent turbines at Tiszalök are less a story about lost electricity than a measure of how seriously Hungary’s water shortage has developed.

World.title: Bucharest Stock Exchange-listed tech company AROBS posts 121% higher net profit in H1
World.content:
AROBS Transilvania Software (BVB: AROBS), one of the largest entrepreneurial technology companies listed on the Bucharest Stock Exchange, recorded consolidated turnover of RON 292 million in the first half of 2026, up 36% compared to H1 2025, EBITDA of RON 40 million, a 29% increase, and net profit of approximately RON 23 million, up 121% compared to the same period of last year.

The first six months of 2026 represented the AROBS group’s best first half of the past three years in terms of turnover, EBITDA, operating profit, and net profit. The positive momentum accelerated in the second quarter, when the group generated turnover of approximately RON 148 million, EBITDA of RON 22 million, and net profit of over RON 15 million, twice the level recorded in Q1 2026 and almost four times higher than in Q2 2025.

“In 2024 and 2025, we increased the scale of the group and added capabilities through the acquisitions we completed. In 2026, our focus is on integrating these capabilities through One AROBS and transforming this structure into an organization that operates as one, both commercially and operationally,” stated Voicu Oprean, founder and CEO of AROBS.

Of the consolidated turnover recorded in H1 2026, RON 242 million, representing almost 83% of the total, was generated by activities classified as organic, while RON 50 million came from companies included in the M&A scope.

At business segment level, Software Services generated turnover of approximately RON 186 million, up 31% compared to H1 2025. Software Products recorded turnover of RON 54 million, 17% above the level reported in the comparable period, while the segment’s gross margin increased from 52% to 54%.

The fastest growth was recorded by Integrated Systems, where turnover advanced by 88% to RON 52 million, mainly as a result of the implementation of projects for the National House of Public Pensions and the Ministry of Health. Furthermore, after the end of the first semester, AROBS Systems signed a contract with the Agency for Payments and Intervention for Agriculture (APIA) with a total value of approximately RON 70 million, excluding VAT, of which approximately 61% is attributable to the company.

In the first half of the year, AROBS achieved 53% of the turnover, 49% of the EBITDA and 65% of the net profit envisaged in the 2026 Consolidated Revenue and Expense Budget, which provides for turnover of RON 552 million, EBITDA of RON 82 million and net profit of RON 35 million. “The results for the first half of the year provide the first financial confirmation of this model. Ascendia (BVB: ASC), a Romanian benchmark and provider of critical learning infrastructure, announced its financial results for the first half of 2026. According to the press release, the company recorded the best first half in its history, marking accelerated growth supported by the completion of previous projects, its own product portfolio, and efficient capital management.

As of June 30, 2026, equity doubled to RON 37.95 million, representing 71% of total assets of RON 53.45 million. The current liquidity ratio strengthened to 4.56, giving the company the capacity to finance future expansion stages without the pressure of an immediate need for external financing.

World.title: CTP delivers 3,000 sqm of built-to-suit temperature-controlled warehousing in Bucharest
World.content:
Developer and operator of logistics and industrial real estate CTP has delivered nearly 3,000 sqm of built-to-suit temperature-controlled warehouse space to Frigonet Logistics at CTPark Bucharest South, according to a press release published on Friday, August 28.

Frigonet Logistics provides integrated cold chain logistics services, including refrigerated warehousing and handling, national dual-temperature distribution for chilled and frozen goods, picking, and cross-docking. The company selected CTPark Bucharest South for its strategic location and excellent connectivity to Bucharest and key regional hubs, enabling more efficient distribution routes and supporting the continued expansion of its operations.

Frigonet Logistics has signed a long-term lease for its new facility, which it will use to expand its temperature-controlled storage operations for refrigerated and frozen food products, supporting its growing logistics network across Romania.

CTPark Bucharest South is strategically located with direct access to Bucharest’s ring road and major national transport corridors, providing excellent connectivity to the capital, the A0, A1 and A2 motorways, and key destinations across Romania and Southeastern Europe. The park comprises nearly 140,000 sqm of built space across a nearly 37-hectare site.

“Beyond the operational advantages, the location at CTPark Bucharest South provides excellent connectivity to Bucharest and our key regional hubs, helping us optimise distribution routes and improve logistics efficiency. This investment gives us the capacity and flexibility required to support our continued growth and to provide our customers with temperature-controlled transport and logistics services that meet the highest standards,” explained David Stoian, Executive Director of Frigonet Logistics.

The facility incorporates dedicated frozen storage operating at -20°C, a 0-4°C buffer area, a refrigeration plant, and the infrastructure required to safely handle and store temperature- sensitive products while maintaining an uninterrupted cold chain.

“We are pleased to welcome Frigonet Logistics to CTPark Bucharest South and to support the company’s next stage of expansion,” said Cristina Manea, Business Developer at CTP in Romania.

World.title: Mastering the Music Business brings over 100 speakers to Bucharest
World.content:
The 11th edition of the Mastering the Music Business (MMB) conference will take place at Hotel Caro in Bucharest from September 1 to 3. More than 100 speakers from 16 countries will participate in 27 panels, workshops, and discussions on building careers in the music industry.

The lineup includes Romanian artists and industry figures such as Grasu XXL, Nicole Cherry, Marius Moga, AFO, Bean of Subcarpați, and television host Cătălin Măruță, who also manages singer Andra.

They will be joined by professionals representing European festivals, booking agencies, record labels, and music organizations. Speakers include European Music Exporters Exchange president Corinne Sadki, ESNS junior booker Janneke de Boer, SoAlive Music Conference founder Ruth Koleva, Music Glue business development head Marion Sosnowicz, and Future Echoes festival director Peter Åstedt.

For the first time, the conference will host representatives of music export offices from 11 European countries: Poland, Latvia, Lithuania, Switzerland, Belgium, France, Italy, Ukraine, Austria, Greece, and Germany. Discussions will focus on festivals, touring, and the professional networks that could help Romanian artists reach European markets.

The program will cover topics including artificial intelligence in the creative process, independent music economics, ticket fraud, songwriting, artist selection by European bookers, mental health, fan communities, copyright, and crisis management.

AFO and Bean will discuss Subcarpați’s development on the opening day, while Marius Moga will participate in a panel about how brands choose music projects. The final day will feature a conversation with Măruță about managing Andra and a keynote address by Grasu XXL.

The conference will also include three small-group accelerators focusing on music marketing, booking, and music business fundamentals. They are open to ticket holders through separate registration, subject to availability.

Each conference day will be followed by concerts at Club Expirat as part of the MMB Showcase Festival. Twelve acts from Romania and elsewhere in Europe will perform during the three evenings, with admission free, subject to venue capacity.

World.title: Romania’s population drop slowed by migration but still ongoing
World.content:
Romania’s resident population reached 19.041 million people on January 1, 2026, 1,829 fewer than a year earlier, according to provisional data published Friday, August 28, by the National Institute of Statistics.

The decline was largely limited by migration. The number of immigrants exceeded that of emigrants by 102,200, but the difference did not fully offset the natural decrease of 104,100 people.

Overall, the positive international migration balance increased compared with previous years and covered almost the entire difference between the number of deaths and the number of births.

Among people who left Romania, men accounted for 57.9% of the total. They were also the majority among those who came to the country, with a share of 58.6%.

The urban population reached 9.792 million people at the beginning of 2026, up 0.2% from the same period in 2025. The female population stood at 9.744 million people, down 0.1%.

Beyond the decrease in the number of inhabitants, INS data indicate an intensification of demographic aging. People aged at least 65 accounted for 20.5% of the population on January 1, 2026, compared with 20.3% a year earlier. At the same time, the share of children aged 0 to 14 fell from 15.4% to 15.1%.

The demographic aging index therefore rose from 131.3 to 135.9 elderly people for every 100 young people. In other words, at the beginning of 2026, Romania had almost 136 people aged at least 65 for every 100 children under 15. The demographic dependency ratio fell slightly, from 55.6 to 55.2 young and elderly people for every 100 working-age adults.

INS included foreign citizens in the resident population, as well as stateless people, who usually live in Romania for a period of at least 12 months. During the war in Ukraine, the statistics also include Ukrainian citizens benefiting from temporary protection in Romania.

World.title: Tour of Romania brings together 23 cycling teams from 16 countries
World.content:
The 2026 Tour of Romania will bring together approximately 150 cyclists from 23 teams representing 16 countries between September 9 and 13. Italian Olympic champion Elia Viviani will also attend the race as manager of Italy’s national team.

The five-stage competition will cover more than 800 kilometers, beginning in Chișinău, Moldova, and ending with a final circuit in Bucharest. This will be the first edition of the race to start outside Romania.

“The presence of 23 teams from 16 countries confirms the growing interest in the Tour of Romania,” Romanian Cycling Federation president Cătălin Sprinceană said. “We are pleased that the public will be able to see athletes from so many countries at the start.”

The lineup includes ten UCI continental teams, eight club teams, and five national teams. The participating countries are Albania, Austria, Belgium, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bulgaria, Greece, Hungary, Italy, Moldova, Monaco, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Romania, Turkey, and the United States.

The national teams of Romania, Italy, Moldova, Albania, and Bosnia and Herzegovina will compete in the race.

Elia Viviani won the Olympic omnium title at Rio 2016 and is a three-time Olympic medalist and three-time track world champion. He has also won stages in all three Grand Tours and claimed the European road race title in 2019. After a 16-year professional career, the Italian cyclist is beginning a new role as manager of his country’s national team.

The participating teams will be officially presented in Chișinău on September 8. The first stage, from Chișinău to Ungheni, will take place the following day.

The race will then continue in Romania with stages from Iași to Piatra Neamț on September 10, Piatra Neamț to Băile Balvanyos on September 11, and Brașov to Ploiești on September 12. The final stage will be held on a circuit in Bucharest on September 13.

The race will be broadcast live by Prima Sport and on the official Tour of Romania and Auchan Romania Facebook pages, while TVR Sport will air daily highlights. Further details can be found here.

World.title: NASA Space Apps Challenge opens registration for Bucharest, Cluj-Napoca events
World.content:
NASA Space Apps Challenge, the world’s largest hackathon, will return to Romania on November 14-15, with simultaneous events in Bucharest and Cluj-Napoca. Registration for the 48-hour international event is open until November 13.

Under the theme The Next Frontier!, participants will form teams of up to six members and use NASA’s open data to develop solutions to challenges related to Earth and space exploration. The challenges will be announced on September 17.

The competition is open to programmers, scientists, engineers, designers, students, storytelling specialists, and other people interested in technology and innovation, regardless of their age, experience, or professional background.

“Romania has people with ideas and skills who can compete at the highest international level, and this competition is an extraordinary opportunity to bring them together and connect them to one of the most innovative global communities,” said Diana Iosu, founder of DiFine PR and organizer of the Bucharest edition.

The Bucharest event will be held at the Romanian-American University, while the Cluj-Napoca competition will take place at ClujHUB. Registration for Bucharest is available here, and for Cluj here.

Two winning teams will be selected from each city to advance to the global competition and compete against thousands of teams worldwide. Global winners will be invited to visit a NASA center or facility, attend an event celebrating their projects, and meet representatives of the US space agency.

Participants will also receive free access to the Google AI Professional Certificate course offered through Coursera.

People under 18 may participate only with the consent of a parent or legal guardian, who must accompany them throughout the event.

The 2025 edition attracted 200 registrations in Romania. Winning projects included an algorithm assessing the environmental effects of business decisions, a visual platform for learning about physics and astrophysics, and an AI solution that converted air-quality data into real-time information.

Launched globally in 2012, the NASA Space Apps Challenge has brought together more than 487,000 participants from 190 countries and territories. The Romanian editions are organized by ROTSA and DiFine PR.

World.title: IKEA opens first Plan and Order Point in Iași
World.content:
IKEA will open its first Plan and Order Point in Iași on Monday, August 31. Located in Egros Shopping Center, the studio will be the retailer’s sixth such facility in Romania.

The location will offer personalized planning services for kitchens, wardrobes, and storage solutions. Customers will be able to work individually with IKEA specialists to select configurations, products, and finishes suited to their homes and budgets, the company said.

The studio will feature three kitchen layouts, three wardrobe solutions, two planning desks, and more than 1,400 IKEA products. Around 50 everyday products will also be available to purchase directly.
