World.title: Gallery: Siim Kallas sent off with state honors
World.content:
Former Prime Minister Siim Kallas will be laid to rest with state honors on Saturday.

The hearse began its journey in Viimsi, from where traveled through Tallinn and via Toompea to the Estonia Concert Hall.

The first memorial stop was at the Viimsi municipal government building where representatives of the Viimsi municipal government and council had gathered. Siim Kallas lived in Viimsi and served as mayor of Viimsi Municipality from 2017 to 2019.

Tunne Kelam and Mari-Ann Kelam arrive for Siim Kallas' farewell ceremony at the Viimsi municipal government building. Source: Ken Mürk/ERR

In Tallinn, the hearse stopped outside the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Bank of Estonia, Ministry of Finance, Riigikogu and Stenbock House.

The hearse then arrived at the Estonia Concert Hall. The coffin was received with military honors by the Guard Battalion's honor guard and the military band of the Estonian Defense Forces.

Inside the Estonia Concert Hall, representatives of Viimsi Municipality, the Reform Party, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Ministry of Finance, Bank of Estonia and Riigikogu stood guard of honor beside the coffin.

The hearse carrying Siim Kallas' remains also stopped outside the Bank of Estonia. Source: Iris Tähema/ERR

President Alar Karis said in a speech at Siim Kallas' memorial ceremony that Kallas was never afraid of bold ideas for advancing life in Estonia and knew that ideas also had to be put into practice, because otherwise there was a risk of remaining invisible in a small and distant corner of the world.

"That is precisely how he helped Estonia grow into a modern country that values freedom and did everything in his power to bring us back into Europe," Karis said.

Following Karis' remarks, the current and former prime ministers placed a parliamentary gavel on the coffin.

Prime Minister and Reform Party Chair Kristen Michal said in his eulogy that the measure of a statesman lies not only in making decisions at the right time, but also in those decisions proving to be right decades later. "Siim Kallas had that fortunate touch, coupled with a sharp mind, courage and perseverance!"

Farewell to Siim Kallas at the Estonia Concert Hall. Source: Iris Tähema/ERR

Siim Kallas died on August 22 at the age of 77. He served as Estonia's prime minister, foreign minister and finance minister, governor of the Bank of Estonia, vice president of the European Commission and a member of the Riigikogu on several occasions. Kallas was one of the authors of the Self-Managing Estonia (IME) proposal, one of the leaders of the 1992 monetary reform and one of the founders of the Reform Party.

World.title: U.S. crude oil imports from Iraq drop to zero
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Official data released by the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) on Sunday, August 30, 2026, shows that United States imports of Iraqi crude oil fell back to zero barrels per day (bpd) during the past week, down from an average of 6,000 bpd recorded the previous week.

The fluctuation follows an extended summer lull where direct crude shipments from Iraq to U.S. refiners remained largely suspended amid ongoing maritime transit adjustments in the Gulf.

World.title: Iraq recovers 1.35T dinars in anti-corruption drive
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The Iraqi federal government has successfully recovered public funds, financial assets, and real estate valued at over 1.359 trillion IQD (approximately $1.04 billion) during its anti-corruption campaign, “Sawlat al-Fajr” (Dawn Assault), government spokesperson Haider Al-Aboudi announced on Saturday, August 29, 2026.

In a statement delivered to Al Iraqiya News and reported by the Iraqi News Agency (INA), Al-Aboudi revealed that the Federal Commission of Integrity has received more than 26,000 formal corruption reports, reflecting heightened institutional activity and public reporting.

Key Operational Milestones & Asset Recovery Figures

Total Asset Value Recovered: Surpassed 1.359 trillion IQD in seized liquid funds, frozen financial instruments, and confiscated real estate properties.

Integrity Commission Reports: Over 26,000 tips and corruption filings registered with the Federal Commission of Integrity during the ongoing enforcement phase.

Whistleblower Financial Incentives: In accordance with the Informants Law (قانون مكافأة المخبرين), individuals who submit verified information leading directly to the recovery of stolen public funds are entitled to financial rewards of up to 5% of the total recovered sum.

Al-Aboudi outlined that the government’s anti-corruption strategy balances punitive judicial enforcement with systemic preventive reforms:

Judicial Safeguards: Emphasized that the Iraqi judiciary stands as the core guarantor supporting the legitimacy, evidence verification, and success of anti-corruption actions.

Direct Prime Ministerial Oversight: Highlighted the Prime Minister’s recent field visit to the Commission of Integrity, confirming direct executive backing for specialized investigative judges and investigators.

Preemptive Contract Auditing: Instituting mandatory advance audits on high-value public procurement contracts to identify irregularities before fund disbursements take place.

Digital Transformation and Automation: Accelerating the digitization of state transactions and public registries to minimize arbitrary human interference, extortion, and bribery opportunities across ministries.

Al-Aboudi characterized systemic corruption as a deeply entrenched web linking financial schemes, administrative loopholes, and political influence that drains public wealth and stalls infrastructure projects.

He reiterated that there will be no halt or political compromise in the government’s anti-corruption drive, noting that institutional transparency, automated governance, and aggressive asset recovery remain long-term priorities.

World.title: Sanad: Iraq targets simultaneous nationwide 5G rollout
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The Iraqi federal government is actively working to coordinate a simultaneous rollout of next-generation 5G telecommunications services across all Iraqi governorates and the Kurdistan Region, Minister of Communications Mustafa Sanad announced on Saturday, August 29, 2026.

Speaking to the Iraqi News Agency (INA), Sanad stated that existing technical and administrative differences between the federal ministry and the Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG) are manageable, emphasizing that bilateral discussions are progressing toward unified protocols.

Key Discussion Tracks & Technical Files

Synchronized 5G Commercial Launch: Noting that the Kurdistan Region had taken earlier exploratory steps toward 5G deployment, the federal ministry is coordinating with regional authorities to synchronize spectrum allocation and commercial launches nationwide.

Transit Fiber-Optic Backbone (Basra to Europe): Coordinating agreements regarding the strategic international transit fiber cable routed from Basra through the Kurdistan Region onward to European hubs, requiring unified commercial terms with operators operating in the region.

Unified International Representation: Sanad underscored Baghdad’s position that Iraq must engage as a unified entity before international telecommunications bodies and multilateral organizations, with the federal Ministry of Communications serving as the sovereign representative.

Regulatory Coordination & Operator Oversight: Addressing regulatory discrepancies stemming from the KRG’s direct ministerial oversight over regional mobile operators (including Korek Telecom), in contrast to the federal model where licensing and sector oversight are managed through an independent communications and media commission.

Sanad confirmed his intention to lead an official delegation to Erbil following a formal written invitation extended by KRG Prime Minister Masrour Barzani during Sanad’s first week in office, which was reaffirmed during a visit to Baghdad by the KRG Minister of Transport and Communications.

The upcoming ministerial meetings aim to finalize an integrated operational framework for cross-border fiber traffic, harmonize telecom licensing standards, and establish joint technical committees to oversee spectrum readiness for 5G network integration.

World.title: Toxic Sulfur odor blankets Baghdad again: Warnings of health crisis
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — A pungent, sulfur-like odor returned to envelope several residential districts across Baghdad overnight between Friday and Saturday, August 29, 2026, marking the latest wave of recurrent toxic air pollution that has triggered widespread public health concerns and resident complaints.

The recurrence comes less than three weeks after an intense sulfur plume blanketed southern and central Baghdad for 48 hours, prompting fresh warnings from the Green Iraq Observatory regarding untreated industrial emissions, unregulated open burning, and poor environmental oversight

According environmental evaluations by the Green Iraq Observatory, the recurrent pollution wave stems from a combination of industrial practices and meteorological dynamics:

High-Sulfur Heavy Fuel Combustion: Heavy reliance on high-sulfur heavy fuel oil (HFO) and untreated crude derivatives across thermal power generation stations, brick kilns, and asphalt plants on the capital’s periphery.

Al-Daura Refinery Smoke Plumes: Previous documentation captured heavy smoke discharges emanating from the Al-Daura refinery complex south of Baghdad, drifting over nearby urban neighborhoods.

Informal Waste Incineration: Continuous unregulated burning of municipal plastic waste and uncontrolled open landfill fires surrounding the municipal perimeter.

Thermal Inversion Trapping: Nocturnal and early-morning thermal temperature inversions create a dense atmospheric lid, preventing vertical dispersion and trapping toxic sulfur dioxide (SO2) and particulate matter near ground level.

The Green Iraq Observatory warned that the return of sulfur emissions within less than two weeks disproves official claims of containment, highlighting severe health ramifications:

Surge in Respiratory Illness: Noticeable increases in bronchitis flare-ups, acute respiratory distress syndrome, and severe asthma attacks.

High-Risk Demographics: Children, elderly residents, and individuals with pre-existing cardiopulmonary conditions face heightened vulnerabilities from prolonged particulate exposure.

World.title: Central Bank freezes assets of MPs and officials in Green Dawn crackdown
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) has issued formal directives ordering the comprehensive freezing of all movable and immovable assets belonging to prominent lawmakers, former officials, and political figures arrested during the high-profile Green Dawn operation, according to an official directive obtained by the 964 Network on Friday, August 28, 2026.

The banking circular, issued by the CBI’s Legal Affairs Department to all licensed operating banks across Iraq, enforces an administrative request from the Ministry of Finance predicated on a judicial order issued by the Central Anti-Corruption Criminal Investigative Court.

Targeted Lawmakers and High-Profile Figures

The asset-freeze schedule names 12 high-profile political and executive figures:

Muthanna Al-Samarrai(Member of Parliament / Azm Alliance Leader)

Bahaa Al-Din Al-Nouri(Member of Parliament)

Ziad Al-Janabi(Member of Parliament)

Abdul Rahman Al-Luwaizi(Member of Parliament)

Mohammed Farman Al-Jubouri(Member of Parliament)

Hind Al-Abbasi(Member of Parliament)

Bushra Al-Qaisi(Member of Parliament)

Mudhar Al-Kuri(Member of Parliament)

Ashwaq Al-Jubouri(Member of Parliament)

Aliah Nassif(Member of Parliament)

Mohammed Al-Sayhood(Former Member of Parliament)

Ibrahim Al-Sumaidaie(Former Political Adviser to the Prime Minister)

Judicial and Administrative Framework

Judicial Order No. 555: The freeze order executes Decision No. 555, handed down on July 13, 2026, by the Investigative Judge at the Central Anti-Corruption Criminal Court.

Baghdad/Karkh Court of Appeal: The decision was officially communicated via formal correspondence from the Presidency of the Baghdad/Karkh Federal Court of Appeal dated July 27, 2026.

Inter-Agency Enforcement: The Ministry of Finance subsequently directed the Central Bank of Iraq to instruct the national financial network to freeze all liquidity, deposit accounts, shares, and registered real estate assets under the defendants’ names.

Asset Disclosure Requirement: Licensed commercial banks were instructed to immediately identify any existing liquid balances, credit assets, or safe-deposit holdings registered to the named individuals and notify the requesting judicial and financial authorities to execute statutory asset impoundment.

The wide-ranging asset freeze following Operation Green Dawn represents one of the most extensive joint judicial-executive crackdowns on high-level political corruption in Iraq’s modern legislative history.

By freezing domestic banking assets and properties of sitting and former parliamentarians across multiple political factions, the specialized anti-corruption judiciary aims to prevent capital flight, safeguard contested public funds, and ensure full transparency during subsequent criminal court proceedings.

World.title: US revokes ex-Iraq finance minister’s visa after FBI adds her to terrorism watchlist
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Trump administration has revoked former Iraqi Finance Minister Taif Sami Mohammed Al Shakarchi’s US visa after she was put on an FBI terrorist blacklist.

The US State Department announced the decision on Friday, stating Sami, Iraq’s finance minister from 2022 to July 2026, had her visa canceled after the FBI added her to its terrorist blacklist.

US authorities did not explain why they included her on the list.

Officials said that Sami had already departed the United States before his visa was canceled.

The action precludes her from returning on that visa.

The discovery comes weeks after Sami was implicated in a broader corruption probe in Iraq.

An Iraqi court summoned the former minister earlier this month, and she was allegedly put on a judicial wanted list as authorities probed charges against high political and government officials.

She was thought to be outside Iraq and had not been captured.

The summons is not a conviction, and Iraqi police have not shown Sami’s crime in court.

Her inclusion on the US terrorist blacklist is unrelated to the Iraqi corruption inquiry, and US officials have not publicly said if the two cases are related.

The action marks a significant shift in Washington’s approach to Sami.

Before becoming finance minister in 2022, she was named to the State Department’s International Women of Courage Award while working as Iraq’s deputy finance minister and budget director-general.

The department at the time recognized her as playing a key role in efforts to combat corruption in Iraq’s public finances.

At the 2022 award ceremony, then-Secretary of State Antony Blinken lauded Sami’s anti-corruption efforts, emphasizing her work exposing financial scams and defending public resources.

In October 2022, previous Prime Minister Mohammed Shia Al-Sudani’s cabinet appointed Sami as Finance Minister, and she served in that role until July of this year.

Her story has given the anti-corruption fight in Baghdad a worldwide dimension.

Prime Minister Ali Falih al-Zaidi’s administration has started a series of investigations, arrests, and asset seizures aimed at former and current officials to recoup public monies and strengthen state control.

The State Department has not publicly explained the information behind the FBI watchlist decision or announced any criminal charges against Sami in the United States.

The FBI’s public Most Wanted Terrorists list should not be confused with the larger terrorist blacklist maintained by the US government; Sami is not included on the public Most Wanted Terrorists site.

World.title: 1 in 5 food samples fails: Why so few cases end in conviction
World.content:
Inadequate packaging can increase the risk of contamination

Food safety checks expose widespread violations

UP finds highest share of violations

Enforcement gaps raise concerns over food safety

Testing reveals gaps in Indiaâs food safety system

Staff shortage adds to enforcement challenge

Shortages in food safety staff hamper monitoring and enforcement.

Milk, dairy among frequently flagged foods

Milk and dairy products among food samples that continue to fail safety standards.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Nearly one in five food samples tested across India was found to be non-conforming in 2025-26, even as only 4.8% of food safety violations ended in convictions, highlighting gaps in enforcement and staffing across states, according to data analysed by Richa Gandhi.The share of non-conforming food samples has remained around 20% over the past five years, despite a steady rise in the number of samples tested. In 2025-26, authorities analysed 2,23,808 samples, of which 40,023 were found to be non-conforming.The proportion of non-conforming samples stood at 17.9% in 2025-26, down from 20.2% in 2024-25 and 19.8% in 2023-24. It had peaked at 25.1% in 2022-23.At the same time, the conviction rate has gradually increased, rising from 2% in 2021-22 to 4.8% in 2025-26. However, monetary penalties remain the more common form of action against violators.Uttar Pradesh recorded the highest proportion of non-conforming samples among the states listed, with 52% of the nearly 40,000 samples tested in 2025-26 found to be non-conforming.The state analysed 39,519 samples and found 20,021 to be non-conforming.Haryana followed with 31%, while Jharkhand recorded 28%, Rajasthan 27%, Puducherry 22% and Himachal Pradesh 20%.Tamil Nadu analysed the highest number of samples among the larger states, with nearly 45,000 tests, and also recorded the highest conviction rate among those states.Chandigarh recorded the highest conviction rate overall at 32.1%, followed by Tamil Nadu at 21.5%, Kerala at 17.7%, Haryana at 16% and Delhi at 14.7%.The data points to a sharp gap between the scale of food safety violations detected through testing and the number of cases that ultimately result in convictions.Shortages in food safety personnel are another major constraint on monitoring and enforcement.Bihar has the largest gap among the states listed, with 91 of its 105 sanctioned food safety posts vacant. Jharkhand has 74 vacancies against 77 sanctioned posts, while Chhattisgarh has 70 vacancies against 125 posts.Andhra Pradesh has 68 vacancies out of 145 sanctioned posts, followed by Uttarakhand with 65 vacancies out of 57 sanctioned posts, according to the data.Haryana has 57 vacancies against 367 sanctioned posts, while Odisha has 57 vacancies against 147. Tripura has 52 vacancies against 23 sanctioned posts, Manipur 50 against 34 and Sikkim 50 against four.The staffing gaps limit the ability of state authorities to regularly inspect establishments, collect samples and pursue violations through the enforcement process.Milk and dairy products, ghee, spices, edible oils and sweets remain among the food categories frequently flagged in regulatory actions and recent cases.In one major case, ghee supplied for the preparation of Tirupati laddus came under scrutiny after samples failed quality tests amid allegations of adulteration with vegetable oils and animal fats.Milk and milk products such as paneer and khoya have also faced increased scrutiny. The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India ordered a nationwide crackdown between September and October following cases involving alleged detergent and urea adulteration in Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra.In Punjab, 47% of milk, cheese and dairy samples reportedly failed tests over a three-year period. Cheese was identified as particularly vulnerable to adulteration involving starch and chemical additives, with 255 of 531 samples failing tests in 2024-25 alone.Spices such as turmeric and chilli powder have also been the subject of seizures over adulteration involving synthetic colours, wood dust and other unsafe fillers.Edible oils are another concern, with cheaper palm oil being used to adulterate more expensive oils such as groundnut and mustard oil.Sweets and khoya are also regularly identified as high-risk categories in FSSAI advisories during festive periods, when demand rises sharply.The figures underline the challenge facing India's food safety system: while testing has expanded and the detection of violations remains significant, limited staffing and the relatively low rate of convictions continue to constrain enforcement.

World.title: Billboard removal row: Abhishek Banerjee receives police notice over office scuffle

"A notice has been served on Abhishek Banerjee in connection with the investigation. He has been asked to appear before the investigating officer. The investigation is underway, and all aspects of the incident are being examined," the Kolkata Police officer told PTI.

The notice was delivered to Abhishek Banerjee at his residence on Saturday evening. The TMC national general secretary has been asked to appear before the Shakespeare Sarani Police Station on September 1 for questioning.

Diamond Harbour MP Abhishek Banerjee, nephew of TMC supremo and former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee, has been named as an accused in two cases. Other TMC leaders, including Rajya Sabha MP Derek O'Brien and former MLA Humayun Kabir, have also been named in the FIRs.

The incident occurred at Banerjee's Camac Street office, where private security guards, supporters and some TMC leaders allegedly clashed with police and Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) officials who had arrived to dismantle an "unauthorised" billboard.





O'Brien, who was present at the spot during the raid, dismissed reports of resistance by the private guards as "fake news", claiming they were merely deployed on duty at the building's entrance.

The billboard, which carried TMC signage and was mounted on an iron structure facing the road on the building's top floor, was dismantled by KMC personnel after police forced their way inside. It was later reinstalled by Abhishek Banerjee and other TMC leaders.

World.title: High-level review meet held over proposed 'ARISE' project for coastal projection and climate resilience in Odisha
World.content:
High-level review meet held over proposed 'ARISE' project for coastal projection and climate resilience in Odisha

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

A high-level meeting on the proposed Adaptive Resilience Investment in Coastal Systems on Economics (ARISE) Project was held on Saturday at Lok Seva Bhawan to deliberate on a comprehensive and long-term strategy for protecting Odisha's coastline, enhancing climate resilience and promoting sustainable economic development in coastal areas.Odisha Minister of Revenue & Disaster Management, Suresh Pujari, who chaired the meeting, emphasised the need for a comprehensive approach to coastal management that combines coastal protection, environmental conservation, livelihood security, biodiversity protection and economic sustainability. He stressed that the ARISE Project should contribute towards strengthening the resilience of coastal communities and ecosystems against the growing impacts of climate change.A preliminary assessment of Odisha's 573-km coastline has been undertaken jointly by the Asian Development Bank (ADB) and the Odisha State Disaster Management Authority (OSDMA). Consultations have also been held with ADB and the Departments of Water Resources, Forest, Fisheries & Animal Resources Development & Revenue & Disaster Management on key issues relating to coastal erosion, sediment management, protection of coastal villages and safeguarding the lives and livelihoods of coastal communities.Based on these consultations, ADB and OSDMA have prepared a preliminary report, which was discussed in detail during the meeting.It was informed that ADB (Asian Development Bank) has also been working with the State Governments of Kerala, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu on coastal protection initiatives. The first phase of the coastal protection project in Karnataka has already been completed. The Minister informed that after completion of the final assessment and report for Odisha, the ARISE Project would be taken up in a phased manner, with appropriate interventions to strengthen coastal protection across the State.The meeting discussed integrated measures to address coastal erosion along Odisha's coastline. Emphasis was placed on scientific & technology-driven interventions to reduce erosion, protect vulnerable coastal stretches and strengthen long-term coastal resilience.The development of Odisha's Blue Economy was also deliberated upon, with emphasis on harnessing the State's vast marine resources and economic potential in a sustainable and responsible manner. The approach would seek to generate greater livelihood and economic opportunities for coastal communities while contributing to the State's overall economic growth, a release said.The meeting also focused on promoting Climate-Resilient Coastal Tourism in view of the increasing impacts of climate change and natural hazards. Discussions centred on developing sustainable tourism models that balance economic opportunities with environmental conservation and strengthen the resilience of coastal tourism infrastructure and communities.Coastal Protection and Sediment Management were identified as key components of the proposed interventions. The meeting emphasised the need to understand the natural dynamics of Odisha's coastline and adopt scientifically informed approaches for managing sediment movement and deposition. Strengthening natural coastal defence systems and undertaking suitable protective measures at vulnerable locations were also discussed.For effective implementation of the ARISE Project, special emphasis was laid on Institutional Strengthening, Capacity Building and Advanced Technological Systems. The meeting discussed strengthening the institutional capacity of departments and agencies involved in coastal management, enhancing the technical skills of officials and personnel, and promoting knowledge and experience sharing among stakeholders.The use of modern technology, real-time data and digital platforms for effective coastal management was also emphasised. An integrated technological monitoring system for tracking coastal erosion, improving hazard forecasting, supporting data-driven decision-making and strengthening preparedness and response mechanisms was identified as an important component of the long-term strategy, a release further said.The meeting emphasised that the ARISE Project should adopt a long-term, scientific, integrated and sustainable approach to enhance climate resilience along Odisha's extensive coastline while simultaneously strengthening environmental protection, disaster resilience, coastal livelihoods and economic development.Special Relief Commissioner and Managing Director, OSDMA, Rajesh Prabhakar Patil, senior officials of OSDMA and senior officials of the Asian Development Bank attended the meeting, a release added.

World.title: 'RSS vision is to see the world as one': Sangh chief Mohan Bhagwat at New York event
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (

) chief

, addressing around 5,000 members of Indian-American organisations at Madison Square Garden in New York, spoke about unity, pluralism, individual responsibility and the obligations of the Indian diaspora, while arguing that material success alone cannot define a fulfilling life.

Bhagwat was speaking at the âUniversal Oneness Celebrationâ, organised by American Hindus for Engagement and Dialogue. He framed his address around the idea of âonenessâ, drawing parallels between the pluralism associated with the United States and what he described as Bharatâs âunity in diversityâ.

âWhen we say America, United States of America, one word is often discussed frequently. That is pluralism,â Bhagwat said.

âAnd when we say Bharat, another word, another phrase is discussed: unity in diversity.â

âFor Bharat, this unity and diversity, both are in their DNA,â he said.

Bhagwat said differences between people were a natural feature of life, but argued that these differences existed alongside an underlying sense of oneness.

âSo many styles of living. We appear different. We are different,â he said, pointing to differences in people's everyday needs and circumstances.





âBut there is innate oneness. That is why we feel for each other,â he added.

He described diversity as the âdecoration of onenessâ, presenting unity not as the absence of differences but as something that exists beneath them.

Bhagwat also linked this idea to what he described as the responsibilities of individuals, societies and nations. Nations, he said, should not be seen merely as geographical entities but as having a larger purpose.

âThese nations are not merely geographical entities. In the design of this universe, nations have to carry out a duty,â he said, quoting Swami Vivekananda's formulation that every nation has a message, a mission and a destiny.

âBe true to Americaâ: RSS chief message to diaspora

Turning to the Indian diaspora in the United States, Bhagwat said Indians living abroad had a primary responsibility towards the country where they lived and worked.

âSo we are Americans, and we should be true to America,â he said.

He described this as a duty towards one's âkarma bhumiâ â the land where a person lives and works.

âThe diaspora, Indian diaspora, they have a duty to their karma bhumi. They must fulfill that. They should be loyal to their karma bhumi,â Bhagwat said.

At the same time, he said Indians abroad could maintain a connection with Bharat as their âjanma bhumiâ, or birthplace, and could contribute to the country if they wished to do so after fulfilling their responsibilities to their adopted home.

âBut it is not obligatory,â he said.

Instead, he said, the connection with Bharat should be reflected in the values carried by the diaspora.

âYour janma bhumi expects you to live the values it has imparted on you,â Bhagwat said.

Bhagwat also questioned the idea that professional success should be measured primarily through earnings and material possessions.

âHow much we earn is not important. How much we distribute is important,â he said.

He asked whether a career could be reduced to money and material happiness, while acknowledging that material aspirations had a legitimate place in Hindu philosophy.

âYou think of career? Is career only money? Is career only material happiness?â Bhagwat asked.

He referred to the four Purusharthas, saying that Artha and Kama represented important material dimensions of life alongside spiritual pursuits.

âIt is not denied. In four Purusharthas, Artha and Kama are two important Purusharthas related to material life,â he said.

Bhagwat also referred to the traditional four stages of life â Brahmacharya, Grihastha, Vanaprastha and Sannyasa â arguing that people acquire different responsibilities as they move through life.

âSo you have to learn, you have to sustain life, and you have to give the advice, your experience to next generation,â he said.

He argued that material abundance by itself could not guarantee fulfilment.

âSo the material happiness is transient, cannot satisfy,â Bhagwat said.

âAnd if abundance of material happiness is there, it may fail also. And therefore there is no satisfaction.â

Highlights responsibility towards others

Bhagwat's broader argument centred on the idea that human intelligence carried with it a responsibility towards others.

Using the example of a hungry person watching someone eat, he said people instinctively recognise another person's suffering and cannot simply ignore it.

âA simple experiment you can do, or I can challenge you to do.

When you are taking your lunch or dinner, let a hungry man stand before you, and let him stare at your full platter with hungry eyes,â he said.

âYou can try; you will not do. Because we are human beings.â

He contrasted human beings' ability to think and plan with the instinctive behaviour of animals, but said the ability to think also brought a responsibility to use that capacity correctly.

âIf you think in the right way, you go nearer to God. If you think in the wrong way, you go nearer to the animal kingdom,â he said.

Bhagwat offers interpretation of Dharma

Bhagwat also offered a broader interpretation of âDharmaâ, saying it should not be understood simply as religion or worship.

âDharma is not religion. It is not worship. It is beyond all this,â he said.

He described Dharma as a sustaining principle that allows people and society to manage competing aspects of life and maintain balance.

âIt is the balance which sustains everything at once, simultaneously, and simultaneously everyone can progress,â Bhagwat said.

He similarly argued that progress should not require either individuals or society to be suppressed.

âIndividual, society and environment, they have to proceed together, progress together,â he said, adding that different aspects of an individual's own life â body, mind and intellect â also had to advance together.

Bhagwat concluded by returning to the idea of responsibility towards both one's place of work and birthplace.

He called on people to fulfil their duties towards their âkarma bhumiâ as well as their âjanma bhumiâ, saying such an approach could help a world struggling with multiple challenges.

âTo that destiny and fulfill our duties in our karma bhumi as well as our janma bhumi,â he said.

âIf we do that, that will be a boon for the world struggling with all these problems and stumbling at every step.â

World.title: 'Slippages reveal design flaw on Kanpur-Lucknow e-way'
World.content:
Slippages on Kanpur-Lucknow Expressway point to design issue, not construction defect; stretches will need bottom-up rebuild. (AI-generated image)

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Slippages on sections of the Kanpur-Lucknow Expressway within days of its inauguration point to a design issue, not a construction defect, a top govt official has said, adding that simple patchwork repairs will not solve the problem. "The affected stretches will have to be rebuilt bottom up. We need to ensure there is no laxity at the designing stage of projects. This is a major concern for us, especially since the expressway has been executed under Hybrid Annuity Model (HAM)," the official said.The Centre is awaiting the final report of an expert who conducted a detailed investigation into the slippages. "There was no deficiency in the thickness of the road or in the pavement layers beneath it," the official added. In HAM projects, the private developer is responsible for the operation and maintenance of the project through the entire concession period, which, typically, is 15 years.A preliminary investigation by an IIT Kharagpur professor had identified the use of weak, highly plastic soil beneath parts of the expressway as one of the main reasons for the slippages. Plastic soil loses strength when wet and can get deformed under load. The preliminary report shows poor drainage as a contributing factor.

World.title: One criminal arrested after gunfight with police in Patna; two officers injured
World.content:
An encounter took place between the police and criminals early Sunday (August 30, 2026) along the Son River near Patna. The clash occurred during a law enforcement operation targeting individuals extorting local boatmen, the police said.

While one of the criminals sustained a gunshot injury in his leg during the gunfight, one Sub-Inspector (SI) Raju Kumar Singh was also injured after a bullet hit his arm. Amit Kumar, the Station House Officer (SHO) of Bihita police station, sustained a head injury.

A total of 62 rounds were fired during the confrontation, according to Patna Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Kartikey Kumar Sharma.

“On August 30, police received information about illegal mining during which boatmen were intimidated and extorted for protection money. Following this, a special police team was formed under the direction of senior officials,” Mr. Sharma said, briefing the media.

“The police team signaled the suspected criminals to stop, who were heading by boat to collect extortion money. Seeing the police team, the criminals suddenly opened fire on the police force,” he added.

The injured criminal, identified as Aneesh Kumar, has been admitted to Patna Medical College and Hospital for treatment, the SSP said. “In the firing, a bullet hit the hand of one police officer, and the station house officer was also injured. The police retaliated in self-defence, in which the criminal Aneesh Kumar was injured.”

He added that approximately 40 rounds were fired from the criminals’ side and about 22 rounds from the police side during the encounter. Other criminals jumped into the river and fled, while their associate Piyush Kumar was arrested from the boat.

Mr. Sharma pointed out that Aneesh Kumar has a criminal history. Last year, in a similar incident, an AK-47 was recovered, which belonged to him, the officer said, adding that six other cases are registered against him. The arrested person, Piyush Kumar, also has a criminal history.

In the police operation, a large quantity of illegal weapons and cartridges were recovered, which include 3 country-made pistols, 1 rifle, 1 country-made carbine and 25 live cartridges.

“Further investigation is being conducted by the police regarding their criminal histories and other aspects related to the incident. The police team promptly confronted the criminals and carried out an effective operation. Patna Police is continuing the relentless and effective action against crime, extortion, and illegal weapons,”Mr. Sharma said.

World.title: Poonch custodial deaths: Gujjar leaders express outrage as Armed Forces Tribunal clears record of Brigadier
World.content:
Prominent Gujjar community leaders and activists have expressed anger over the decision of the Armed Forces Tribunal (AFT) to strike out from record the administrative punitive action against a senior Army officer for the custodial deaths of three civilians in Poonch district of Jammu and Kashmir in December 2023.

Strongly reacting to the tribunal's decision to remove Brigadier Padmasambhava Acharya's name from administrative files after his two-year period of "severe displeasure" censure, Gujjar community leader Shahnawaz Choudhary described the episode as a "complete betrayal of the community".

The dispute originated from an operation in response to an ambush near the Dera Ki Gali (DKG) area of Poonch District on December 21, 2023, during which four soldiers were killed, two of them being mutilated.

While conducting searches, the security forces arrested local civilians for questioning. Three of those arrested died due to injuries allegedly received during interrogation at the Company Operating Base in Mastan Dhara and a purported video of the torture was leaked on social media.

Consequent to the Court of Inquiry ordered by the Headquarters of XVI Corps, punitive administrative action was taken against Brig. Acharya, who then commanded 13 Sector, for lack of exercising proper command and control, improper handling of civilians and inability to stop the excesses committed.

"Gujjars have always maintained their patriotism in the depth of their hearts and have never felt any need to showcase it, but again and again, we are faced with injustice," said Mr. Choudhary.

Mr. Choudhary and his team provided extensive help to the Army when this unfortunate incident happened to douse the anger following an assurance that the Army will take strict action against the guilty.

The fact that the senior army officer has been censured for two years but now a tribunal order has directed that this action of the officer will not be reflected in his personal record makes a mockery of our judicial system, Choudhary said.

"In other words, this judicial process is paving the way for the promotion of the officer in future and thereby undermining accountability for those innocent lives that were lost," he said.

He asked the government to respond to the written submissions filed in the proceedings claiming that senior leadership, including the then Corps Commander of XVI Corps stationed at Nagrota, was present in the control room at DKG during the "torture" of civilians in Mastan Dhara.

"One can not escape the issue of moral and operational responsibility by taking refuge in legal technicalities," he said.

Social activist Zahid Parwaz stated, "Justice cannot be treated as a symbolic slap on the wrist that fades away with the arrival of the season of promotions."

Referring to the submissions made by the officer with respect to monitoring by high-ranking officials from the nearby control room, social activist Parwaz demanded an uncompromising investigation, warning that the shielding of command responsibility would prove to be a dangerous precedent with regard to civil-military accountability in sensitive areas.

Sharif Chouhan, former Senior Superintendent of Jammu and Kashmir Police and General Secretary of the Gujjar Desh Charitable Trust, stressed that "absolute accountability is the only moral strength of the army."

"If internal submissions establish that top operational commanders knew about systemic atrocities being committed by their men just kilometres away, then the decision of the tribunal in diluting record entries will be detrimental to the discipline of the armed forces," Mr. Chouhan added.

During the AFT hearing, the Bench dismissed the plea filed by the officer to challenge the censure "severe displeasure" imposed on July 8, 2024, stating that excessive use of force against civilians cannot be allowed and emotions have to give way to military discipline and Constitutional obligations.

The officer challenged the imposition of the censure and claimed that "senior officers including the Corps Commander of XVI Corps and General Officer Commanding (GOC) of Counter Insurgency Force 'Romeo' had been present in the control room during the operations and therefore should share the blame".

The officer further contended that there was a clear case of the Corps Commander acting as a judge in his own cause.

Dismissing these submissions, the AFT bench stated that the direction, control and supervision of ground operations rest with the sector commander and commanding officer.

The tribunal observed that the policy under the guidelines of the Armed Forces (Jammu and Kashmir) Special Powers Act (AFSPA), 1990 strictly prohibits the use of physical force and third degree methods.

Nevertheless, taking into account a policy of the Ministry of Defence dated October 30, 2023, according to which the duration of the period of "Severe Displeasure" of the Corps Commander is two years only, the tribunal instructed the authorities to delete the punishment from the administrative file of the Brigadier.

The Bench explained that the deletion of the record was done as an exception in this particular case only.

World.title: India emerges as key petrol supplier to Russia as refinery attacks disrupt fuel supplies
World.content:
India has emerged as a key supplier of gasoline (petrol) to Russia amid a surge in Russian fuel imports triggered by Ukrainian drone attacks on refineries, ship tracking data showed.

Russia's seaborne gasoline imports surged to a record around 125,000 barrels per day (kbd) in August, equivalent to a projected 470,000 tonnes for the month, as repeated attacks on its refineries disrupted domestic fuel production, according to energy analytics firm Vortexa.

Indian refiners supplied as much as 1 million barrels of gasoline in the last two months, trade sources said. The supplies essentially came from Vadinar refinery in Gujarat, operated by Nayara Energy, which is half owned by Russia's Rosneft.

Since 2022, India has pivoted towards Russia to meet the bulk of its crude oil needs — raw material for making fuels like petrol and diesel.

India's purchases of Russian crude oil hit a record high as the conflict in the Gulf squeezes supply from other sources. India imported more than 2.6 million barrels per day of Russian crude in June and July, up from a low of 1 million bpd in February and accounting for more than half of the country's crude imports.

It's likely that fuel exported to Russia may have been made from Russian crude.

Russia, one of the largest crude exporters, has to import gasoline after Ukrainian drone attacks on its energy infrastructure led to up to 70% drop in domestic production. This has triggered a fuel supply crunch that has forced Moscow to import petroleum products while continuing to impose restrictions on fuel sales across the country.

India, Turkey, and Morocco supplied gasoline to Russia in August, as Moscow grappled with a growing mismatch between domestic fuel supply and demand.

Russia in July extended its full export ban on gasoline for both producers and non-producers through the end of January 2027. Its diesel export ban was extended through September 1, 2026.

Around 55%, or about 260,000 tonnes, of Russia's imported gasoline in August arrived on sanctioned tonnage, Vortexa said.

"All India-origin gasoline cargoes Russia imported in August were carried on sanctioned fleets and involved dark ship-to-ship (STS) transfers in the Mediterranean," it said.

Overall, around 40% of Russia's August gasoline imports moved via ship-to-ship transfers, with the majority conducted in the dark, with vessels switching off their automatic identification system (AIS) signals.

While gasoline imports have surged, Russian diesel exports remain severely constrained by the export ban, refinery damage and disruptions at fuel terminals.

Vortexa said 32 attacks were carried out on Russian refineries during July and August, roughly one every other day.

Russia's seaborne diesel/gasoil exports were around 150,000 bpd in August through August 25, flat month-on-month but down 610,000 bpd from a year earlier and 81% below the five-year seasonal average, Vortexa said, adding that Russia is likely to continue importing some gasoline volumes in the near term, reflecting its historically lower gasoline-to-diesel production yields.

World.title: Switzerland rave shooting: One dead, five others wounded; police operation under way
World.content:
One person was killed and five others were wounded, some of them seriously, in a shooting at a rave party in northern Switzerland, local police said on Sunday (August 30, 2026).

“The search for the perpetrators, whose identities are currently unknown, is under way,” they said on X, adding that the motives and exact circumstances were not yet known. The incident in Aarau, north of Zurich, prompted a “large-scale” police response.

Die Fahndung nach der unbekannten Täterschaft läuft. Mögliche Motive sowie die genauen Umstände der Tat sind noch unklar.

Die Kantonspolizei Aargau ist mit einem Grossaufgebot im Einsatz und hat ihre Ermittlungen aufgenommen. — Kapo_Aargau (@Kapo_Aargau) August 30, 2026

Cantonal police ​in ‌Aargau also appealed to the ⁠public for any ‌film or pictures of the incident. Some 3,500 people attended the annual techno party between 3 p.m. on Saturday and 2 a.m. on Sunday.

Police spokesperson Vanessa Rumpold was quoted as telling the newspaper that the shooting happened at the racecourse where the event was held. “Several shots were fired within a large group of people,” she added.

Witnesses told Blick that shots were fired at about 2.30 a.m. while the rave was still going on and that many people took refuge in a nearby gymnasium. Partygoers at first thought the shots were fireworks. One told the newspaper there was a “burst of gunfire”.

A local resident in Aarau posted a video on social media showing deserted streets and what sounded like several gunshots in the background.

Media reports said an Srmy helicopter was deployed in the cantonal capital, Aargau, as well as numerous police officers, rescue workers and medical teams.

World.title: Committed to conclude trade pact talks this year with Chile: Centre
World.content:
India is committed to conclude negotiations for a comprehensive trade agreement with Chile this year as it would help further strengthen economic ties between the two countries, the Commerce Ministry said on Sunday (August 30, 2026).

Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal was there in Santiago, Chile to review the progress of the talks.

India–Chile CEPA must deliver a balanced and mutually beneficial framework that creates tangible outcomes for businesses on both sides.



Commerce Secretary Shri @RajeshAgrawal94, in his meeting with Ms. Paula Estévez Weinstein, Vice-Minister of International Economic Relations of… pic.twitter.com/tnJilDfu09 — Dept of Commerce, GoI (@DoC_GoI) August 27, 2026

The proposed comprehensive economic partnership agreement (CEPA) is expected to open new avenues for greater trade and investment, while fostering cooperation in technology, talent and resilient supply chains.

"India remains committed to concluding the CEPA negotiations within this year, with the aim of delivering a balanced and mutually beneficial framework that provides equitable and commercially meaningful outcomes for businesses on both sides," the Ministry said.

Mr. Agrawal met Paula Estevez Weinstein, Vice-Minister of International Economic Relations, Chile, on August 26 to advance negotiations on the India-Chile CEPA.

The Secretary highlighted the immense potential for enhanced economic cooperation in sectors, including healthcare, pharmaceuticals, energy, minerals, agriculture, machinery, and engineering.

"The successful conclusion of the CEPA negotiations would provide further momentum to the growing bilateral trade and economic partnership between the two countries," it said.

World.title: After years of neglect, restoration of heritage Puducherry Police Headquarters begins
World.content:
Work on the much-awaited restoration of the Police Headquarters complex, a Grade II B heritage structure, comprising the office of the Director General of Police (DGP) and the Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) has commenced in Puducherry. The work is being taken up the Public Workd Department at a cost of ₹8.73 crore.

Official sources said the architectural features and facade of the existing heritage building would be maintained. The renovation work would be carried out by strictly observing the extant regulations for conservation of heritage buildings notified by the Government of Puducherry without changing the original French architectural design.

The Indian National Trust for Art and Cultural Heritage (INTACH) is the architectural consultant while Puducherry Technological University (PTU) is the structural consultant.

According to A. Arul, co-convenor of INTACH, “The work on both buildings is being taken up simultaneously. The work includes plastering of ceiling and walls, replacement of the wooden rafters and beams on the first floor of the DGP office and the SSP office. The ground floor height of the DGP office will also be raised by one feet. The ground floor and the first floor of the two buildings and the verandah will be laid with Kota stones while pressed clay tiles and lime concrete would be used for the terrace. The roof will be restored with ‘Madras Terrace’, an architectural style popular in the city during the early 19th century.”

Heritage conservationists, drawing attention over the dilapidated condition of the structure over the last few years, had been seeking urgent measures to restore the building to its past glory.

The landmark building, constructed in the 1790s, is believed to have served as the Barracks and is said to be one of the oldest remaining military buildings dating back to the French period in the Indian subcontinent.

While the building in the centre of the complex, also built in the 1790s, serves as the office and residence of the Director-General of Police, the building in the southern side has been renovated and it houses meeting rooms and the Police Museum.

However, the building on the northern side remained unoccupied because of a serious structural distress. The iconic structure had developed huge cracks and the building remains partially hidden, thanks to the thick vegetation that has taken over the building.

“The unchecked growth of vegetation on all sides had created deep fissures and led to water seepage. The cracks, if left unchecked, would penetrate the foundation, leading to the loss of strength and stability of the structure. This is also one of the major reasons for structural distress on the roof and the wall located on the western side of the complex,” an official said.

“Over the years, the northernmost part of the complex has undergone several changes. The wooden rafters on the roof have been replaced with steel and precast concrete rafters, resulting in serious damage. The window grills and door fixtures have also undergone serious corrosion. Vegetation growth had become rampant on all sides of the building and this has become one of the major causes of deterioration of the structure,” the official added.

An expert team, which inspected the structure a few years ago, had recommended to the government to ascertain the foundation’s strength and the condition of the walls before commencing renovation. The window grills should be replaced, and the vegetation should be removed, and regular maintenance should be ensured, the team had said in its report.

Historical significance

The complex evolved in three phases. The main building was constructed between 1788 and 1790 as the warehouse of the third French East Indian Company, which ceased activities in 1793. The complex was purchased by the local government in 1821 and used as the government warehouse in Puducherry.

In 1857, the place was taken over by the military department to serve as the Barracks. Governor D’Ubraye decided to station a company of the 4th regiment of the Naval infantry at Puducherry by making suitable changes and extensions to the buildings. The building complex occupies an entire block in the administrative quarter and is said to be the oldest military building dating back to the French period, according to INTACH.

World.title: History-sheeter hacked to death in Kelambakkam
World.content:
A 26-year-old history-sheeter was murdered by a gang in Kelambakkam on Saturday (August 29, 2026) night.

A senior official of the Tambaram Police Commissionerate said the deceased man Sahul Hameed was a resident of Anna Nagar in Kelambakkam and was having more than 10 criminal cases of murder, and attempted murder, registered against him at the Kelambakkam and Thalambur police stations.

On Sunday (August 30) morning, the Kelambakkam police received information about a person being found dead in the cremation ground located behind the Matha Church in K.S.S. Nagar of Kelambakkam. The police officials, during investigation, found that Sahul Hameed was seen consuming alcohol with a few unknown persons yesterday night in the cremation ground.

The police official said a special police team has been formed and are enquiring whether Sahul Hameed, who was associated with a rowdy from the Kolathur area of ​​Mambakkam and had parted ways, was murdered due to the fallout.

World.title: Woman, two young sons run over by train near Arakkonam railway station
World.content:
A 27-year-old woman and her two young sons were hit and run over by a train near Arakkonam railway station in Ranipet district on Sunday (August 30,2026).

Police said the victims were identified as K. Valli (27), and her two sons K. Bharath (7) and K. Santhosh (3). Around 9 a.m., when the incoming Chennai Central Suburban – Tiruchanur MEMU train that was proceeding towards Tiruttani town, the woman was seen walking across the track with her children near Arakkonam railway station. All three were hit and run over by the train.

Police said an initial inquiry revealed that S. Kottaiyah (30) was married to Valli in Kancheepuram, her hometown. They were involved in making flat grinding stones for household purposes along roadsides in villages and small towns.

Police said the couple moved to Mangamapettai village near Arakkonam to make a living out of making grinding stones. Kottaiyah died a few months ago due to illness. Since then, Valli faced financial challenges in running the family.

Relatives of the couple in Kancheepuram were informed and they were on their way to Government Taluk Hospital in Arakkonam town where the bodies of deceased family were kept for post-mortem.

Police said a case has been registered and an investigation is under way. Suicide angle is also being probed.

World.title: DPM Dar concludes UK visit, heads to Istanbul: FO
World.content:
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Sunday concluded an official visit to the United Kingdom and has departed for Turkiye’s Istanbul, where he will “undertake official engagements,” the Foreign Office (FO) said.

Dar’s visit to Turkiye comes ahead of the upcoming Regional 4 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting in Istanbul.

In a post on social media platform X, FO said Dar “concluded a successful official visit to the UK”, where he met several officials including UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband, Minister of State for Pakistan Stephen Doughty, National Security Adviser Jonathan Powell, International Maritime Organisation (IMO) Secretary General Arsenio Dominguez and Commonwealth Secretary General Shirley Ayorkor Botchwey.

During the visit, Dar also interacted with British parliamentarians of Pakistani origin and the Pakistani diaspora in the UK.

Earlier this month, Turkiye’s Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan invited DPM Dar to the Regional 4 meeting, which includes Saudi Arabia and Egypt, in addition to Turkiye and Pakistan.

At the time, Dar had accepted the invitation and confirmed his participation in the meeting.

The meeting in Istanbul comes as negotiations between the United States and Iran have stalled as the nearly six-month-old war grinds on with little sign of resolution.

The last R-4 meeting was held in June in Cairo, with the countries then welcoming the signing of the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding between the US and Iran.

At the time, FO had said that the “R-4 framework reflects the participating countries’ shared commitment to consultation, cooperation, and coordinated efforts in support of regional peace and prosperity”.

The first meeting was held in Riyadh on the sidelines of a consultative ministerial meeting, while the second meeting was held in Islamabad. Both meetings were held in March.

World.title: AJK PM vows to restore internet, road links in days
World.content:
MUZAFFARABAD: Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) Prime Minister Barrister Iftikhar Gillani has assured the business community and students that his government would restore internet services at educational institutions and remove restrictions on road links with Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa within the next few days.

Speaking during his visit to the Central Press Club on Saturday, Mr Gillani said the government was also working on a policy to address the losses suffered by the business community, particularly in Mirpur, due to the internet shutdown and recent protests. “We will try to restore business activity and help recover the losses,” he said.

PM Gillani, who was accompanied by fellow legislators Chaudhry Abdul Rehman Arain and Dr Mustafa Bashir Abbasi, expressed concern over the situation in Rawalakot, saying his government would make every effort to bring it under control. He said the educational loss being suffered by children was the government’s foremost concern, as teaching activities had been disrupted in educational institutions. “I will make every effort to have internet services restored in educational institutions within the next few days,” he said.

He also assured the public that restrictions on routes connecting AJK with Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa would be removed within a day or two. “I assure you that these closures will no longer be visible anywhere in the next one or two days. There will be no restrictions or hindrances of any kind on movement,” he declared.

The prime minister said his government wanted to bring political forces and the people of the state together to move AJK forward. “If the government is genuinely interested in resolving the problems of the people, there should be nothing that creates discord within the state or sends a message of division to the outside world,” he said.

Gillani leaves for Lahore to meet Nawaz, Maryam

Mr Gillani said the election of a number of young PML-N legislators had brought a “clear change” to the political landscape and expressed confidence in his team’s ability to deliver. “Our entire team has the ability to deliver. It has delivered in the past and will deliver again, and you will all see that delivery,” he said.

Referring to development in AJK, the prime minister credited former prime minister Nawaz Sharif with doubling the region’s development budget, saying the increase had enabled people to see tangible development. He said the building of the Central Press Club was also made possible by the resources provided by the PML-N federal government.

Mr Gillani thanked Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif for establishing Danish schools in four AJK districts. He described the initiative as a manifestation of the PML-N leadership’s “affection” for the people of AJK. He also appealed to the media to help create a positive environment and play its role in countering what he described as negative effects.

“This is also the purpose of my visit to the Press Club today,” he said, adding that society needed to move beyond the pursuit of “fame and views” and join hands to build a strong, educated and developed AJK.

Earlier, Mr Gillani visited the terminal of the green electric buses provided to AJK by Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz. Senior Member Board of Revenue Sardar Mohammad Zafar and other officials briefed him on the proposed launch of the bus service, its routes and other arrangements.

The prime minister inspected the e-buses and reviewed facilities at the terminal, issuing directions to the officials concerned.

Speaking on the occasion, Mr Gillani thanked PML-N President Nawaz Sharif and CM Maryam for fulfilling their commitment to provide green buses to AJK before the elections. He said the PML-N government’s objective was to promote development, ensure public welfare and reduce people’s hardships. “I assure the people of Azad Kashmir that the PML-N government will work to reduce their problems and address their sense of deprivation. We will make every effort to improve their lives and ensure that the people feel the difference of having a PML-N government in place,” he said.

Later, Mr Gillani left for Lahore on Saturday, where his key engagement would be a courtesy call on party supremo Nawaz Sharif and CM Maryam on Sunday.

Published in Dawn, August 30th, 2026

World.title: Putin, Xi, Pezeshkian to attend Kyrgyzstan summit
World.content:
BISHKEK: Russia’s Vladimir Putin and China’s Xi Jinping are expected in Central Asia’s Kyrgyzstan on Monday for a two-day summit, also attended by Pakistan, Iran and India’s leaders, of a regional bloc seeking to be a counter-influence to the West.

Around a dozen heads of states will head to the Kyrgyz capital Bishkek to mark 25 years of the Shanghai Cooperation Group (SCO).

The group brings together Russia, China, India, Pakistan, Iran, four Central Asian countries and Moscow-allied Belarus.

It takes place four-and-a-half years into Moscow’s Ukraine invasion and six months into the war between Washington and Tehran. Iran will be represented by its president, Masoud Pezeshkian.

PM Shehbaz and Modi to join them at SCO event

Putin, Xi, Pezeshkian as well as India’s Narendra Modi and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif are due to take part in a plenary session chaired by Kyrgyz leader Sadyr Japarov.

Putin is also expected to hold separate bilateral talks with Pezeshkian and Xi, among other leaders, Kremlin spokesman Yuri Ushakov said.

Russia and Iran, among the most sanctioned states in the world, have massively deepened their military and economic ties during the Ukraine war.

US President Donald Trump has warned Moscow and Beijing against arming Iran.

Putin’s meeting with Pezeshkian comes days after the CIA’s director John Ratcliffe made a rare trip to Moscow, with US media speculating he could have discussed Ukraine and Iran with his Russian counterparts.

The SCO has historically focused on economic issues. It gained momentum in recent years under Moscow’s and Beijing’s leadership.

The SCO’s founding declaration says the group is “not an alliance directed against other states”.

Real and trade wars

The Bishkek summit takes place as some SCO members are in the midst of real wars — the Ukraine and Iran conflicts — or trade wars, with the imposition of US tariffs on Chinese and Indian goods.

Mohammad Hassan Najmi, an international relations expert, told AFP that Tehran “believes its membership and active participation in these alliances can enable it to circumvent US and European sanctions”.

But concrete benefits of the group are uncertain, he said, as “in times of crisis, these alliances have rarely allowed Iran to resolve its difficulties”.

While the bloc claims to represent some 40 per cent of the world’s population and 25pc of global GDP, it remains diverse, with some disagreements among members.

Published in Dawn, August 30th, 2026

World.title: Karachi police chief seeks report on DHA residents' scuffle, cops' alleged involvement
World.content:
The Karachi police chief has sought a report within three days on a recent scuffle between two apartment residents in Defence Housing Authority’s (DHA) Phase 6 and the alleged involvement and “misconduct” of police personnel in the matter.

His directive came on Sunday, after the CCTV footage of the incident went viral on social media.

Karachi Additional Inspector General (AIG) Azad Khan ordered a “complete and unbiased” inquiry into the incident, instructing the South deputy inspector general to submit a report within three days, an official police statement said.

He sought a “fact-based report” on the alleged misconduct of police personnel in the matter, it added.

The AIG directed that all aspects of the case should be assessed and those involved should be identified, according to the statement.

On Saturday, South DIG Asad Raza had told Dawn that he had directed the investigation officer to conduct a probe on merit and in an impartial manner.

CCTV and FIR

In the CCTV footage of the incident, a woman can be seen rushing down a flight of stairs with a dumbbell in her hand and charging at another woman before using it to hit her.

The video also showed two individuals in what appeared to be police uniforms restraining the woman being assaulted, and a man who came up the stairs shortly after and began arguing with the woman with the dumbbell.

At one point, the man and woman being assaulted manage to go inside what appeared to be their home, following which the woman with a dumbbell and another man begin banging on their door and yelling obscenities.

At the end, a man in a shalwar kameez can be seen using a weapon, provided by one of the people in uniform, to smash the CCTV camera.

But the incident’s first information report (FIR) offered a different version of events.

It was registered at Darakhshan police station at 1:40am on Aug 21 on the complaint of a woman.

The FIR seen by Dawn invoked Sections 354 (assault or criminal force to woman with intent to outrage her modesty), 504 (intentional insult with intent to provoke breach of the peace), 506 (criminal intimidation), 337A(i) (punishment of shajjah), 382 (theft after preparation made for causing death, hurt or restraint to commit theft) and 34 of the Pakistan Penal Code.

However, DIG Raza said that Section 382 pertaining to the alleged theft of gold ornaments had been removed from the FIR as the incident appeared to be a case of assault.

In the complaint, the woman described herself as a resident of the fourth floor of an apartment building, adding that a man, his sister and their mother — who resided on the third floor — came to their door and started kicking it.

The complainant alleged that the three family members hurled verbal abuses over a parking issue, and upon opening the door, began beating and threatening her.

Subsequently, local police arrived on the spot and took the brother and sister into custody on the complainant’s statement, while their mother fled, the FIR said.

In the FIR, the woman also claimed that the other side “snatched” her gold earring and two rings.

World.title: PTA tells telcos to enforce uniform SIM policy
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The telecom sector regulator has directed all three telcos to implement a uniform policy on SIM expiry and recharge amounts, after finding that two telcos were not complying with the prescribed terms and conditions.

A senior Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) official said consumers had lodged complaints against Zong and Telenor Pakistan, which has now been acquired by PTCL. The complainants had demanded that prepaid balance should remain valid for the entire active life of the SIM.

“The complaints were that these two companies demanded that consumers maintain a certain amount of balance even during the active period of the SIMs, failing which the SIMs were eventually cancelled. The other issue was that they did not carry over the balance amount after the next recharge,” the official added.

Zong and the merged company, Ufone/Telenor, did not respond to the query; however, a Jazz official said the active base of a SIM is 90 days, with 180 days as a quarantine period.

Orders companies to implement 180-day minimum balance validity policy

“After that, the recycling of the SIM is allowed — that means the ownership of the SIM can be changed,” the official added.

The official added that Jazz has a recycling policy under which any SIM that remains dormant for up to 720 days is recycled.

“But after this period, a dormant SIM is allowed to be totally recycled, and the previous owner can no longer claim any rights over the recycled SIM,” the official added.

The determination issued by the PTA directed all telcos to implement a minimum validity period of 180 days for any recharge/balance amount.

The PTA has said any expired balance will automatically be reinstated and become usable upon a subsequent recharge during the active life of the SIM, as per the Telecom Consumers Protection Regulations.

Telecom companies will not engage in any unfair commercial practices when implementing this decision, which will take effect on Oct 1.

The PTA had received multiple complaints from subscribers regarding the forfeiture of unused prepaid balances upon expiry of validity periods.

The complainants had said that such deduction and non-adjustment of the balance to subsequent recharges required intervention by the regulator.

The complaint lodged with the PTA was that the non-adjustment of the remaining balance significantly impacts the average subscriber financially, particularly low-income subscribers.

The PTA has noted that around 97 per cent of subscribers in Pakistan, Azad Jammu and Kashmir, and Gilgit-Baltistan are prepaid users.

World.title: ‘Disproportionate use of force deepened polarisation in AJK’
World.content:
LAHORE: The Human Rights Commission of Pakistan (HRCP) has attributed the recent unrest in Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) to longstanding political and socioeconomic grievances, institutional distrust and governance deficits, saying an increasingly confrontational state response, including the disproportionate use of force, further deepened polarisation and eroded public trust.

The HRCP fact-finding report, Civic Spaces under Strain in Azad Jammu and Kashmir, (a copy available with Dawn), stated that the dispute over implementation of a 2025 agreement with the Jammu Kashmir Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC), coupled with controversy over 12 seats reserved for Kashmiri refugees in Pakistan, had become central to the political confrontation.

The report said negotiations between the government and JAAC failed on May 30, after which the government proscribed the organisation on June 5 under the AJK Anti-Terrorism Act 2014 and imposed restrictions on movement and communications, including a prolonged suspension of mobile internet services. The ensuing unrest coincided with the AJK Legislative Assembly elections, which were eventually held in phases because of security concerns.

The HRCP mission, which conducted fact-finding and election observation from Aug 8 to 10 after a stakeholder consultation in Islamabad on July 31, said it received sharply conflicting accounts about the scale of violence, JAAC’s methods and the conduct of security forces. However, it found broad agreement among political and community stakeholders, including people critical of JAAC, that the underlying dispute should have been resolved through political dialogue rather than coercion.

HRCP fact-finding report calls for independent investigation into deaths, injuries during protests

The commission expressed particular concern at the allegations of lethal and excessive use of force against protesters. It said the AJK police chief had reported around 38 security personnel killed and 742 police personnel injured since June but the HRCP mission also received multiple accounts from families, alleging that protesters had been killed or seriously injured by the security forces.

The HRCP cautioned that it could not independently establish the full scale or circumstances of civilian casualties, particularly because it was unable to access Rawalakot, one of the main centres of violence. It therefore called for an independent and impartial investigation into all deaths and serious injuries since June, including whether the use of force was lawful, necessary and proportionate.

The report also raised concerns at the government’s use of anti-terrorism and preventive-detention provisions against political activists. It said at least 147 JAAC activists were initially placed on the Fourth Schedule, while a series of notifications issued between June and August reportedly brought the total number of political workers, journalists, residents and activists listed under anti-terrorism legislation to at least 157.

The HRCP urged authorities to ensure due process for everyone arrested in connection with the protests, including their production before courts, access to lawyers and information about the grounds for arrest. It called for independent review of cases against protesters, activists, journalists and political workers, with cases withdrawn where individuals had been detained or prosecuted solely for peaceful political activity or lawful assembly.

It also criticised restrictions on journalism and access to information, saying journalists had faced arrests, legal action, restrictions on access to affected areas and special security requirements while the prolonged communications shutdown severely constrained independent reporting and verification of deaths, injuries, arrests and alleged electoral irregularities.

The report noted that journalists had reported pressure from both state authorities and JAAC supporters, creating a difficult environment for independent reporting during the unrest and elections.

The communications shutdown, according to the mission, went far beyond political activity, disrupting banking, education, commerce, transport, public administration and healthcare.

On the elections, the HRCP made a distinction between political boycott and physical obstruction of voters. At polling stations it visited in Bagh, it found limited evidence of systematic physical coercion by JAAC supporters. In some areas, extremely low turnout appeared to reflect voluntary boycott, political disillusionment, fear and the wider security and communications environment rather than voters being physically prevented from casting ballots.

At the same time, the mission said the heavy deployment of security personnel, prolonged communications restrictions, boycott by major political actors, phased polling and postponement of seven constituencies raised wider questions about the credibility of the electoral process. The HRCP said the credibility of elections could not be judged solely by what happened inside polling stations but also had to take into account the broader environment in which voters, candidates, political parties, journalists and civil society exercised their rights.

The mission observed orderly voting at the polling stations it visited in Bagh. At some other stations, however, polling staff reported exceptionally low turnout and said voters had not been threatened or prevented from voting, attributing the low participation to a voluntary boycott.

The HRCP also noted particularly low participation by women, with respondents linking their reluctance to vote partly to the wider climate of insecurity. It said reports concerning violence against women and the placement of women protesters on the Fourth Schedule required independent verification but indicated that the unrest may have generated fear affecting women’s participation.

The report concluded that the 2026 electoral process took place amid unresolved political grievances, insecurity, communications restrictions and significant limitations on independent observation. It stopped short of concluding that the elections had been systematically manipulated or that voters had been systematically prevented from participating.
